facts: The compound mixed team event was added to the 2028 program by the IOC Executive Board on April 9, 2025, making it the first compound medal event at the Games.
It is the first time since archery returned to the Games in 1972 that a new bowstyle has been added.
The compound addition brings the total number of archery medal events at the 2028 Games to six.
Compound mixed team has been part of The World Games since 2017 and featured at the Chengdu 2025 edition.
Compound bows use pulleys and cables, magnifying sights and mechanical release aids, making them more accurate than recurve bows.
India's Jyothi Surekha Vennam and Ojas Pravin Deotale won compound mixed team gold together at the Hangzhou Asian Games.
Jyothi Surekha Vennam has said she hopes compound individual and team events will also be added to the Games in the future.
India's Aditi Swami was the reigning women's individual compound world champion when the event was announced in April 2025.
India has never won an archery medal at the Games, and Ojas Deotale said he hoped the first would come from compound.
This session covers the full bracket from the 1/8 round through the quarterfinals, semifinals, and bronze and gold medal matches in one evening at Carson Stadium (7:30 PM-11:15 PM).

facts: The 2028 Games schedule, published in November 2025, puts every round of the women's 100m on July 15 at the LA Memorial Coliseum, the first time the women's 100m final will be held on the first day of competition.
Sprinters usually run no more than two races in a day at a major championship, and World Athletics said it consulted its sprinters before putting all the women's 100m rounds on one day.

The July 15 morning session holds the women's and men's 100m preliminary rounds and Round 1, plus Round 1 of the women's 5000m and women's 800m and qualification for the women's shot put, men's pole vault and women's hammer throw.

Melissa Jefferson-Wooden (USA), bronze medalist at Paris 2024, won the 2025 world 100m title in Tokyo in a championship record of 10.61, the fourth-fastest time in history; Tina Clayton (JAM) took silver in 10.76 and Julien Alfred (LCA) bronze in 10.84.
Alfred ran the fastest women's 100m heat time at the 2025 World Championships (10.93), while Sha'Carri Richardson finished fifth in the final in 10.94.

Mondo Duplantis (SWE) set his 14th pole vault world record, 6.30m, at the 2025 World Championships, winning a third straight world outdoor title; he cleared 5.75m to get through qualification in Tokyo.
Camryn Rogers (CAN), the Paris 2024 hammer champion, won the 2025 world title with 80.51m; China's Zhao Jie and Zhang Jiale took silver and bronze.
In 2025 world hammer qualification, Finland's Silja Kosonen led Group A with 75.88m, and American Brooke Andersen went out without recording a mark.
Jessica Schilder (NED) won the 2025 world shot put title with 20.29m, ahead of Chase Jackson (USA, 20.21m) and Maddi Wesche (NZL, 20.06m PB); Paris 2024 champion Yemisi Ogunleye finished sixth.
Beatrice Chebet (KEN) set the women's 5000m world record of 13:58.06 in Eugene on July 5, 2025, and won the 2025 world title in 14:54.36.
Lilian Odira (KEN) won the 2025 world 800m title in a championship record of 1:54.62; Paris 2024 champion Keely Hodgkinson took bronze in 1:54.91, behind Georgia Hunter Bell (1:54.90).

Brooke Andersen (USA), the 2022 world champion, led the world in 2025 with 79.29m but did not get through qualifying at the 2025 World Championships.
Rogers's 80.51m was the longest women's hammer throw anywhere since July 2017; Poland's Anita Wlodarczyk holds the only longer marks.
Camryn Rogers is listed as the women's hammer gold medalist at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow.

facts: Mondo Duplantis (SWE), the Paris 2024 pole vault champion with a then-world record of 6.25m, raised the outdoor world record to 6.30m at the 2025 World Championships in Tokyo.
The 6.30m jump was Duplantis's 14th world record; each time, he has raised the record by the minimum one centimetre.
Duplantis's 2025 title was his third straight world outdoor crown; Sergey Bubka is the only other man to win three in a row.
Duplantis is listed with an indoor world record of 6.31m set in 2026.
At the 2025 World Championships, Emmanouil Karalis (GRE) took pole vault silver with his first clearance over 6.00m, and Kurtis Marschall (AUS) took bronze with 5.95m.
For the first time, seven men cleared 5.90m in one competition at the 2025 world pole vault final, and 5.95m was not enough to win a medal.
The mixed 4x100m relay is new to the 2028 Games program, and its Round 1 and final are both held in this session.
Cole Hocker (USA), the Paris 2024 1500m champion, won the 2025 world 5000m title, the first U.S. world champion in that event since Bernard Lagat in 2007.
Lilian Odira (KEN) won the 2025 world 800m in a championship record of 1:54.62, while Paris 2024 champion Keely Hodgkinson (GBR) took bronze in 1:54.91.
Hodgkinson went into the 2025 World Championships with the world lead of 1:54.74, set in Chorzów in August 2025.

facts: Katie Moon (USA), the Paris 2024 pole vault silver medalist, won the 2025 world title in Tokyo, with Sandi Morris (USA) second and Tina Šutej (SLO) third.
Moon has won three world outdoor pole vault titles (2022-2025).
Nina Kennedy (AUS) won the Paris 2024 women's pole vault, with Alysha Newman (CAN) taking bronze.
Pedro Pichardo (POR), the Paris 2024 triple jump silver medalist, won gold in the men's triple jump on day seven of the 2025 World Championships.
Jordán Díaz (ESP) won the Paris 2024 men's triple jump, and Andy Díaz (ITA) took bronze.
Marileidy Paulino (DOM) won the Paris 2024 women's 400m ahead of Salwa Eid Naser (BRN) and Natalia Kaczmarek (POL).
Sydney McLaughlin-Levrone skipped the 400m hurdles at the 2025 World Championships to focus on the flat 400m, which makes her a possible contender in the women's 400m at the 2028 Games.
The women's 400m final at the 2025 World Championships was won in a world-leading national record time.
This July 18 morning session also holds Round 1 of the men's 3000m steeplechase and men's 110m hurdles, which use the heats-repechage-semifinal-final format for sprint and hurdle events.

facts: Noah Lyles (USA), bronze medalist in the Paris 2024 200m, won his fourth world 200m title in 2025, matching Usain Bolt's record.
Letsile Tebogo (BOT) won the Paris 2024 200m, Botswana's first gold in the event, with Kenny Bednarek (USA) taking silver.
Hamish Kerr (NZL) won the Paris 2024 high jump ahead of Shelby McEwen (USA) and Mutaz Essa Barshim (QAT).
Beatrice Chebet (KEN) won the 2025 world 5000m in 14:54.36, ahead of Faith Kipyegon (KEN, 14:55.07) and Nadia Battocletti (ITA, 14:55.42), repeating her Paris 2024 5000m win over Kipyegon.
Chebet also won the 2025 world 10,000m in 30:37.61, and she holds the 5000m world record of 13:58.06 (Eugene, July 2025).
Shelby Houlihan (USA) finished fourth in the 2025 world 5000m final in 14:57.42.
Lilian Odira (KEN) won the 2025 world 800m in a championship record of 1:54.62, ahead of Georgia Hunter Bell (GBR, 1:54.90) and Paris 2024 champion Keely Hodgkinson (GBR, 1:54.91).
Rai Benjamin (USA) and Femke Bol (NED) are the reigning world 400m hurdles champions from 2025, with winning times of 46.52 and 51.54.
Benjamin finished second in the 400m hurdles at the 2026 World Ultimate Championship in Budapest.
Cole Hocker (USA), who beat Josh Kerr and Jakob Ingebrigtsen to win the Paris 2024 1500m, won the 2025 world 5000m title.

facts: Rai Benjamin (USA) won the Paris 2024 400m hurdles ahead of Karsten Warholm and added the 2025 world title in 46.52, beating Alison dos Santos (BRA) by 0.32 seconds despite knocking over the final hurdle.
Benjamin was briefly disqualified after the 2025 world final for dislodging the hurdle in the next lane, then reinstated as champion.
Warholm (NOR) holds the 400m hurdles world record of 45.94, set in Tokyo in 2021, and ran the 2025 world-leading 46.28 before the World Championships.
Cole Hocker (USA) won the Paris 2024 1500m ahead of Josh Kerr and Jakob Ingebrigtsen, and won the 2025 world 5000m title.
Miltiadis Tentoglou (GRE) won the Paris 2024 long jump, with Wayne Pinnock (JAM) second and Mattia Furlani (ITA) third.
Faith Kipyegon (KEN) won the 2025 world 1500m title in 3:52.15.
Melissa Jefferson-Wooden (USA) won the 2025 world 200m in a world-leading PB of 21.68, completing a 100m-200m sweep.
Gabby Thomas (USA) won the Paris 2024 200m ahead of Julien Alfred (LCA) and Brittany Brown (USA).
This July 19 evening session holds three finals: women's discus, men's long jump and men's 1500m, plus the men's 400m hurdles final.

facts: This evening session at LA Memorial Coliseum includes three medal finals: women's pole vault, men's hammer throw and women's 400m hurdles.
Paris 2024 women's pole vault medalists were Nina Kennedy (AUS) gold, Katie Moon (USA) silver and Alysha Newman (CAN) bronze.
Katie Moon won the 2025 world pole vault title in Tokyo with 4.90m, ahead of Sandi Morris (USA) at 4.85m and Tina Sutej (SLO) at 4.80m.
The Tokyo 2025 title was Moon's third straight world crown after 2022 and 2023; World Athletics reported Morris holds a 52-29 head-to-head record over Moon.
Ethan Katzberg (CAN) won the 2025 world hammer title with a championship record of 84.70m, ahead of Merlin Hummel (GER) and Bence Halasz (HUN), adding to his Paris 2024 gold.
Merlin Hummel won the men's hammer at the inaugural World Athletics Ultimate Championship in Budapest in September 2026 with 81.46m.
Sydney McLaughlin-Levrone set the 400m hurdles world record of 50.37 at Paris 2024, but switched to the flat 400m in 2025 and won the world 400m title in 47.78.
Femke Bol (NED) won the 2025 world 400m hurdles title in 51.54 ahead of Jasmine Jones (USA, 52.08) and Emma Zapletalova (SVK, 53.00), with Anna Cockrell fourth.
Bol moved to the 800m from 2026, so she is not expected to contest the 400m hurdles at the 2028 Games; she ran a Dutch 800m record of 1:55.41 in Lausanne in August 2026.
Anna Cockrell held the 2026 world lead in the women's 400m hurdles at 52.13, set in Zurich on 27 August 2026.
Men's 400m semifinal contenders include 2025 world champion Busang Collen Kebinatshipi (BOT, 43.53) and silver medalist Jereem Richards (TTO, 43.72); Paris 2024 gold went to Quincy Hall (USA).
Men's 200m semifinal contenders include Noah Lyles, who won his fourth straight world 200m title in 2025 in 19.52, and Kenny Bednarek, who won the 2026 Ultimate Championship 200m in 19.52.
Men's 110m hurdles semifinal contenders include world record holder Ja'Kobe Tharp (USA, 12.75 in June 2026) and 2025 world champion Cordell Tinch (USA, 12.99).

Paris 2024 men's 200m medalists were Letsile Tebogo (BOT) gold, Kenny Bednarek (USA) silver and Noah Lyles (USA) bronze.
Noah Lyles won the 2025 world 200m title in 19.52, his fourth straight world 200m crown, ahead of Kenny Bednarek (19.58) and Bryan Levell (JAM, 19.64).
Kenny Bednarek won both the 100m (9.85) and 200m (19.52) at the 2026 World Athletics Ultimate Championship in Budapest, beating 2025 world 100m champion Oblique Seville in the 100m.
Ja'Kobe Tharp (USA) set the 110m hurdles world record of 12.75 in the NCAA semifinals at Hayward Field on 10 June 2026, breaking Aries Merritt's 12.80 from 2012.
Tharp won the 110m hurdles at the 2026 Ultimate Championship in 12.94, beating 2025 world champion Cordell Tinch (USA) by 0.01 seconds, and also won the 2026 Diamond League final.
Cordell Tinch won the 2025 world 110m hurdles title in 12.99.
Beatrice Chebet (KEN) won the Paris 2024 5000m and 10,000m and won both again at the 2025 World Championships, taking the 10,000m in 30:37.61 ahead of Nadia Battocletti (ITA) and Gudaf Tsegay (ETH).
Paris 2024 women's 5000m medalists were Chebet, Faith Kipyegon (KEN) and Sifan Hassan (NED).

Women's 200m semifinal contenders include Paris 2024 champion Gabby Thomas and silver medalist Julien Alfred, plus Melissa Jefferson-Wooden, who won the 2025 world 200m title and the 2026 Ultimate Championship 200m in a world-leading 21.47.
The heptathlon continues with the shot put and 200m, and the men's javelin qualification also takes place in this session.

facts: This session at LA Memorial Coliseum ends the women's heptathlon (long jump, javelin, 800m) and includes medal finals in the women's long jump, women's 400m, men's 400m and women's 200m.
Paris 2024 women's long jump medalists were Tara Davis-Woodhall (USA) gold, Malaika Mihambo (GER) silver and Jasmine Moore (USA) bronze.
Tara Davis-Woodhall won her first world long jump title in Tokyo in 2025 with a world-leading 7.13m.
Paris 2024 women's 400m medalists were Marileidy Paulino (DOM), Salwa Eid Naser (BRN) and Natalia Kaczmarek (POL).
Sydney McLaughlin-Levrone won the 2025 world 400m title in a championship and North American record of 47.78, with Paulino also under 48 seconds, the first time two women broke 48 in one race.
Paulino won the women's 400m at the 2026 Ultimate Championship in Budapest, with Henriette Jaeger second in 49.28 and Nickisha Pryce third in 49.56.
Paris 2024 men's 400m medalists were Quincy Hall (USA), Matt Hudson-Smith (GBR) and Muzala Samukonga (ZAM).
Busang Collen Kebinatshipi (BOT) won the 2025 world 400m title in 43.53, ahead of Jereem Richards (TTO, 43.72) and Bayapo Ndori (BOT, 44.20), becoming Botswana's first men's world champion.
Kebinatshipi also won the 400m at the 2026 Ultimate Championship in 43.39.
Paris 2024 women's 200m medalists were Gabby Thomas (USA), Julien Alfred (LCA) and Brittany Brown (USA).
Melissa Jefferson-Wooden won the 100m, 200m and 4x100m at the 2025 World Championships and won the 2026 Ultimate Championship 200m in a world-leading 21.47.
Anna Hall (USA) is the 2025 world heptathlon champion.
Men's 800m semifinalists are expected to include Paris 2024 champion Emmanuel Wanyonyi, who won the 2025 world title in a championship record of 1:41.86.

facts: This session at LA Memorial Coliseum includes medal finals in the women's high jump, women's javelin, men's 800m, women's 1500m and men's 4x100m relay.
Paris 2024 women's high jump medalists were Yaroslava Mahuchikh (UKR) gold, Nicola Olyslagers (AUS) silver and Eleanor Patterson (AUS) bronze.
Paris 2024 men's 800m medalists were Emmanuel Wanyonyi (KEN) gold, Marco Arop (CAN) silver and Djamel Sedjati (ALG) bronze.
Wanyonyi won the 2025 world 800m title in a championship record of 1:41.86, ahead of Sedjati (1:41.90) and Arop (1:41.95).
Sedjati won the men's 800m at the 2026 Ultimate Championship in 1:41.91, passing Arop in the last 200m.
Faith Kipyegon (KEN) won her fourth world 1500m title in Tokyo in 2025 in 3:52.15, ahead of Dorcus Ewoi (KEN, 3:54.92) and Jessica Hull (AUS, 3:55.16).
Kipyegon also took silver behind Beatrice Chebet in the 2025 world 5000m.
Canada won the Paris 2024 men's 4x100m relay.
Noah Lyles won gold in the men's 4x100m relay at the 2025 World Championships as part of his two-gold, one-bronze haul.
Kenny Bednarek won the 100m at the 2026 Ultimate Championship in 9.85, ahead of 2025 world champion Oblique Seville (JAM); Kishane Thompson (JAM) took 2025 world 100m silver.
The 2027 World Championships in Beijing are the next global championship before the 2028 Games; the 2026 World Relays in Gaborone were a qualifier for Beijing.

Paris 2024 men's 5000m medalists were Jakob Ingebrigtsen (NOR) gold, Ronald Kwemoi (KEN) silver and Grant Fisher (USA) bronze.
Cole Hocker (USA), the Paris 2024 1500m champion, won the 2025 world 5000m title.
Ingebrigtsen won the 5000m at the 2026 Ultimate Championship in 12:59.24, edging Hocker (13:00.05).
The United States won the 2025 world women's 4x100m relay with a team that included Melissa Jefferson-Wooden, Twanisha Terry, Kayla White and Sha'Carri Richardson.

Botswana won the 2025 world men's 4x400m relay with Lee Eppie, Letsile Tebogo, Bayapo Ndori and Collen Kebinatshipi, and the United States took silver.
Grace Stark (USA) won bronze in the women's 100m hurdles at the 2025 World Championships.
Femke Bol, who anchored the Netherlands to Paris 2024 mixed 4x400m gold and won 2025 world 4x400m bronze, has moved to the 800m; her 2028 relay plans have not been confirmed.

facts: The men's and women's half-marathon race walk finals are both scheduled in a single morning session from 7:30 to 11:35 a.m. on Thursday, July 27, 2028.
The order of the two races within the July 27 session had not been announced when the athletics schedule was released in November 2025.
Track and field events at the 2028 Games run at the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum from July 15-24, so the race walks take place after the track program ends.
The women's marathon is scheduled for July 29 and the men's marathon for July 30, the final day of the 2028 Games.
The 2028 Games replace the 20 km walks with half-marathon (21.1 km) race walks for men and women, following World Athletics' shift to half-marathon and marathon walk distances.
The mixed marathon race walk relay, held only at Paris 2024, has been dropped from the 2028 program to make room for a mixed 4x100m relay.
Canada's Evan Dunfee publicly criticized dropping the walk relay, calling it part of the 'ongoing TikTokification' of the Games.
At Paris 2024, Ecuador's Brian Pintado won the men's 20 km walk, Brazil's Caio Bonfim took silver and Spain's Alvaro Martin took bronze.
At Paris 2024, China's Yang Jiayu won the women's 20 km walk, Spain's Maria Perez took silver and Australia's Jemima Montag took bronze.
Spain won the Paris 2024 mixed marathon race walk relay, with Ecuador second and Australia third.
Spain, Ecuador and Australia each won medals in two of the three race walk events at Paris 2024.
The race walk venue and course for the 2028 Games were listed as TBD at the time of this brief.

facts: The women's marathon at the 2028 Games is a single-race final starting at the Venice Beach Boardwalk; organizers list the marathon finish venue as still to be confirmed.

Sifan Hassan (NED) won the Paris 2024 women's marathon in a Games record of 2:22:55, ahead of Tigst Assefa (ETH, silver) and Hellen Obiri (KEN, bronze), after winning bronze in the 5,000m and 10,000m at the same Games.
Tigst Assefa won the 2025 London Marathon in 2:15:50, a women-only world record at the time, with Joyciline Jepkosgei second in 2:18:44 and Hassan falling back from the leaders around halfway.
After her 2025 London win, Assefa said she was targeting gold at the 2028 Games.
Assefa won the 2026 London Marathon in 2:15:41, lowering her own women-only world record.
Hassan and reigning world champion Peres Jepchirchir both withdrew from the 2026 London Marathon due to injury, leaving Assefa, Jepkosgei and Obiri as the headliners.
Peres Jepchirchir (KEN) won the 2025 World Championships marathon in Tokyo in 2:24:43, outsprinting Assefa (2:24:45), with Uruguay's Julia Paternain third and USA's Susanna Sullivan fourth.
Jepchirchir was also the Tokyo 2020 Games marathon champion, in a race moved to Sapporo over heat concerns.
Hassan skipped the 2025 World Championships to run the Sydney Marathon in August 2025, and by then had won the London, Chicago and Sydney majors.
Hellen Obiri, the Paris 2024 bronze medalist, is known mostly for results on slower courses like Boston and New York and ran London for the first time in 2026.

Kenya's Ruth Chepngetich, who holds the overall women's world record of 2:09:56 from the 2024 Chicago Marathon, was banned for three years in October 2025 for a hydrochlorothiazide violation; reports say she cannot race again until 2028, and it is not clear whether she could be eligible for the 2028 Games.
London Marathon organizers are considering bringing back male pacers for the elite women's race in 2027 so athletes can attack the overall world record.

Tamirat Tola (ETH) won the Paris 2024 men's marathon in a Games record of 2:06:26, ahead of Bashir Abdi (BEL, silver) and Benson Kipruto (KEN, bronze).

At the 2025 London Marathon, half-marathon world-record holder Jacob Kiplimo was the only man able to chase Sawe, in his marathon debut.
Tanzania's Alphonce Simbu won the 2025 World Championships marathon in Tokyo in 2:09:48, beating Germany's Amanal Petros in a photo finish, with Italy's Iliass Aouani third in 2:09:53.
Clayton Young was the top American at the 2025 World Championships marathon, finishing ninth in 2:10:43.
Eliud Kipchoge finished sixth at the 2025 London Marathon.

facts: The 2028 Games badminton quota is 172 places (86 men and 86 women), including 166 regular places, two host-country places and four universality places, under BWF qualification regulations approved in December 2025.
Qualification is based on a dedicated ranking list covering results from 3 May 2027 to 30 April 2028, and the list of 2 May 2028 determines the initial qualifiers.
Each doubles event at the 2028 Games is set for 16 pairs, and each singles event for 38 players before any reallocation of quota places.

BWF members voted on 25 April 2026 to adopt best-of-three games to 15 points scoring from 4 January 2027; the 2026 World Championships were the last Worlds played to 21, and the Games are expected to use the new format, though no Games-specific confirmation was found.
Viktor Axelsen, the Paris 2024 and Tokyo 2020 men's singles champion, announced his retirement at 32 in April 2026 because of persistent back problems, so the men's singles title will change hands.

Zheng Siwei and Huang Yaqiong (Paris 2024 mixed doubles gold) and Chen Qingchen (Paris 2024 women's doubles gold with Jia Yifan) retired from competitive badminton in a joint ceremony with Liu Yuchen in Hangzhou on 21 December 2025.
Lee Yang, who won men's doubles gold for Chinese Taipei at Paris 2024 with Wang Chi-Lin, retired in September 2024.

2026 world champions: Alex Lanier (FRA, men's singles), An Se-young (KOR, women's singles), Liang Weikeng/Wang Chang (CHN, men's doubles), Baek Ha-na/Lee So-hee (KOR, women's doubles) and Thom Gicquel/Delphine Delrue (FRA, mixed doubles).
2025 world champions: Shi Yuqi (CHN), Akane Yamaguchi (JPN), Kim Won-ho/Seo Seung-jae (KOR), Liu Shengshu/Tan Ning (CHN) and Chen Tang Jie/Toh Ee Wei (MAS).
An Se-young won 11 international titles in 2025, equalling Kento Momota's single-season record, and added the 2026 world title without dropping a game.

facts: This evening session covers group play in men's and women's doubles and men's and women's singles.
The 2028 Games quota is 172 players, with each singles event set for 38 players and each doubles event for 16 pairs before reallocation.
A country may qualify two singles players in an event only if both rank in the top 16 of the qualifying ranking published on 2 May 2028.
With Viktor Axelsen retired since April 2026, the men's singles event will have a new champion.
France's Alex Lanier won the 2026 men's singles world title, beating Japan's Kodai Naraoka 21-11, 21-11 as the ninth seed, the first French man to do so.
China's Shi Yuqi, the 2025 world champion, lost in the first round of the 2026 Worlds as top seed, and reports in October 2026 said injuries could end his 2026 season.
An Se-young won seven titles from nine tournaments in 2026 before winning the world title in New Delhi.
Korea's Kim Won-ho and Seo Seung-jae won the 2025 men's doubles world title and the 2025 World Tour Finals, and took bronze at the 2026 Worlds as the top-ranked pair.
Baek Ha-na and Lee So-hee became the first Korean women's doubles world champions in 31 years in 2026 and were ranked world No. 2 as of October 2026.

facts: This session covers group play in all five events: men's, women's and mixed doubles and men's and women's singles.
Qualifying for the 2028 Games runs on results from 3 May 2027 to 30 April 2028, and qualifiers are taken from the ranking of 2 May 2028.
Matches from January 2027 onward are scheduled to be best-of-three games to 15 points, after BWF members approved the change by the required two-thirds majority in April 2026.
Christo Popov (FRA) won the 2025 World Tour Finals in Hangzhou, beating Shi Yuqi 21-19, 21-9 in the final, the first French player to win the season-ending title.
Kunlavut Vitidsarn (THA), the Paris 2024 men's singles silver medalist, reached the 2025 world final and lost to Shi Yuqi 21-19, 10-21, 18-21.
Akane Yamaguchi (JPN) won the 2025 women's singles world title over Chen Yufei and was runner-up to An Se-young in 2026.
Feng Yanzhe and Huang Dongping (CHN) were 2026 mixed doubles world silver medalists, and Huang won the 2025 World Tour Finals mixed doubles title, her second after 2018.
Aaron Chia and Soh Wooi Yik (MAS), Paris 2024 men's doubles bronze medalists, won the 2025 Asia Championships and took 2026 world silver.
Liu Shengshu and Tan Ning (CHN) won the 2025 women's doubles world title over Malaysia's Pearly Tan and Thinaah Muralitharan.

facts: This afternoon session covers group play in all five events.
Each doubles event at the 2028 Games is set for 16 pairs, and each doubles event must include at least one pair from each of the five BWF continental confederations.
The 2028 Games quota includes two host-country places, which do not require a ranking on the 2 May 2028 list.
Chen Tang Jie and Toh Ee Wei won Malaysia's first mixed doubles world title in Paris in August 2025, ending a 19-year wait for a Malaysian world medal in the event.
Indonesia's Amri Syahnawi and Nita Violina Marwah won mixed doubles bronze at the 2026 World Championships.
Canada's Victor Lai won men's singles bronze at both the 2025 and 2026 World Championships; his 2025 medal was Canada's first at the Worlds in any discipline.
Chinese Taipei's Lee Jhe-huei and Yang Po-hsuan won men's doubles bronze at the 2026 Worlds.
India's Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand won women's doubles bronze at the 2026 World Championships.
Indonesia's Putri Kusuma Wardani won women's singles bronze at the 2025 Worlds, and Gregoria Mariska Tunjung won bronze for Indonesia at Paris 2024.

facts: This evening session covers group play in all five events.
BWF's approved 2028 qualification system has 172 places (86 men and 86 women), with each country limited to eight players per gender.
The Paris 2024 men's doubles champions will not return as a pair because Lee Yang retired in September 2024.
Liang Weikeng and Wang Chang, who lost the Paris 2024 men's doubles final 21-17, 18-21, 21-19 to Chinese Taipei, won the 2026 world title as third seeds.
Indonesia's Fajar Alfian and Muhammad Shohibul Fikri were second seeds at the 2026 Worlds and lost in the quarterfinals; India's Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty were fifth seeds.
Korea's Kim Won-ho, the Paris 2024 mixed doubles silver medalist with Jeong Na-eun, has since won the 2025 men's doubles world title with Seo Seung-jae.
Thom Gicquel and Delphine Delrue (FRA), 2025 world bronze medalists, won the 2026 mixed doubles world title.
Wang Zhiyi (CHN) was runner-up to An Se-young at the 2025 World Tour Finals.
Anders Antonsen (DEN) won men's singles bronze at the 2025 Worlds and was fourth seed in 2026, losing in the quarterfinals.

Each singles event at the 2028 Games is set for 38 players and each doubles event for 16 pairs before reallocation.
Korea won both the 2026 women's singles (An Se-young) and women's doubles (Baek Ha-na/Lee So-hee) world titles.
France won two 2026 world titles, men's singles (Alex Lanier) and mixed doubles (Gicquel/Delrue), its best Worlds ever.
Baek Ha-na and Lee So-hee won the World Tour Finals women's doubles title in 2024 and 2025.
Kim Won-ho and Seo Seung-jae won the 2025 World Tour Finals men's doubles title; it was Seo's second, after 2023.
Shi Yuqi was world No. 1 and reigning world champion when he lost the 2025 World Tour Finals final to Christo Popov.
Viktor Axelsen had back surgery in April 2025 and retired in April 2026, ending his hopes of competing at the 2028 Games.

facts: This session opens the mixed doubles knockout stage with the quarterfinals, alongside men's and women's singles group play.
The 2028 Games mixed doubles event is set for 16 pairs, and the group stage cuts the field to eight quarterfinalists.
Paris 2024 mixed doubles champions Zheng Siwei and Huang Yaqiong retired in December 2025, so a new champion will be crowned.
Thom Gicquel and Delphine Delrue (FRA) won the 2026 mixed doubles world title after taking bronze in 2025.
Feng Yanzhe and Huang Dongping (CHN) were the 2026 world runners-up.
Chen Tang Jie and Toh Ee Wei (MAS) won the 2025 world title, beating Jiang Zhenbang and Wei Yaxin 21-15, 21-14 in 39 minutes.
Indonesia's Amri Syahnawi and Nita Violina Marwah won 2026 world bronze.
Korea's Kim Won-ho, Paris 2024 mixed silver medalist with Jeong Na-eun, has since focused on men's doubles with Seo Seung-jae.
Knockout matches are expected to be best of three games to 15 points under BWF's 2027 rule change, though no Games-specific confirmation was found.

Each singles event at the 2028 Games is set for 38 players before reallocation, and a country can have two entries only if both are in the top 16 of the 2 May 2028 ranking.
Viktor Axelsen, two-time defending men's singles champion, retired in April 2026 because of a persistent back injury.
Alex Lanier (FRA) won the 2026 world title; Christo Popov (FRA) won the 2025 World Tour Finals.
Shi Yuqi won the 2025 world title and 2026 Asia title but lost in the first round of the 2026 Worlds, and in October 2026 was reported to be dealing with ongoing injuries.
An Se-young won 11 titles in 2025 and the 2026 world title without dropping a game.
Akane Yamaguchi won the 2025 women's singles world title and was 2026 runner-up.
Canada's Victor Lai won world bronze in 2025 and 2026, after starting 2025 ranked 99th.

facts: This session includes the mixed doubles semifinals, the women's doubles quarterfinals and the women's singles round of 16.
Paris 2024 mixed doubles gold went to China's Zheng Siwei and Huang Yaqiong, who beat Korea's Kim Won-ho and Jeong Na-eun 21-8, 21-11; Zheng and Huang retired in December 2025.

Mixed doubles semifinal contenders based on 2025-26 form include 2026 world champions Gicquel/Delrue (FRA), 2026 runners-up Feng Yanzhe/Huang Dongping (CHN) and 2025 champions Chen Tang Jie/Toh Ee Wei (MAS).
Paris 2024 women's doubles champion Chen Qingchen retired in late 2025, splitting her pair with Jia Yifan.
Baek Ha-na and Lee So-hee (KOR) won the 2026 women's doubles world title; Liu Shengshu and Tan Ning (CHN) won in 2025 and were runners-up in 2026.
Pearly Tan and Thinaah Muralitharan (MAS) were 2025 women's doubles world silver medalists.
Paris 2024 women's singles champion An Se-young beat He Bingjiao 21-13, 21-16 in the final, and Gregoria Mariska Tunjung won bronze.
An Se-young won the 2026 world title over Akane Yamaguchi and had won seven of nine tournaments that season before New Delhi.

facts: This session decides the mixed doubles gold and bronze medals and holds the women's doubles semifinals.
Paris 2024 mixed doubles: China's Zheng Siwei and Huang Yaqiong won gold over Korea's Kim Won-ho and Jeong Na-eun 21-8, 21-11, and Japan's Yuta Watanabe and Arisa Higashino took bronze.
Zheng Siwei and Huang Yaqiong, three-time world champions, retired in December 2025, so a new mixed doubles champion will be crowned.
Thom Gicquel and Delphine Delrue won France's first mixed doubles world title in 2026, beating Feng Yanzhe and Huang Dongping.
Chen Tang Jie and Toh Ee Wei became Malaysia's first mixed doubles world champions in 2025.
Huang Dongping won the 2025 World Tour Finals mixed doubles title, her second after 2018.
Paris 2024 women's doubles: China's Chen Qingchen and Jia Yifan won gold in an all-China final, and Japan took bronze; Chen retired in late 2025.
Women's doubles semifinal contenders based on recent form include 2026 world champions Baek Ha-na/Lee So-hee (KOR) and 2025 champions Liu Shengshu/Tan Ning (CHN).
Medal matches are expected to be best of three games to 15 points under BWF rules from January 2027, though no Games-specific confirmation was found.

facts: Paris 2024 women's doubles gold went to China's Chen Qingchen and Jia Yifan, silver to a second Chinese pair, and bronze to Japan.

Chen Qingchen retired from competitive badminton in October 2025 and had a formal farewell ceremony at the 2025 BWF World Tour Finals in Hangzhou, so the Paris 2024 gold-medal pair will not defend together.
At her farewell, Chen Qingchen told longtime partner Jia Yifan she would return for the 2028 Games if needed; no comeback had been announced as of October 2026.
China's Liu Shengshu and Tan Ning were ranked world No. 1 in women's doubles as of 6 October 2026.
Liu Shengshu and Tan Ning won the 2025 world title in Paris, beating Malaysia's Pearly Tan and Thinaah Muralitharan in the final, and also won the 2025 Badminton Asia Championships.
Korea's Baek Ha-na and Lee So-hee won the 2026 world women's doubles title in New Delhi, beating Liu Shengshu and Tan Ning in the final.
China's Li Yijing and Luo Xumin and India's Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand Pullela won bronze at the 2026 World Championships.
Japan had two bronze-medal pairs at the 2025 World Championships: Rin Iwanaga/Kie Nakanishi and Nami Matsuyama/Chiharu Shida.
Under the approved qualification rules, a country can enter two women's doubles pairs only if both are in the top eight of the qualifying ranking on the qualification date.
Each doubles event must include one pair from each of the five continental confederations, provided that pair is ranked inside the top 50.
The qualification period runs from 3 May 2027 to 30 April 2028, and all BWF World Tour events in that window will use the new 3x15 scoring system, which takes effect on 4 January 2027.
Badminton at the 2028 Games runs July 15-24 at USC's Galen Center in Exposition Park, which seats about 10,200.

facts: Korea's An Se-young won Paris 2024 women's singles gold by beating China's He Bingjiao 21-13, 21-16, and Indonesia's Gregoria Mariska Tunjung took bronze.
The 2028 singles format starts with group play, then a round of 16, then quarterfinals; this session is the women's singles quarterfinals.
An Se-young was ranked world No. 1 as of 6 October 2026.
An Se-young won 11 titles in 2025, tying the single-season record, and finished the year 73-4 after beating Wang Zhiyi at the World Tour Finals.
An Se-young won the 2026 world title in New Delhi, beating defending champion Akane Yamaguchi in the final; it was her second world title.
An Se-young won a second straight Asian Games women's singles gold at Aichi-Nagoya in 2026 and the 2026 Badminton Asia Championships in Ningbo.
An Se-young beat Yamaguchi to win the 2026 Denmark Open in October, her ninth title of 2026, taking her season record to 61-1 and her winning streak against Yamaguchi to 10 matches.
Japan's Akane Yamaguchi won the 2025 world title in Paris, beating Chen Yufei 21-9, 21-13, and took silver at the 2026 World Championships.
China's Wang Zhiyi won the 2025 China Open, Hong Kong Open and Malaysia Masters, was runner-up at the 2025 World Tour Finals, and took bronze at the 2026 World Championships.
Thailand's Pornpawee Chochuwong won bronze at the 2026 World Championships.
China's Chen Yufei won the 2025 Badminton Asia Championships and silver at the 2025 World Championships.
A country can enter two women's singles players only if both are ranked in the top 16 of the qualifying ranking published on 2 May 2028.

facts: This session has the men's doubles gold medal match and the men's singles semifinals.
Chinese Taipei's Lee Yang and Wang Chi-Lin won Paris 2024 men's doubles gold, beating China's Liang Weikeng and Wang Chang 21-17, 18-21, 21-19, and Malaysia took bronze.
Lee Yang retired after the September 2024 Taipei Open, so the two-time champion pair will not defend the title together.
China's Liang Weikeng and Wang Chang won the 2026 world men's doubles title in New Delhi, beating Malaysia's Aaron Chia and Soh Wooi Yik in the final.
Korea's Kim Won-ho and Seo Seung-jae won the 2025 world title in Paris, beating China's Chen Boyang and Liu Yi 21-17, 21-12.
Kim Won-ho and Seo Seung-jae won 11 titles in 2025, including the World Tour Finals, where they beat Liang Weikeng and Wang Chang for their fourth straight win over that pair.
Kim Won-ho and Seo Seung-jae were ranked world No. 1 in men's doubles as of 6 October 2026 and won bronze at the 2026 World Championships.
Aaron Chia and Soh Wooi Yik won the 2025 Badminton Asia Championships and silver at the 2026 World Championships.
Chinese Taipei's Lee Jhe-Huei and Yang Po-Hsuan won bronze at the 2026 World Championships.
In men's singles, two-time defending champion Viktor Axelsen retired in April 2026 because of chronic back problems, so a new champion will be crowned.
France's Alex Lanier won the 2026 world men's singles title, beating Japan's Kodai Naraoka 21-11, 21-11, and Canada's Victor Lai and Chinese Taipei's Chou Tien-chen took bronze.
Qualification runs from 3 May 2027 to 30 April 2028 under the new 3x15 scoring system.

facts: Denmark's Viktor Axelsen won Paris 2024 men's singles gold over Thailand's Kunlavut Vitidsarn, and Malaysia's Lee Zii Jia beat India's Lakshya Sen for bronze.
Axelsen announced his retirement in April 2026 at age 32 because of a persistent back injury, so the 2028 men's singles gold will go to a new champion.
France's Alex Lanier won the 2026 world title in New Delhi as the ninth seed, beating Japan's Kodai Naraoka 21-11, 21-11, and became the first French man to win the world singles title.
Lanier, the 2025 European champion, also became the first French men's singles champion at the 2026 Denmark Open.
China's Shi Yuqi won his first world title in 2025, coming from a game down to beat Kunlavut Vitidsarn in the final in Paris, and was named 2025 BWF Player of the Year.
Shi Yuqi won the 2026 Badminton Asia Championships but lost in the first round of the 2026 World Championships as top seed and lost to Korea's Yoo Tae Bin at the 2026 Asian Games.
In October 2026, reports said injuries could keep Shi Yuqi out for the rest of the 2026 season; he was ranked world No. 5 as of 6 October 2026.
Kunlavut Vitidsarn, the Paris 2024 silver medalist, reached world No. 1 in June 2025, took silver at the 2025 World Championships, and won Thailand's first Asian Games men's singles gold in 2026.
Canada's Victor Lai won world bronze in both 2025 and 2026, and Chinese Taipei's Chou Tien-chen won bronze in 2026.
France's Christo Popov won the 2025 World Tour Finals men's singles title.
A country can enter two men's singles players only if both are ranked in the top 16 of the qualifying ranking published on 2 May 2028.

Thailand's Pornpawee Chochuwong won bronze at the 2026 World Championships.
The 2028 women's singles gold and bronze medal matches are scheduled for the evening of Monday, July 24, the last day of badminton at the Galen Center.

facts: The 2028 Games 3x3 tournaments will feature 12 teams per gender, up from 8 at Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024, following an IOC Executive Board decision in April 2025.
Host nation USA is automatically qualified in both the men's and women's 3x3 tournaments, with 11 further places per gender available.
The 3x3 competition is scheduled for July 16-22, 2028 at Valley Complex 3, a temporary outdoor venue in the Sepulveda Basin Recreation Area in the San Fernando Valley.
Valley Complex 3 is planned to provide an octagonal viewing area for spectators, part of a Valley Zone that also hosts BMX, skateboarding and modern pentathlon.
Five berths per gender will be awarded via the FIBA 3x3 Federation Ranking based on standings as of 1 December 2027.

The first Federation Ranking of the new 24-month window had the Netherlands top of the combined table with USA, Spain and France close behind; the Netherlands led the women's ranking and Serbia led the men's.
At Paris 2024 the Netherlands beat France 18-17 in overtime for men's gold on a Worthy de Jong two-pointer, while Latvia won all seven pool games but lost to France in the semifinals.
At Paris 2024 Germany beat Spain 17-16 in the women's final for their first title, with Sonja Greinacher named MVP, and the United States took bronze.
Worthy de Jong said he considered retiring after Paris 2024 and has not committed to playing at the 2028 Games, though he expects the 2028 tournament to be the biggest yet.
Canada beat Azerbaijan 21-12 to win the 2025 FIBA 3x3 Women's Series Final in Shanghai on September 14, 2025, its third Women's Series title, with Saicha Grant-Allen named MVP.
The United States won the 2026 FIBA 3x3 World Cup women's title in Warsaw (June 1-7, 2026), its fourth World Cup crown, with Australia finishing runner-up.

facts: The 2028 Games 3x3 tournaments will feature 12 teams per gender, up from 8 at Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024, following an IOC Executive Board decision in April 2025.
Host nation USA is automatically qualified in both the men's and women's 3x3 tournaments, with 11 further places per gender available.

One of the 2028 qualifying tournaments is a Universality event of 12 teams limited to nations that did not compete in basketball at Tokyo 2020 and/or Paris 2024.
Qualifier series events are listed for Tokyo on May 4-7, 2028 and Shanghai on May 11-14, 2028, per the men's 3x3 qualification page on Wikipedia.
Five berths per gender will be awarded via the FIBA 3x3 Federation Ranking based on standings as of 1 December 2027.

Australia won both the men's and women's titles at the 2025 FIBA 3x3 Asia Cup, with Alex Wilson named women's MVP.
Canada beat Azerbaijan 21-12 to win the 2025 FIBA 3x3 Women's Series Final in Shanghai on September 14, 2025, its third Women's Series title, with Saicha Grant-Allen named MVP.
Spain won the 2024 FIBA 3x3 Europe Cup women's title after taking Paris 2024 silver, with Vega Gimeno a central figure.

facts: The 2028 Games 3x3 tournaments will feature 12 teams per gender, up from 8 at Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024, following an IOC Executive Board decision in April 2025.
The 3x3 competition is scheduled for July 16-22, 2028 at Valley Complex 3, a temporary outdoor venue in the Sepulveda Basin Recreation Area in the San Fernando Valley.

The first Federation Ranking of the new 24-month window had the Netherlands top of the combined table with USA, Spain and France close behind; the Netherlands led the women's ranking and Serbia led the men's.
The FIBA Central Board approved extending the 3x3 Federation Ranking to a 24-month window in May 2025, and the new cycle began on 1 December 2025.
The United States won the 2026 FIBA 3x3 World Cup women's title in Warsaw (June 1-7, 2026), its fourth World Cup crown, with Australia finishing runner-up.
France were listed as 2026 FIBA 3x3 Women's Series champions, their third title, tying Canada for the most Women's Series titles.
The Netherlands won the 2025 FIBA 3x3 Europe Cup women's title in Copenhagen, with Azerbaijan second, Spain third and France fourth.
The Netherlands men's 2025 World Cup roster was Bryan Alberts, Jan Driessen, Worthy de Jong and Dimeo van der Horst.
Worthy de Jong was named MVP of FIBA 3x3 World Tour Bucharest on November 9, 2025, leading Amsterdam to the stop title as top scorer with 33 points.
USA's Mitch Hahn was named MVP at FIBA 3x3 World Tour Utsunomiya 2025.
Valley Complex 3 is planned to provide an octagonal viewing area for spectators, part of a Valley Zone that also hosts BMX, skateboarding and modern pentathlon.

Basketball at the 2028 Games is played entirely at Intuit Dome in Inglewood, home of the NBA's Los Angeles Clippers.

The USA women qualify automatically as hosts and are seeking a ninth consecutive title after beating France 67-66 in the Paris 2024 final.
Kara Lawson, a former US gold medalist and Duke head coach, was named USA women's head coach through the 2028 Games in September 2025, selected by managing director Sue Bird.
The 2026 FIBA Women's World Cup was scheduled for September 4-13, 2026 in Berlin, and its winner earns a direct place at the 2028 Games; the outcome was not confirmed in this research.
The USA's 2026 World Cup roster included A'ja Wilson, Breanna Stewart and Chelsea Gray as the US sought a fifth straight World Cup title.
Australia, the Paris 2024 bronze medalists, won their first FIBA Women's Asia Cup in July 2025, beating Japan 88-79 in the Shenzhen final with Alex Fowler named MVP.
Belgium won a second straight Women's EuroBasket in 2025, rallying from 12 points down in the fourth quarter to beat Spain 67-65 in Piraeus.
France took silver at Paris 2024 and lost the final by one point after Gabby Williams' tying attempt came from just inside the arc and counted for two.

facts: BKB07 is a Saturday July 15 men's group-phase doubleheader, the day after the Opening Ceremony.
Basketball at the 2028 Games is played entirely at Intuit Dome in Inglewood, home of the NBA's Los Angeles Clippers.
The men's tournament schedule runs group phase July 13-21, quarterfinals July 24-25, semifinals July 27, bronze game July 29 and gold medal game July 30, 2028.
The USA men qualify automatically as hosts and are seeking a sixth consecutive title after beating France 98-87 in the Paris 2024 final.
Kevin Durant, the US men's all-time leading scorer and a four-time gold medalist, told ESPN in early 2026 that he plans to play for the US again in 2028.
LeBron James has indicated he will not play in 2028, and Stephen Curry has called a return unlikely as of 2026.
Germany won EuroBasket 2025 unbeaten, beating Turkiye 88-83 in the final in Riga, and Dennis Schroder was named MVP after averaging 20.3 points and 7.2 assists.
Greece, led by Giannis Antetokounmpo, finished third at EuroBasket 2025.
Seven men's places for 2028 come from the 2027 FIBA World Cup in Qatar, with qualifiers running from November 2025 to March 2027.
In NBA.com's 2027 World Cup qualifier standings after the fourth window, the USA was 7-1 and Canada 8-0 in the Americas, and Australia 8-0 in Asia-Oceania.

facts: The men's gold medal game is scheduled for Sunday, July 30, 2028, at Intuit Dome, the last day of the 2028 Games, a few hours before the Closing Ceremony.
The United States beat France 98-87 in the Paris 2024 final for its fifth straight men's title and 17th overall, and Serbia took bronze.
LeBron James has ruled out playing at the 2028 Games, saying he will be watching; he would be 43 during the tournament.
Stephen Curry said it is highly unlikely he will play at the 2028 Games; he will have just turned 40.
USA Basketball chairperson Gen. Martin Dempsey named Victor Wembanyama as the top threat to the United States for the 2028 Games.
Wembanyama scored 26 points in the Paris 2024 final and said the loss would motivate France's pursuit of gold in 2028.
Media projections expect Wembanyama and France to face a United States team that may include younger players such as Cooper Flagg and Chet Holmgren; no United States roster has been announced.
The United States qualifies automatically as host, seven places come from the FIBA Basketball World Cup 2027 in Qatar, and the remaining places come from qualifying tournaments in mid-2028.

facts: The men's and women's park qualification session is scheduled for Valley Complex 1, one of four temporary Valley Complexes in the Sepulveda Basin Recreation Area in the San Fernando Valley.
The Sepulveda Basin venue cluster will also host BMX racing, skateboarding park and street, modern pentathlon and 3x3 basketball at the 2028 Games.
The UCI qualification system for the 2028 Games gives BMX freestyle park a total quota of 24 riders, 12 men and 12 women, the same field size as Paris 2024.

Qualifying points can be earned at UCI World Championships and UCI World Cup events between 1 November 2026 and 11 June 2028, and the 2026 UCI Urban Cycling World Championships is listed as a qualification event.
The multi-sport Q-Series, set for May and June 2028, is a main qualification route for BMX freestyle park, with up to 24 riders per gender eligible to enter.
To enter the Q-Series, riders need at least 10 points in the UCI individual BMX freestyle park ranking as of 7 December 2027, and they must be at least 15 years old or turn 15 during 2028.

Anthony Jeanjean of France, the Paris 2024 bronze medalist, won the 2025 world title in Riyadh with 94.4 after falling on his first run, ahead of Marcus Christopher of the USA (94.02) and Tokyo 2020 champion Logan Martin of Australia (91.68).
Paris 2024 men's champion José Torres Gil of Argentina finished seventh at the 2025 world championships and won the Pan American BMX freestyle title in Lima, Peru in September 2025.
China swept the women's podium at the 2025 world championships, with Sun Sibei (95.86) ahead of Sun Jiaqi (93.08) and Fan Xiaotong (92.10); Japan's Miharu Ozawa was fourth with 89.38.
Six-time world champion Hannah Roberts of the USA finished 10th at the 2025 world championships, the first time in eight appearances at the event that she missed the podium.
Paris 2024 women's champion Deng Yawen of China placed fourth at the 2025 World Cup opener in Montpellier.
Japanese teenager Miharu Ozawa won the 2025 UCI BMX Freestyle Park World Cup overall title for women, ahead of Kim Lea Müller of Germany and Paris 2024 bronze medalist Natalya Diehm of Australia.
Final 2025 World Cup men's park standings: Jeanjean first, Justin Dowell of the USA second, Rimu Nakamura of Japan third, and Torres Gil fourth.

facts: The men's and women's park finals are scheduled at Valley Complex 1 in the Sepulveda Basin Recreation Area, the day after the combined qualification session.
Each gender's field at the 2028 Games is capped at 12 riders under the UCI qualification system.
At Paris 2024 José Torres Gil of Argentina won men's park gold with 94.82, ahead of Kieran Reilly of Great Britain (93.91) and Anthony Jeanjean of France (93.76).
At Paris 2024 Deng Yawen won China's first women's park title with 92.60, ahead of Perris Benegas of the USA (90.70) and Natalya Diehm of Australia (88.80).
Jeanjean is the reigning world champion after winning the 2025 title in Riyadh with 94.4, and he also won the 2025 UCI World Cup men's park overall title.
Marcus Christopher of the USA took 2025 world silver with 94.02, finishing 0.38 points behind Jeanjean, and Logan Martin of Australia took bronze with 91.68.
Kieran Reilly landed two world-first tricks, a 720 triple tailwhip and a 540 triple tailwhip to barspin, at a progression event in Manchester in April 2025.
Sun Sibei of China won the 2025 women's world title with 95.86 after back-to-back world silvers in 2023 and 2024, leading a Chinese sweep with Sun Jiaqi and Fan Xiaotong.
Hannah Roberts of the USA, who crashed out of medal contention in the Paris 2024 final, has won six world titles but placed 10th at the 2025 world championships.
Perris Benegas of the USA, the Paris 2024 silver medalist, took bronze in women's BMX park at X Games Salt Lake City 2025.
Japan's Miharu Ozawa, a teenager, won the 2025 World Cup final in Sakai and the 2025 women's World Cup overall title; Diehm finished third both in Sakai and in the overall standings.
British riders Jude Jones and Jordan Clark, who first made their names in scootering, finished first and second in men's park at the November 2025 World Cup final in Sakai.
None of the Paris 2024 medalists in either park event had publicly confirmed or ruled out competing at the 2028 Games in the sources reviewed.

facts: BMX racing at the 2028 Games will be held at the Sepulveda Basin Recreation Area in the San Fernando Valley, part of the Valley Complexes 1-4 cluster that also hosts BMX freestyle, skateboarding, modern pentathlon and 3x3 basketball.
The Sepulveda Basin is Los Angeles' second-largest urban park, and the 2028 Games are planned with no new permanent venue construction.
Under the UCI qualification system published in December 2025, the qualification period for BMX racing at the 2028 Games runs from 4 August 2026 to 29 May 2028.
Quota places for BMX racing go to national committees rather than to individual riders, and are based on the UCI BMX Racing qualification ranking as of 30 May 2028.
The UCI confirmed that gender parity holds for 2028, so the men's and women's BMX racing fields are equal in size.
No national team has named its 2028 BMX racing roster as of late 2026.
France's Arthur Pilard won the 2025 UCI BMX Racing World Championships elite men's title in Copenhagen, ahead of Australia's Izaac Kennedy and France's Eddy Clerte.
Paris 2024 gold medalist Joris Daudet, who had said he planned to retire after Paris, was still racing in 2025 and placed fourth at the Copenhagen world championships.
Pilard won the 2025 UCI BMX Racing World Cup elite men's overall title; Paris 2024 silver medalist Sylvain André was second overall and Cameron Wood was third.
Saya Sakakibara of Australia won the 2025 UCI BMX Racing World Cup elite women's overall title, her third World Cup overall crown.
Sakakibara took silver in elite women at the 2025 UCI BMX World Championships in Copenhagen.

France put four riders in the top five of the 2025 elite men's world championship final (Pilard, Clerte, Daudet, plus Mathis Ragot in fifth), which suggests strong competition just to make France's 2028 team.

facts: The men's and women's BMX racing medals will be decided at the Sepulveda Basin Recreation Area (Valley Complex 4) in the San Fernando Valley.
At Paris 2024, France swept the men's podium with Joris Daudet (gold), Sylvain André (silver) and Romain Mahieu (bronze).
At Paris 2024, Saya Sakakibara of Australia won women's gold, ahead of Manon Veenstra of the Netherlands (silver) and Zoé Claessens of Switzerland (bronze).
AusCycling says Sakakibara won every quarterfinal, semifinal and the final in Paris, making her the first Australian to win a gold medal in BMX racing.
Sakakibara won the 2025 UCI BMX Racing World Cup elite women's overall title, her third World Cup overall crown, and took world championship silver in Copenhagen in 2025.
Sakakibara released a memoir titled Just Go in October 2025.
Arthur Pilard of France won both the 2025 world title and the 2025 World Cup elite men's overall, which makes him a projected contender for 2028 based on 2025 form.
Australia's Izaac Kennedy finished second behind Pilard at the 2025 world championships in Copenhagen.
Sylvain André was second in the 2025 World Cup elite men's overall standings and also won bronze at the 2025 European championships in Valmiera.
Joris Daudet was still racing after Paris 2024 and finished fourth at the 2025 world championships; in spring 2025 he told franceinfo he had been left without a sponsor after his gold medal.
Romain Mahieu, the 2023 world champion and Paris 2024 bronze medalist, was born in February 1995 and would be 33 at the 2028 Games.
Neither Daudet nor Sakakibara had publicly confirmed plans to compete at the 2028 Games, according to the sources reviewed.
Medalists will be decided in the final, after the semifinals held the same day, with places in the final earned from the previous day's quarterfinals and last chance runs.

facts: BOX01 is the opening boxing session of the 2028 Games at Peacock Theater, featuring women's 54kg, 60kg and 65kg and men's 55kg and 65kg round-of-32 bouts plus men's +90kg round-of-16 bouts.

Peacock Theater is a 7,100-seat venue at the L.A. Live complex in downtown Los Angeles and hosts boxing preliminary stages from July 15 to July 23, with later medal-round sessions at DTLA Arena (Crypto.com Arena).

World Boxing's qualification system provides 248 quota places (124 men, 124 women) across 14 weight classes, with each nation limited to one boxer per class, and quota distribution varies by category.

Qualification runs April 1, 2027 to May 31, 2028, beginning with the 2027 World Boxing Championships in Astana, Kazakhstan (44 quotas), followed by five continental qualifiers (112 quotas) and two World Qualification Tournaments in 2028.

Chinese Taipei's Huang Hsiao-Wen, a two-time world champion and Paris 2024 bronze medalist, won the women's 54kg final at the 2025 World Boxing Championships in Liverpool over Yoseline Perez of the United States.
Yoseline Perez earned silver at 54kg in Liverpool, the only U.S. medal of the 2025 World Boxing Championships, after beating Italy's Sirine Charaabi by unanimous decision in the semifinal.

Two-time champion Kellie Harrington of Ireland retired after defending her lightweight title at Paris 2024, came out of retirement in late 2025, and said in August 2026 she will attempt to qualify for the 2028 Games.
India's Parveen Hooda won women's 60kg gold at the November 2025 World Boxing Cup Finals, beating Japan's Ayaka Taguchi by a 3-2 split decision.
Chen Nien-Chin of Chinese Taipei won women's 65kg gold at the 2025 World Boxing Cup Finals.

Bakhodir Jalolov of Uzbekistan, Paris 2024 super-heavyweight champion and two-time Games gold medalist, was reported in August 2026 to have been selected for Uzbekistan's Asian Games squad, a move linked to a possible 2028 bid for a third gold.
Uzbekistan's Khalimjon Mamasoliev won men's +90kg gold at the 2025 World Boxing Cup Finals with a 5-0 decision over India's Narender Berwal.
Uzbekistan's Samandar Olimov won men's 55kg gold at the 2025 World Boxing Cup Finals.
Hasanboy Dusmatov (flyweight) and Abdumalik Khalokov (featherweight) won Paris 2024 gold for Uzbekistan, which took five of seven men's titles in Paris.

facts: BOX02 is the evening session on opening day at Peacock Theater, continuing women's 54kg, 60kg and 65kg and men's 55kg and 65kg round-of-32 bouts and men's +90kg round-of-16 bouts.
Peacock Theater, a 7,100-seat venue at L.A. Live in downtown Los Angeles, stages all boxing preliminary rounds from July 15 to July 23, before medal rounds move to DTLA Arena.
Each boxing division at the 2028 Games is single elimination with two bronze medals per weight class, and nations may enter at most one boxer per class.
Women's 54kg was won at the 2025 World Boxing Championships in Liverpool by Chinese Taipei's Huang Hsiao-Wen, with Yoseline Perez of the United States taking silver.
India's Preeti won women's 54kg gold at the November 2025 World Boxing Cup Finals in Greater Noida.
China's Chang Yuan won Paris 2024 bantamweight gold, one of three Chinese women's titles in Paris.
Kellie Harrington, 36, said in August 2026 that qualifying for a third Games would be a big dream after earlier wins at the Irish Elite Championships and Four Nations since her comeback.
India's Parveen Hooda beat Japan's Ayaka Taguchi 3-2 in the women's 60kg final at the 2025 World Boxing Cup Finals.

Algeria's Imane Khelif, Paris 2024 welterweight champion, appealed to CAS in 2025 against World Boxing's requirement that she undergo genetic sex testing; CAS declined to suspend the rule while the case was heard.
Khelif and Lin Yu-ting had not competed in official international events since Paris 2024 as of March 2026 reports.
Jalolov holds an unbeaten professional record and fought Solomon Dacres in London on October 17, 2026, while also being linked to an amateur return for Uzbekistan.
In late 2025 Jalolov told Boxing News he would want to become a three-time champion but that his professional career was important to him.
Spain's Ayoub Ghadfa was the Paris 2024 super-heavyweight silver medalist, losing the final to Jalolov.

facts: BOX04 is the Sunday evening session at Peacock Theater, continuing women's 51kg round-of-32, women's 70kg round-of-16, men's 60kg and 70kg round-of-32, and men's 90kg round-of-16 bouts.
Boxing medal rounds move from Peacock Theater to DTLA Arena (Crypto.com Arena) after the preliminary stages end on July 23.
Qualification for the 2028 Games runs April 1, 2027 to May 31, 2028, with 248 total quota places split evenly between men and women.
Nikhat Zareen of India, a two-time world champion, won women's 51kg gold at the 2025 World Boxing Cup Finals.
Wu Yu won Paris 2024 flyweight gold for China, which led the women's events in Paris with three golds.
Arundhati Choudhary won women's 70kg gold at the 2025 World Boxing Cup Finals with a 5-0 final win over Uzbekistan's Aziza Zokirova.
Algeria's Imane Khelif won Paris 2024 welterweight gold but has been barred from World Boxing events unless she completes genetic sex testing, and she appealed that decision to CAS in 2025.
Khelif's weight class for any 2028 qualification attempt has not been confirmed in available reports.
India's Hitesh won men's 70kg gold at the 2025 World Boxing Cup Finals, beating Kazakhstan's Nurbek Mursal 3-2.
Cuba's Erislandy Alvarez (lightweight), Uzbekistan's Asadkhuja Muydinkhujaev (welterweight) and Lazizbek Mullojonov (heavyweight) were Paris 2024 champions.
Uzbekistan's Fazliddin Erkinboev won men's 75kg gold at the 2025 World Boxing Championships in Liverpool, a class not on the 2028 program.

facts: BOX05 features round-of-16 bouts in women's 60kg, men's 55kg and men's 65kg at Peacock Theater; winners advance to the quarterfinals, one win from a guaranteed bronze.
Peacock Theater, a 7,100-seat venue at L.A. Live in downtown Los Angeles, hosts boxing preliminary stages from July 15 to July 23.
Kellie Harrington won the women's lightweight title at both Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024, retired after Paris, and said in August 2026 she will try to qualify for the 2028 Games.
A medal at the 2028 Games would make Harrington only the second Irish athlete to medal at three separate Games, after rower Paul O'Donovan.
India's Parveen Hooda won women's 60kg gold at the 2025 World Boxing Cup Finals, beating Japan's Ayaka Taguchi 3-2.
Taguchi was the top seed at the 2026 Asian Boxing Championships, World Boxing's first continental championship, where she was drawn against Lin Yu-ting in the quarterfinals.
Lin Yu-ting, Paris 2024 featherweight champion, was cleared by World Boxing in March 2026 to compete in the female category after a successful appeal by Chinese Taipei's federation.
Ireland entered Zara Breslin at 60kg and the United States entered Jajaira Gonzalez at 60kg at the 2025 World Boxing Championships; Gonzalez was eliminated in Liverpool.
Uzbekistan's Samandar Olimov won men's 55kg gold at the 2025 World Boxing Cup Finals.
Hasanboy Dusmatov won Paris 2024 flyweight gold and Abdumalik Khalokov won Paris 2024 featherweight gold, both for Uzbekistan.
Each nation may enter only one boxer per weight class at the 2028 Games.

facts: BOX07 features women's 54kg round-of-16, women's 57kg round-of-32, men's 80kg round-of-16 and men's +90kg quarterfinal bouts at Peacock Theater.
Because each weight class awards two bronze medals, men's +90kg quarterfinal winners in this session are guaranteed at least a bronze.
Lin Yu-ting won Paris 2024 featherweight gold, beating Poland's Julia Szeremeta in the final, and was cleared by World Boxing in March 2026 to compete in the female category.
India's Jaismine won women's 57kg gold at the 2025 World Boxing Championships in Liverpool with a split-decision win over top seed Julia Szeremeta.
Jaismine also won 57kg gold at the 2025 World Boxing Cup Finals, beating Paris 2024 bronze medalist Wu Shih-yi of Chinese Taipei 4-1.
Huang Hsiao-Wen of Chinese Taipei won women's 54kg gold at the 2025 World Boxing Championships, with Yoseline Perez of the United States taking silver.
Ukraine's Oleksandr Khyzhniak won Paris 2024 light-heavyweight gold.
England's Oladimeji Shittu won men's 80kg gold at the 2025 World Boxing Cup Finals.
Bakhodir Jalolov, two-time Games super-heavyweight champion, was selected for Uzbekistan's Asian Games squad in 2026, which reports linked to a possible bid for a third gold.
Only Laszlo Papp, Teofilo Stevenson and Felix Savon have won three Games boxing golds.
Uzbekistan's Khalimjon Mamasoliev won men's +90kg gold at the 2025 World Boxing Cup Finals.

England's Odel Kamara took men's 70kg bronze at the 2025 World Boxing Championships after losing a semifinal in Liverpool.
Algeria's Imane Khelif won welterweight gold at Paris 2024 amid a gender-eligibility controversy.

The 2028 Games have 14 medal events split evenly by gender, up from 13 events at Paris 2024.
The 2027 World Boxing Championships will be a key qualifying event, and qualification closes in May 2028.

facts: This session includes the women's 65kg and men's 90kg finals plus the women's 57kg semifinals.
Uzbekistan's Turabek Khabibullaev won men's 90kg gold at the 2025 World Boxing Championships in Liverpool, with Brazil's Isaias Ribeiro taking silver.
Azerbaijan's Loren Alfonso and Spain's Enmanuel Reyes won 90kg bronze at the 2025 Worlds.
Uzbekistan's Lazizbek Mullojonov won the Paris 2024 heavyweight title at 92kg.
Algeria's Imane Khelif won Paris 2024 welterweight gold at 66kg; the 2028 women's 65kg class is the closest equivalent.
Chinese Taipei's Lin Yu-Ting won Paris 2024 featherweight gold at 57kg, the same weight as the 2028 women's 57kg class.
Khelif and Lin were at the center of an eligibility controversy at Paris 2024, and World Boxing now requires sex testing for women's divisions.
The 2028 Games will be the first time boxing has full gender parity, with seven classes each for women and men.

facts: BSB01 is the first baseball session of the 2028 Games and starts the six-team men's tournament at Dodger Stadium on Thursday, July 13, 2028, the day before the Opening Ceremony.
The baseball tournament pauses on July 14 for the Opening Ceremony and resumes on July 15, with the group stage running July 13-16 and the knockout rounds following through July 19.
The United States qualified automatically as host; the Dominican Republic and Venezuela earned spots by reaching the semifinals of the 2026 World Baseball Classic.
The 2026 World Baseball Classic was the first qualifying event for any sport on the 2028 Games program.

Two more spots will be decided at the 2027 WBSC Premier12 in Tokyo (November 8-21, 2027), one for the top Asian team and one for the top team from Europe or Oceania, and the last spot goes to a final qualifying tournament held no later than March 2028.
Each national team may name a 24-player squad, for a total of 144 players in the tournament.
Dodger Stadium, opened in 1962, is the oldest MLB stadium on the West Coast and also hosted baseball when it was a demonstration sport at the 1984 Los Angeles Games.
MLB owners have reportedly backed an 11-day midseason pause, combined with the 2028 All-Star break, so that major leaguers can play, but the players' union had not agreed as of July 2026.

At Tokyo 2020, the most recent Games tournament, Japan won gold, the United States took silver and the Dominican Republic won bronze by beating South Korea 10-6; players on MLB 40-man rosters were barred from that event.

facts: The bronze medal game at Dodger Stadium is the third-place game of a six-team men's tournament, and baseball's return in 2028 marks its first appearance at the Games since Tokyo 2020.
At Tokyo 2020, the Dominican Republic won bronze by beating South Korea 10-6 in the bronze medal game.
The Dominican Republic and Venezuela became the first teams to qualify for the 2028 Games in any sport by reaching the semifinals of the 2026 World Baseball Classic.
WBSC listed the Dominican Republic at No. 12 and Venezuela at No. 5 in the world rankings when the two teams qualified in March 2026.
The United States qualified automatically as host, joining the Dominican Republic and Venezuela as the first three confirmed teams in the field.

The Dominican Republic lost 2-1 to the United States in the 2026 World Baseball Classic semifinal in Miami after home runs by Gunnar Henderson and Roman Anthony in the fourth inning; the game ended on a disputed called third strike against Geraldo Perdomo.
In pool play at the 2026 World Baseball Classic, the Dominican Republic beat Venezuela, with Ketel Marte hitting a home run in that game.
Venezuela beat Italy's semifinal path to reach the 2026 Classic final, while Italy reached the semifinals of that tournament as a European side.
The remaining three places in the 2028 field will come from the 2027 WBSC Premier12 (one Asian team and one from Europe or Oceania) and a final qualifying tournament held no later than March 2028.

MLB owners reportedly support an 11-day season pause, tied to the 2028 All-Star break, so active major leaguers could play, but talks with the players' union over hotel rooms, tickets, insurance, NIL rights and a mandatory participation agreement were unresolved as of mid-2026.
Teams appearing in the bronze game will be the two semifinal losers, so the matchup cannot be known until the semifinals are played.

facts: The gold medal game is the final of the six-team men's tournament at Dodger Stadium, and baseball's return in 2028 marks its first appearance at the Games since Tokyo 2020.
At Tokyo 2020, host Japan won gold and the United States took silver.
Venezuela won the 2026 World Baseball Classic, defeating the United States 3-2 in the final on March 17, 2026, in front of a sold-out crowd of 36,190 at loanDepot Park in Miami.
It was Venezuela's first World Baseball Classic title; Wilyer Abreu and Eugenio Suarez delivered key hits in the final, and Maikel Garcia was named tournament MVP.

Bryce Harper hit a two-run home run in the eighth inning of the 2026 Classic final to tie the score before Venezuela won, and the loss was the second straight Classic final defeat for the United States after losing to Japan in 2023.
Venezuela will make its first appearance in baseball at the Games in 2028 after qualifying through the 2026 World Baseball Classic.
The United States qualified automatically as host and reached the 2026 Classic final by beating the Dominican Republic 2-1 in the semifinal, with Paul Skenes starting.
WBSC ranked Venezuela No. 5 in the world when it qualified in March 2026.

The Dominican Republic also qualified through the 2026 Classic; three further places will come from the 2027 WBSC Premier12 and a final qualifier held no later than March 2028, so 2020 champion Japan has not yet qualified.

MLB owners reportedly support pausing the season for 11 days, tied to the 2028 All-Star break, to allow active major leaguers to play, but union talks over hotels, tickets, insurance, NIL rights and a mandatory participation agreement were unresolved as of mid-2026.
A United States-Venezuela gold medal game would be a rematch of the 2026 World Baseball Classic final, though the finalists depend on the semifinal results.

facts: The 2028 Games softball tournament will be held at Devon Park (OKC Softball Park) in Oklahoma City from July 23 to 29, 2028.
Softball was moved to Oklahoma City after organizers decided not to build new temporary softball venues in Los Angeles.
Devon Park seats 13,000 spectators and is described as the largest softball-specific stadium in the world.
Devon Park hosts the NCAA Women's College World Series every year.
As host, the USA has qualified automatically; the other five teams had not been determined as of October 2026, so opening-day matchups are not yet set.

The first qualification event, the WBSC Women's Softball World Cup Finals 2027, is scheduled for April 5-10, 2027, at Kayo Stadium in Moreton Bay (Redcliffe), Queensland, Australia, with one berth to the 2028 Games available.
Japan was ranked No. 1 in the WBSC women's softball world rankings after The World Games 2025, with the USA closing the gap later in 2025.
The most recent Games softball tournament, Tokyo 2020, ended with Japan winning gold, the USA silver and Canada bronze.

Japan qualified for the eight-team WBSC Women's Softball World Cup Finals 2027 in Australia, where the best non-host finisher earns a 2028 Games berth.
Japan has not yet qualified for the 2028 Games as of October 2026; the USA is the only team confirmed.

Yukiko Ueno, Japan's veteran pitcher, was born July 22, 1982, so she would turn 46 the day before the 2028 Games softball tournament starts.
Ueno pitched for Japan at the 2004, 2008 and Tokyo 2020 Games, winning gold in 2008 and 2020 and bronze in 2004.
Ueno was on Japan's roster for The World Games 2025 and was named to the squad for the 2026 World Cup Group Lima.
Ueno has said she still finds playing softball the most fun, as Japan works toward the 2028 Games.
Ueno has not publicly confirmed she will play at the 2028 Games as of October 2026.

Oklahoma City approved a $25.4 million indoor softball facility at Devon Park, scheduled for completion in late 2027, before the 2028 Games tournament.
Oklahoma City-based STUDIO Architecture designed the two-story indoor facility, which sits west of Devon Park.
Oklahoma City also hosts canoe slalom for the 2028 Games, at Riversport OKC.
The USA Women's National Team is based in Oklahoma City, where USA Softball has its headquarters.
Through 2025, the USA U-18 Women's National Team had won five straight world titles, including a 7-2 win over Japan in the 2025 final in Oklahoma City.

facts: The 2028 Games softball tournament will be played at Devon Park in Oklahoma City, after organizers decided not to build temporary softball venues in Los Angeles.

Six women's teams play a single round-robin preliminary round, so each team plays five games before the medal games.

Japan held the No. 1 spot in the WBSC Women's Softball World Ranking after The World Games 2025.
The USA won women's softball gold at The World Games 2025 in Chengdu, China.
At the 2025 Asia Cup in Xi'an, China, Chinese Taipei and Japan earned the three Asian places at the 2026/2027 Women's Softball World Cup.
The Netherlands moved into the top five of the WBSC Women's Softball World Ranking for the first time ever in 2024.

facts: The organizing committee announced on May 8, 2025 that the 2028 Opening Ceremony will be held across two stadiums at the same time, the LA Memorial Coliseum in Exposition Park and SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, which no previous edition of the modern Games has done.
The official schedule lists the Opening Ceremony on Day 0, Friday, July 14, 2028, at 5:00 p.m. PT (8:00 p.m. ET).

SoFi Stadium will be called the 2028 Stadium (also referred to as the Stadium in Inglewood) during the Games; it opened in September 2020 and is home to the NFL's Los Angeles Rams and Los Angeles Chargers.
SoFi Stadium will also host swimming during the 2028 Games, and the Games will be its first.
The LA Memorial Coliseum opened in 1923 and hosted the Opening Ceremonies of the 1932 and 1984 Summer Games, which makes 2028 its third Games.
In a Los Angeles City Council vote in November 2025 that moved the Closing Ceremony entirely to the Coliseum, the two-stadium plan for the Opening Ceremony was kept unchanged.

On October 28, 2026, organizers named film producer Kathleen Kennedy, former president of Lucasfilm, as Head of Ceremonies and Content; she will serve as an Executive Producer of the Opening and Closing Ceremonies.
Kennedy took over the role from Peter Rice, who stays on as an Executive Producer of the ceremonies after being named Netflix's Chief Content Officer in October 2026.
The ceremonies team also includes Ben Winston as Executive Producer and Creative Director, and longtime Games ceremonies producer Scott Givens as Executive Producer of Production.
Kennedy said that she and her husband, producer Frank Marshall, have attended almost every Games since Los Angeles 1984.
Official hospitality packages list the Opening Ceremony as session CER01A at 17:00 PT on Friday, July 14, 2028.
Reports from the 2025-2026 ticket sales said top Opening Ceremony seats went for more than $5,000 each, and ticket prices drew public complaints about cost.
According to the schedule, the first medals of the 2028 Games will be awarded in the women's triathlon after the Opening Ceremony.

facts: The official schedule lists the Closing Ceremony on Day 16, Sunday, July 30, 2028, at 6:00 p.m. PT (9:00 p.m. ET).

The Closing Ceremony was first planned to be split between the LA Memorial Coliseum and SoFi Stadium, but in November 2025 the Los Angeles City Council voted unanimously to hold it entirely at the Coliseum in Exposition Park.
Los Angeles Councilmember Marqueece Harris-Dawson said the change was meant to confirm the Coliseum as one of the only buildings in the world to host three Games opening or closing ceremonies.
The LA Memorial Coliseum opened in 1923, was built to attract the Games, and hosted the Opening Ceremonies of the 1932 and 1984 Summer Games.
The Coliseum will host both competition and ceremonies in 2028 and is expected to become the first venue to host events at three Summer Games.

On October 28, 2026, organizers named producer Kathleen Kennedy, former president of Lucasfilm, as Head of Ceremonies and Content, with responsibility for shaping the Games' farewell at the Closing Ceremony.

Peter Rice, Kennedy's predecessor and now Netflix's Chief Content Officer, stays on as an Executive Producer; Ben Winston is Executive Producer and Creative Director, and Scott Givens is Executive Producer of Production.
The Paralympic Closing Ceremony will also be held at the Coliseum, on August 27, 2028, after a Paralympic Opening Ceremony at the 2028 Stadium in Inglewood on August 15, 2028.

At the Paris 2024 Closing Ceremony, Los Angeles received the flag in a handover segment that included Tom Cruise and a pre-recorded Los Angeles program with Billie Eilish, Snoop Dogg and the Red Hot Chili Peppers.

facts: CKT01 is a women's group-stage first round session at the Fairgrounds Cricket Stadium in Pomona, scheduled for Wed July 12, 2028, 9:00 AM-12:30 PM PT.
CKT01 is the opening women's group-stage session and the first cricket session of the 2028 Games.
Cricket at the 2028 Games will be played in T20 format, with separate six-team women's and men's tournaments that each award gold, silver and bronze medals.
Each team can name a 15-player squad, with 90 athlete quota places set aside for each gender.
The 2028 cricket competition is scheduled for July 12 to 29, with medal matches on July 20 and July 29, and no cricket on July 14 or July 21.
Most cricket matchdays at the 2028 Games are double-headers, with morning and evening starts in Los Angeles local time.
All matches will be played at the Fairgrounds Cricket Stadium, a temporary, purpose-built venue at the Fairgrounds (Fairplex) in Pomona, about 50 km from Los Angeles.
The Pomona Fairgrounds is a site of nearly 500 acres that has hosted the Los Angeles County Fair since 1922.
Construction of the Pomona cricket stadium began with a ground-breaking ceremony in spring 2026, which ICC chair Jay Shah called a major milestone.
India's women secured Asia's automatic qualification place for the 2028 Games even though they went out in the group stage of the 2026 Women's T20 World Cup.
Under the ICC qualification system, Africa, Asia, Europe and Oceania each have one automatic place in the six-team women's tournament.
As of October 2026, the US women's team was ranked 19th in T20Is and had to meet the ICC's host ranking requirement by December 31, 2026, to get direct entry as hosts.

In October 2026 the ICC said that if the US women miss the ranking requirement, their place will be reallocated based on standings from the inaugural Women's Champions Trophy in February 2027 (cut-off March 1, 2027).
The US men's team, ranked 13th in T20Is as of October 2026, has secured direct entry to the 2028 Games as hosts.
Cricket's only previous Games appearance was at Paris 1900, so 2028 marks its return after 128 years.
