facts: This men's group stage second round session on Tuesday 25 July 2028 is in the morning (9am) slot at the Fairgrounds Cricket Stadium. The matchups depend on qualification, which is still being decided.

All cricket matches at the 2028 Games will be played at a temporary, purpose-built stadium at the Fairgrounds (Fairplex) in Pomona, about 50 km from Los Angeles, which has hosted the LA County Fair since 1922.
Construction of the Pomona cricket stadium began with a ground-breaking ceremony in April 2026, which ICC chair Jay Shah called a major milestone.
The men's tournament features six teams in T20 format, with 180 players in total across the men's and women's events.
The United States men's team secured its host place by ranking inside the top 15 of the ICC Men's T20I Team Rankings during the qualification window, having been ranked 13th as of 26 July 2026.

The highest-ranked eligible men's teams from Africa, Asia, Europe and Oceania in the ICC T20I rankings on 31 December 2026 qualify directly, provided they are in the top 15; the sixth place goes through an eight-team ICC qualifier.
In a May 2026 ICC rankings update, India led the men's T20I table on 275 points, ahead of England (262), Australia (258), New Zealand (247), South Africa (244), Pakistan (240) and West Indies (233).

Based on those May 2026 rankings, India (Asia), England competing as Great Britain (Europe), Australia (Oceania) and South Africa (Africa) are projected to hold the continental direct places, pending the 31 December 2026 cutoff.

India won the 2026 Men's T20 World Cup, beating New Zealand by 96 runs in the final in Ahmedabad on 8 March 2026 to become the first team to defend the title and the first to win three T20 World Cups.
Most match days in the cricket schedule are double-headers, with reported start times of 9am and 6:30pm local time.
After the 2026 T20 World Cup, Shreyas Iyer replaced Suryakumar Yadav as India's T20I captain for the tour to the UK against Ireland and England.

Suryakumar Yadav said after the 2026 T20 World Cup final that the next goal was a gold medal at the 2028 Games; in August 2026 he said he was shocked by his T20I omission and was preparing for a comeback.
Pakistan's Sahibzada Farhan set records during the 2026 Men's T20 World Cup, according to the ICC.

facts: This men's group stage second round session on Wednesday 26 July 2028 is in the morning (9am) slot at the Fairgrounds Cricket Stadium. The matchups depend on qualification, which is still being decided.

All cricket matches at the 2028 Games will be played at a temporary, purpose-built stadium at the Fairgrounds (Fairplex) in Pomona, about 50 km from Los Angeles, which has hosted the LA County Fair since 1922.
Construction of the Pomona cricket stadium began with a ground-breaking ceremony in April 2026, which ICC chair Jay Shah called a major milestone.
The men's tournament features six teams in T20 format, with 180 players in total across the men's and women's events.
The United States men's team secured its host place by ranking inside the top 15 of the ICC Men's T20I Team Rankings during the qualification window, having been ranked 13th as of 26 July 2026.

The highest-ranked eligible men's teams from Africa, Asia, Europe and Oceania in the ICC T20I rankings on 31 December 2026 qualify directly, provided they are in the top 15; the sixth place goes through an eight-team ICC qualifier.
In a May 2026 ICC rankings update, India led the men's T20I table on 275 points, ahead of England (262), Australia (258), New Zealand (247), South Africa (244), Pakistan (240) and West Indies (233).

Based on those May 2026 rankings, India (Asia), England competing as Great Britain (Europe), Australia (Oceania) and South Africa (Africa) are projected to hold the continental direct places, pending the 31 December 2026 cutoff.

India won the 2026 Men's T20 World Cup, beating New Zealand by 96 runs in the final in Ahmedabad on 8 March 2026 to become the first team to defend the title and the first to win three T20 World Cups.
Most match days in the cricket schedule are double-headers, with reported start times of 9am and 6:30pm local time.
After the 2026 T20 World Cup, Shreyas Iyer replaced Suryakumar Yadav as India's T20I captain for the tour to the UK against Ireland and England.

Suryakumar Yadav said after the 2026 T20 World Cup final that the next goal was a gold medal at the 2028 Games; in August 2026 he said he was shocked by his T20I omission and was preparing for a comeback.
Pakistan's Sahibzada Farhan set records during the 2026 Men's T20 World Cup, according to the ICC.

facts: The men's bronze medal match is scheduled for Friday 28 July 2028 at the Fairgrounds Cricket Stadium in Pomona. The finalists and bronze contenders are not yet known.

All cricket matches at the 2028 Games will be played at a temporary, purpose-built stadium at the Fairgrounds (Fairplex) in Pomona, about 50 km from Los Angeles, which has hosted the LA County Fair since 1922.
The United States men's team secured its host place by ranking inside the top 15 of the ICC Men's T20I Team Rankings during the qualification window, having been ranked 13th as of 26 July 2026.

The highest-ranked eligible men's teams from Africa, Asia, Europe and Oceania in the ICC T20I rankings on 31 December 2026 qualify directly, provided they are in the top 15; the sixth place goes through an eight-team ICC qualifier.
In a May 2026 ICC rankings update, India led the men's T20I table on 275 points, ahead of England (262), Australia (258), New Zealand (247), South Africa (244), Pakistan (240) and West Indies (233).

Based on those May 2026 rankings, India (Asia), England competing as Great Britain (Europe), Australia (Oceania) and South Africa (Africa) are projected to hold the continental direct places, pending the 31 December 2026 cutoff.
Cricket's reported schedule runs from 12 to 29 July 2028, and medal matches use the same 9am and 6:30pm local start slots as other match days.
New Zealand reached the 2026 Men's T20 World Cup final and lost to India by 96 runs, while the May 2026 rankings placed them fourth on 247 points.

In the May 2026 rankings, Pakistan were sixth (240) and West Indies seventh (233); West Indies can only reach the 2028 Games through the qualifier route, which includes a Caribbean regional qualifier winner.
The United States men were ranked 18th before the 2026 T20 World Cup and had climbed to 13th by July 2026, which secured their host place.

facts: The 2028 Games program includes six climbing medal events, men's and women's Boulder, Lead and Speed, with a total quota of 76 athletes (38 men and 38 women).
The 2028 Games are the first time Boulder has its own standalone medal event, separate from Lead and Speed.
Japan's Sorato Anraku won men's Boulder gold at the 2025 World Championships in Seoul, his first world championship title.
Anraku came into Seoul having won the previous three Boulder World Cup season titles, and he took silver in the Boulder and Lead combined at Paris 2024.
Toby Roberts of Great Britain won the Paris 2024 men's Boulder and Lead combined gold, with Anraku second and Austria's Jakob Schubert third.
Under the approved qualification system, 2027 qualification events run by or with World Climbing award about half of the 2028 places, one spot at each event.
The rest of the places will be allocated through the Qualifier Series in 2028, which reserves a minimum number of spots for Boulder.
The 2025 World Championships in Seoul (Sept 21-28, 2025) had separate medals for Boulder, Lead and Speed, the same format the 2028 Games will use.

facts: The Speed medal session runs head-to-head knockout races from the quarterfinals through the semifinals and the final.
At Paris 2024, Veddriq Leonardo (INA) beat Wu Peng (CHN) 4.75 to 4.77 for men's gold, and Sam Watson (USA) set a world record on his way to bronze.
At Paris 2024, Aleksandra Mirosław (POL) won women's gold ahead of Deng Lijuan (CHN) and Aleksandra Kałucka (POL), after breaking her own world record twice in qualifying.
Mirosław won the 2025 world title in Seoul by beating Deng Lijuan in a rematch of the Paris 2024 final, setting a world record of 6.03 seconds.
The Seoul title was Mirosław's third world Speed title and her first since 2019.
China's Long Jianguo won men's Speed gold at the 2025 World Championships in 4.80 seconds, beating Germany's Leander Carmanns, with Zach Hammer of the USA taking bronze.
Long ran under five seconds in four straight races on the Seoul finals night.
Carmanns' 2025 silver was Germany's first sport climbing medal at a world championships.
Long also won Speed gold in the Single 4 format and the Speed relay at the 2025 World Games in Chengdu, plus bronze in the individual Speed event.
World-record holder Sam Watson slipped in the 2025 world quarterfinal and was eliminated, and defending world champion Matteo Zurloni also missed the podium.

facts: Women's Lead has its own medal event for the first time at the 2028 Games, with a semifinal followed by a final.
Janja Garnbret (SLO) won women's Lead gold at the 2025 World Championships in Seoul, which Olympics.com reported as her ninth world title.
At Paris 2024, Garnbret won the women's Boulder and Lead combined ahead of Brooke Raboutou (USA) and Jessica Pilz (AUT).
The 2027 World Climbing Championship for Lead in Brno, Czech Republic (August 2027) is a qualification event for the 2028 Games.
2027 qualification events award about half of the 2028 places, one spot at each event, and the 2028 Qualifier Series awards the rest.
The total climbing quota for the 2028 Games is 38 women and 38 men.

facts: The 2028 Games road cycling time trials are scheduled for July 19, 2028, with men's and women's individual events.
Organizers confirmed on June 9, 2026 that the time trial courses will start at the Los Angeles Zoo in Griffith Park and finish at Griffith Observatory, both in the Griffith Park Zone.
The organizing committee describes the time trial as a challenging 35km course, with full course routes to be unveiled before the end of 2026.
The road races follow on July 22 (women, 150km) and July 23 (men, 250km), starting at Venice Beach Boardwalk and also finishing at Griffith Observatory.

The Griffith Observatory finish means the time trial course is expected to include a climb into the hills of Griffith Park, though exact gradients have not been published as of the June 2026 announcement.
The Los Angeles Zoo will also serve as the start and finish for para cycling road events on August 22-26, 2028.
Cycling Road at the 2028 Games will feature an equal number of men's and women's participants and events.
Remco Evenepoel of Belgium won the men's time trial at Paris 2024 ahead of Filippo Ganna of Italy and Wout Van Aert of Belgium.
Evenepoel won the men's individual time trial at the 2025 UCI Road World Championships in Kigali, Rwanda, finishing ahead of Tadej Pogacar for his third straight world time trial title.
Grace Brown of Australia won the women's time trial at Paris 2024 in 39:38.24, ahead of Anna Henderson of Great Britain and Chloe Dygert of the USA.
Brown retired at the end of the 2024 season, so the women's event at the 2028 Games will crown a new champion.
Neither Evenepoel nor Ganna has been confirmed as a 2028 Games time trial entrant as of the latest available reports.

facts: The 2028 Games women's road race is scheduled for July 22, 2028, the eighth day of the Games, and starts at the Venice Beach Boardwalk.
Organizers announced on June 9, 2026 that both road races will finish at Griffith Observatory in the Griffith Park Zone.
The 2028 women's road race course is listed by organizers at 150 km, compared with 250 km for the men.
The final climb to Griffith Observatory is reported at about 3.9 km long with roughly 190 m of elevation gain, an average gradient of 4.9 percent, and steepest sections averaging about 6.7 percent.

Organizers say the route runs from the Pacific coastline through urban areas into the hills overlooking Los Angeles; the full turn-by-turn route had not been published as of the June 2026 announcement.
The Venice Beach Boardwalk, LA Zoo and Griffith Observatory will all be used as competition venues at a Games for the first time in 2028.
At Paris 2024, Kristen Faulkner (USA) won gold, Marianne Vos (NED) took silver and Lotte Kopecky (BEL) took bronze in the women's road race.
Faulkner's Paris 2024 win was the first US medal of any color in the road race since the 1984 Los Angeles Games; she has not publicly confirmed 2028 participation per available sources.
Canada's Magdeleine Vallieres Mill won the 2025 UCI Road World Championships women's road race in Kigali, finishing 23 seconds clear after attacking on the final lap's cobbled climb.
At the 2025 Worlds, New Zealand's Niamh Fisher-Black took silver and Spain's Mavi Garcia took bronze, with Switzerland's Elise Chabbey fourth and Demi Vollering (NED) seventh.
Vallieres Mill was ranked 131st in the world before winning the 2025 world title.
Switzerland's Marlen Reusser won the 2025 world time trial title ahead of Anna van der Breggen and Demi Vollering, form indicators for riders who could contend on a hilly 2028 finish.
The 2028 Tour de France has been moved earlier, to June 24 to July 16, 2028, to avoid a conflict with the Games.

facts: The 2028 Games men's road race is scheduled for July 23, 2028, the ninth day of the Games, and starts at the Venice Beach Boardwalk.
Organizers list the 2028 men's road race course at 250 km, finishing at Griffith Observatory in the Griffith Park Zone.
The final climb to Griffith Observatory is reported at about 3.9 km with roughly 190 m of elevation gain, averaging 4.9 percent with steepest sections around 6.7 percent.
The full men's road race route had not been published as of the June 2026 announcement; organizers said complete course details would come later.
At Paris 2024, Remco Evenepoel (BEL) won gold, Valentin Madouas (FRA) took silver and Christophe Laporte (FRA) took bronze in the men's road race.
Evenepoel won both the road race and time trial at Paris 2024, so he goes into 2028 as the reigning champion in both events.
Tadej Pogacar (SLO) won the 2025 UCI Road World Championships men's road race in Kigali, his second straight world title, after riding the final 66 km alone.
At the 2025 Worlds, Evenepoel took silver and Ireland's Ben Healy took bronze behind Pogacar.
Pogacar attacked on Mont Kigali more than 100 km from the finish at the 2025 Worlds and dropped Mexico's Isaac Del Toro, the last rider with him.
Pogacar does not have a gold medal from the Games; NBC Sports has said a finish climbing to the Observatory could suit him, a four-time Tour de France winner.
Media previews also name Jonas Vingegaard (DEN) and Mathieu van der Poel (NED) alongside Pogacar and Evenepoel as the leading men of the current era.
The 2028 Tour de France will run June 24 to July 16, 2028, a week earlier than usual, which avoids a clash with the Games road race.

facts: Canoe slalom at the 2028 Games will be held at RIVERSPORT Rapids in Oklahoma City, a whitewater course that opened in 2016.
The Los Angeles City Council approved the organizers' venue proposal naming RIVERSPORT Rapids the canoe slalom venue in March 2025.
RIVERSPORT OKC is a U.S. national training site for canoe/kayak and rowing and houses the OKC National High Performance Center.
RIVERSPORT OKC hosted the 2026 ICF Canoe Slalom World Championships from July 20-25, 2026, the first world championships held in Oklahoma City, and the event served as a qualifier for the 2028 Games.
The women's K1 at the 2026 World Championships drew 62 competitors from 29 nations, using a three-round format of heats, semifinal and final.
Australia's Jessica Fox, Noemie Fox and Kate Eckhardt won the women's K1 team title at the 2026 World Championships in Oklahoma City, ahead of France and Slovakia.
Slovenia's Ziga Lin Hocevar, Lan Tominc and Peter Kauzer won the men's K1 team title at the 2026 World Championships in Oklahoma City, ahead of Switzerland and Austria.
Paris 2024 K1 champions were Jess Fox of Australia in the women's event and Giovanni De Gennaro of Italy in the men's event.
The Czech Republic topped the 2026 World Championships medal table with three golds and seven medals, while Australia also won three golds and Great Britain won two golds and six medals.
K1 heats at the 2028 Games consist of two runs, with athletes advancing to the semifinal and final rounds.

facts: Marine Stadium in Long Beach was confirmed in July 2024 as the canoe sprint venue for the 2028 Games, and it will also host rowing, as it did in 1932.
This session holds heats and quarterfinals for the men's and women's K2 500m, the men's C1 1000m and the women's C1 200m.
At Paris 2024, Czechia's Martin Fuksa won the men's C1 1000m, with Brazil's Isaquias Queiroz second.
Martin Fuksa won the men's C1 1000m at the 2025 World Championships in Milan, winning his heat in 3:46.32 and the final in 3:46.09.
Isaquias Queiroz finished ninth and last in the men's C1 1000m final at the 2026 World Championships in Poznan, after saying he had eye surgery and a hip problem that year.
Queiroz missed the 2025 World Championships because of the flu and has five career Games medals, including Tokyo 2020 gold and Paris 2024 silver in the C1 1000m.
Canada's Katie Vincent won the Paris 2024 women's C1 200m in a world-record 44.12 seconds, 0.01 seconds ahead of American Nevin Harrison (44.13), with Cuba's Yarisleidis Cirilo third in 44.36.
Nevin Harrison won the women's C1 200m at Tokyo 2020, the first gold won by a U.S. woman in sprint canoeing, and she was world champion in 2019 and 2022.
New Zealand's Lisa Carrington won the women's K2 500m at Paris 2024 with Alicia Hoskin, and Germany and Hungary shared the bronze after a photo-finish tie.
Carrington announced in April 2026 that she was pregnant and due in late September 2026, and she said the 2028 Games remain her goal.

Lisa Carrington won the women's K1 500m at Paris 2024 in a new Games-best time, part of a three-gold Games that took her career total to eight golds and tied the all-time canoeing record.
Carrington made her Games debut at London 2012, where she won the women's K1 200m.
Carrington announced in April 2026 that she was pregnant, due in late September, and she skipped the 2026 World Championships but said the 2028 Games are still her goal.
Carrington was 36 when she announced her pregnancy in April 2026 and would be chasing a fifth Games appearance in 2028.
Poland's Anna Pulawska won the women's K1 500m world title in Milan in 2025, ahead of Australia's Natalia Drobot and Hungary's Zsoka Csikos.
Josef Dostal of Czechia is the Paris 2024 men's K1 1000m champion, and Hungary's Adam Varga and Balint Kopasz took silver and bronze.
Kopasz won the 2025 world K1 1000m title in 3:25.50, with Australia's Thomas Green second, Portugal's Fernando Pimenta third and Dostal fourth.
Dostal, born in 1993, won the 2025 world K1 500m title, and the ICF lists him with one Games gold, one silver and three bronzes plus five world golds.
China won the women's C2 500m at Paris 2024.

facts: Track cycling at the 2028 Games is scheduled at Carson Velodrome, which publicly listed schedules show hosting sessions from July 25 to July 30, 2028.
Carson Velodrome is described as the largest indoor velodrome in the United States and is home to USA Cycling's national track program.
Carson Velodrome hosted the 2005 Track Cycling World Championships and the 2017 Para Cycling Track World Championships, and has a listed capacity of 2,400 for the Games.
The Netherlands won the men's team sprint at the 2025 World Championships in Santiago, Chile, with Roy van den Berg, Jeffrey Hoogland and Harrie Lavreysen beating Great Britain in the final.
The Netherlands posted the fastest men's team sprint qualifying time at the 2025 World Championships, 41.860.

The Netherlands (Kimberly Kalee, Hetty van de Wouw, Steffie van der Peet) won the women's team sprint at the 2025 World Championships in 45.743, ahead of Great Britain (46.003) and Australia (46.773).
Great Britain's Rhianna Parris-Smith, Iona Moir and Emma Finucane set the fastest women's team sprint qualifying time at the 2025 World Championships in 45.808.

The United States women's team sprint qualified fourth at the 2025 World Championships in 47.631, the first time the US had advanced to the first round at a World Championships, and finished seventh, the program's best result.
Great Britain is the reigning Paris 2024 women's team sprint champion, and the Netherlands is the reigning men's champion.

facts: CTR02 at Carson Velodrome on July 25, 2028 is the team sprint final session, also listed with men's team pursuit qualifying.
The Netherlands won the 2025 world men's team sprint title, beating Great Britain in the final with Roy van den Berg, Jeffrey Hoogland and Harrie Lavreysen.
Matt Richardson, who rode for Australia through Paris 2024 and switched to Great Britain in September 2024, won team sprint silver with Great Britain at the 2025 World Championships.
The Netherlands won the 2025 world women's team sprint in 45.743, ahead of Great Britain (46.003) and Australia (46.773).
Great Britain won the Paris 2024 women's team sprint in a world record 45.186, and the Netherlands won the men's event in a world record 40.949.
Denmark won the men's team pursuit at the 2025 World Championships in 3:43.915, ahead of Australia (3:47.258) and New Zealand (3:48.77).
The United States men's team pursuit finished fourth at the 2025 World Championships, 1.03 seconds behind New Zealand in the bronze-medal final.
Australia, the Paris 2024 men's team pursuit champion, took silver at the 2025 World Championships.

British Cycling withdrew Richardson from its squad for the 2026 World Championships in Shanghai, and he is reportedly under investigation over misconduct allegations; his 2028 status had not been publicly resolved as of October 2026.

facts: All diving events at the 2028 Games are scheduled for the Rose Bowl Aquatics Center in Pasadena, California.
The Rose Bowl Aquatics Center was confirmed as the diving venue in September 2025.
The 2028 diving program has eight medal events, four for men and four for women, with about 136 competitors expected.
Diving at the 2028 Games is governed by World Aquatics, which finalized the qualification system with the IOC.
The women's 3m springboard is an individual event decided over preliminary, semifinal and final rounds; the preliminary round sets the field for the semifinal.
Chen Yiwen of China won the women's 3m springboard gold medal at Paris 2024.
Maddison Keeney of Australia won the women's 3m springboard silver medal at Paris 2024.
China won all eight diving gold medals at Paris 2024, the first clean sweep of every diving event by any nation.

facts: Santa Anita Park in Arcadia, California, was confirmed in April 2025 as the venue for all equestrian events at the 2028 Games, having also hosted equestrian at the 1984 Los Angeles Games.
Santa Anita Park is a Thoroughbred racetrack with an on-site veterinary clinic that has hosted the Breeders' Cup.
Eventing dressage at the 2028 Games is spread over two days, with this session opening the equestrian program on Saturday July 15.
Germany's Michael Jung won the Paris 2024 individual eventing title on FischerChipmunk FRH, his third individual title, and set a Games record eventing dressage score there along with Laura Collett.
At the 2025 Kentucky Three-Day Event, Jung and FischerChipmunk FRH scored 18.6 in dressage, a CCI5*-L record that beat his own 20.1 mark from Kentucky 2022.
FischerChipmunk FRH was 17 years old in 2025, which raises questions about whether the horse will still be competing in 2028.
Great Britain's Laura Collett and London 52 won the 2025 European Eventing Championships individual title at Blenheim Palace.
Great Britain won Paris 2024 team eventing gold ahead of France and Japan.

facts: Eventing cross-country at the 2028 Games is set for Monday July 17 at Santa Anita Park, a Thoroughbred racetrack with grandstand seating for about 26,000 and room for about 50,000 more in the infield, according to NBC.
Under the FEI's hybrid eventing proposal for 2028, cross-country would still run to the current 10-minute specification, FEI eventing committee chair David O'Connor said.

The FEI's proposal put the team competition on a short format, with team medals decided after cross-country, while the individual competition kept the long format, with jumping the day after cross-country.
The published session schedule lists cross-country as a team and individual preliminary round, followed by a combined jumping finals session the next day.
Laura Collett and London 52 led after cross-country at the 2025 European Championships at Blenheim before winning the individual gold.
Horse & Hound reported that Collett called her Aachen 2026 cross-country round with London 52 the best she had ever had, after she survived a near miss.
Michael Jung, the three-time individual champion, won the 2025 Kentucky CCI5*-L on FischerChipmunk FRH.

The 2026 World Championships at Aachen ran from August 11 to 23, 2026, and were part of the qualification pathway to the 2028 Games.

facts: The dressage Grand Prix Special team final is on Saturday July 22 at Santa Anita Park and decides the team dressage medals.
Germany won Paris 2024 team dressage gold ahead of Denmark (silver) and Great Britain (bronze).
Germany won its 26th European team dressage title in 2025 at Crozet with 229.644 points, ahead of Great Britain on 226.785 and Denmark on 223.385.
Carl Hester, Charlotte Fry and Becky Moody provided the scores behind Great Britain's 2025 European team silver.
Eurodressage reported that Great Britain went into the 2025 European team competition as title favorites.

facts: The FEI confirmed Santa Anita Park in Arcadia, California, as the equestrian venue for the 2028 Games in April 2025, replacing the previously planned Galway Downs site in Temecula.
Santa Anita Park also hosted the equestrian events at the 1984 Los Angeles Games, where West Germany's Reiner Klimke won team and individual dressage gold on Ahlerich.
Santa Anita Park covers 320 acres and has veterinary facilities, a 26,000-seat grandstand and an infield.
At Paris 2024, Germany won team dressage gold ahead of Denmark (silver) and Great Britain (bronze).
The team dressage medals are decided in the Grand Prix Special, which follows the Grand Prix qualifying days.
TSF Dalera BB, the mare Jessica von Bredow-Werndl rode to team and individual gold at Paris 2024, was retired from competition in August 2024 at age 17.
Dalera BB had her first foal, a filly, in early 2026.
Von Bredow-Werndl won a World Cup dressage leg in Stuttgart in November 2025 on her newer horse Diallo BB, a sign of her possible next championship partner.
Germany's Paris 2024 team dressage gold continued its long record of team dressage titles, and Isabell Werth took individual silver at Paris 2024.
Team quota places for the 2028 Games come through the 2026 world championships, the 2027 continental championships, the 2027 Pan American Games and designated qualifying events.

facts: The men's tournament at the 2028 Games will have 12 teams, down from 16 at Paris 2024, after the IOC Executive Board approved 12 men's and 16 women's teams in April 2025.
The cut was part of a program change that gives every team sport at least as many women's teams as men's teams, and the total number of footballers at the Games stays the same.
Spain won the Paris 2024 men's gold, France won silver and Morocco won bronze.
Etihad Park in Willets Point, Queens, is the future home of New York City FC, holds about 25,000 and is set to open on July 17, 2027.
NYCFC pushed the Etihad Park opening back from its original plan to the start of the 2027-28 MLS season, so the stadium will have about one year of use before the 2028 Games.

Etihad Park will be called New York Stadium during the Games and will host nine football matches, with men's and women's group games on July 10-11, 13-14 and 16-17, plus a men's quarterfinal on July 20.
The football schedule runs east to west to cut down on travel: group games start in New York, Columbus, Nashville and St. Louis, and the medal matches are at the Rose Bowl in Pasadena.
The men's gold medal match is scheduled for July 28, 2028 at the Rose Bowl.
Asia's qualifying route for the men's event includes the 2028 AFC U-23 Asian Cup in Japan, which offers two places, plus an AFC-CONMEBOL play-off for one more.
Which teams will play the July 10 men's group matches at Etihad Park has not been confirmed; the men's event is expected to stay mostly under-23.

facts: Geodis Park in Nashville, home of MLS club Nashville SC, holds 30,109 and was named a football venue for the 2028 Games on Feb. 3, 2026.
Geodis Park is one of six MLS stadiums outside Los Angeles hosting group stage and knockout matches before the final rounds at the Rose Bowl.
The women's tournament at the 2028 Games expands to 16 teams, up from the 12 teams used in each of the previous five editions, after the IOC Executive Board approved the change in April 2025.
The United States, the Paris 2024 women's gold medalist, has qualified automatically for the 2028 Games as host nation.

The 2026 Concacaf W Championship, held in Texas from Nov. 27 to Dec. 5, 2026, also serves as qualifying: the top three finishers earn places at the 2028 Games, and if the US finishes in the top three, the fourth-place team gets the berth instead.
CAF's women's qualifying for the 2028 Games runs from June 4, 2026 to Dec. 4, 2027 for two berths, and AFC's runs from April 19, 2027 to March 4, 2028, also for two berths.
Group matchups at the 2028 Games will not be known until qualification progresses further and the official tournament draw is held.
In the FIFA women's world ranking of June 16, 2026, Spain was first, the United States second and Germany third.
Spain took the FIFA No. 1 ranking from the United States in August 2025 despite losing the Euro 2025 final to England on penalties.
At Paris 2024 the United States beat Brazil 1-0 in the final on a Mallory Swanson goal, and Germany won bronze.
US head coach Emma Hayes has capped 60 different players since taking over in November 2023, including a program-record 44 in 2025 alone, according to U.S. Soccer roster data.
The football tournament at the 2028 Games starts July 10, four days before the opening ceremony, and the women's gold medal match is set for July 29 at the Rose Bowl.

facts: Energizer Park in St. Louis, home of MLS club St. Louis City SC, holds 22,423 and was named a football venue for the 2028 Games on Feb. 3, 2026.
Energizer Park is one of six MLS stadiums outside Los Angeles hosting group stage and knockout matches before the final rounds at the Rose Bowl.
The women's tournament at the 2028 Games expands to 16 teams, up from the 12 teams used in each of the previous five editions, after the IOC Executive Board approved the change in April 2025.
The United States, the Paris 2024 women's gold medalist, has qualified automatically for the 2028 Games as host nation.

The 2026 Concacaf W Championship, held in Texas from Nov. 27 to Dec. 5, 2026, also serves as qualifying: the top three finishers earn places at the 2028 Games, and if the US finishes in the top three, the fourth-place team gets the berth instead.
CAF's women's qualifying for the 2028 Games runs from June 4, 2026 to Dec. 4, 2027 for two berths, and AFC's runs from April 19, 2027 to March 4, 2028, also for two berths.
Group matchups at the 2028 Games will not be known until qualification progresses further and the official tournament draw is held.
In the FIFA women's world ranking of June 16, 2026, Spain was first, the United States second and Germany third.
Spain took the FIFA No. 1 ranking from the United States in August 2025 despite losing the Euro 2025 final to England on penalties.
At Paris 2024 the United States beat Brazil 1-0 in the final on a Mallory Swanson goal, and Germany won bronze.
US head coach Emma Hayes has capped 60 different players since taking over in November 2023, including a program-record 44 in 2025 alone, according to U.S. Soccer roster data.
The football tournament at the 2028 Games starts July 10, four days before the opening ceremony, and the women's gold medal match is set for July 29 at the Rose Bowl.

facts: Etihad Park, a 25,000-seat soccer-specific stadium being built next to Citi Field at Willets Point in Queens, is the future home of New York City FC and was named a football venue for the 2028 Games on Feb. 3, 2026.

NYCFC pushed Etihad Park's opening back to summer 2027, the start of the 2027-28 MLS season, with test events planned before the club moves in, so the stadium will be about a year old at the 2028 Games.
NWSL club Gotham FC was reported in May 2026 to be exploring a move to Etihad Park for the 2028 NWSL season.

The men's tournament at the 2028 Games shrinks to 12 teams from 16 at Paris 2024, a change approved by the IOC Executive Board in April 2025, and the FIFA Council approved the final allocation of berths in December 2025.
The United States has qualified for the men's tournament as host nation, and Mexico has qualified through the 2026 CONCACAF U-20 Championship, played in Mexico from July 25 to Aug. 9, 2026.
UEFA has three men's berths, decided at the 2027 UEFA European Under-21 Championship in Albania and Serbia from June 17 to July 4, 2027; Spain and France would need to qualify through that event.
CAF's two men's berths will be decided at the 2027 U-23 Africa Cup of Nations in Egypt from Nov. 19 to Dec. 4, 2027; Paris 2024 bronze medalist Morocco would qualify through that route.
AFC's two men's berths will be decided at the 2028 AFC U-23 Asian Cup in Japan from Jan. 4 to 22, 2028.
CONMEBOL has two men's berths and OFC has one, and as of September 2026 neither confederation had announced its qualification process.
At Paris 2024, men's squads were limited to under-23 players born on or after Jan. 1, 2001, with up to three overage players; the 2028 men's event is expected to keep a mostly under-23 format.
At Paris 2024, Spain beat host France 5-3 after extra time in the final for its second men's football gold, and Morocco won bronze, its first medal in the sport.
The football tournament at the 2028 Games starts July 10, four days before the opening ceremony, and the men's gold medal match is set for July 28 at the Rose Bowl.
Group matchups at the 2028 Games will not be known until qualification progresses further and the official tournament draw is held.

facts: ScottsMiracle-Gro Field in Columbus, home of MLS club Columbus Crew, holds 20,371 and was named a football venue for the 2028 Games on Feb. 3, 2026.
ScottsMiracle-Gro Field is one of six MLS stadiums outside Los Angeles hosting group stage and knockout matches before the final rounds at the Rose Bowl.

The men's tournament at the 2028 Games shrinks to 12 teams from 16 at Paris 2024, a change approved by the IOC Executive Board in April 2025, and the FIFA Council approved the final allocation of berths in December 2025.
The United States has qualified for the men's tournament as host nation, and Mexico has qualified through the 2026 CONCACAF U-20 Championship, played in Mexico from July 25 to Aug. 9, 2026.
UEFA has three men's berths, decided at the 2027 UEFA European Under-21 Championship in Albania and Serbia from June 17 to July 4, 2027; Spain and France would need to qualify through that event.
CAF's two men's berths will be decided at the 2027 U-23 Africa Cup of Nations in Egypt from Nov. 19 to Dec. 4, 2027; Paris 2024 bronze medalist Morocco would qualify through that route.
AFC's two men's berths will be decided at the 2028 AFC U-23 Asian Cup in Japan from Jan. 4 to 22, 2028.
CONMEBOL has two men's berths and OFC has one, and as of September 2026 neither confederation had announced its qualification process.
At Paris 2024, men's squads were limited to under-23 players born on or after Jan. 1, 2001, with up to three overage players; the 2028 men's event is expected to keep a mostly under-23 format.
At Paris 2024, Spain beat host France 5-3 after extra time in the final for its second men's football gold, and Morocco won bronze, its first medal in the sport.
The football tournament at the 2028 Games starts July 10, four days before the opening ceremony, and the men's gold medal match is set for July 28 at the Rose Bowl.
Group matchups at the 2028 Games will not be known until qualification progresses further and the official tournament draw is held.

facts: Geodis Park, home of Nashville SC, will be called Nashville Stadium during the Games and has a listed capacity of 30,109, second only to San Diego's 35,000 among the six venues outside the Rose Bowl.

The women's tournament expands to 16 teams for the 2028 Games, the first time a Games football program will feature more women's teams than men's teams (16 vs 12).
The United States, defending champion from Paris 2024 where it beat Brazil 1-0 in the final, is qualified automatically as host nation.

CONCACAF's remaining berths will be decided at the 2026 CONCACAF W Championship in the United States from November 27 to December 5, 2026; because the U.S. is already qualified, all semifinalists will qualify if the U.S. reaches the semifinals.

England beat world champion Spain 3-1 on penalties after a 1-1 draw in the Euro 2025 final in Basel on July 27, 2025, with Chloe Kelly scoring the winning kick to defend the European title.
Brazil took silver and Germany took bronze in the women's tournament at Paris 2024.
The women's gold medal match is scheduled for July 29, 2028 at the Rose Bowl in Pasadena.
Women's teams at the Games have no age restrictions, so full senior national teams take part.

facts: This session is a women's group-stage match. Group opponents and pairings depend on qualifying that is still going on.
Snapdragon Stadium in San Diego, home of San Diego FC, San Diego Wave FC and San Diego State University, is one of seven football venues for the 2028 Games.
The 2028 Games football tournaments are scheduled for July 10 to 29, 2028, in Los Angeles and six other U.S. cities.
The women's tournament expands to 16 teams for 2028 after the IOC Executive Board approved FIFA's recommendation in April 2025.
The United States, the Paris 2024 women's gold medalist, qualified automatically as host nation.

The FIFA Council's December 2025 allocation gives women's berths of 2.5 to AFC, 2 to CAF, 3 to Concacaf, 2.5 to CONMEBOL, 1 to OFC and 4 to UEFA, plus the host slot, with an AFC-CONMEBOL playoff in 2028 for the final place.
Brazil and Colombia qualified by reaching the 2025 Copa America Femenina final, which Brazil won 5-4 on penalties after a 4-4 draw on August 2, 2025, with Marta named player of the match.
Concacaf's three women's berths are decided at the 2026 Concacaf W Championship, scheduled for November 27 to December 5, 2026, in the United States.

UEFA's four women's berths go to the four highest-ranked eligible League A teams in the 2027 UEFA Women's Nations League, which runs February 25 to June 15, 2027. Spain are the two-time defending Nations League champions.
AFC women's qualifying runs April 2027 to March 2028 and CAF women's qualifying runs June 2026 to December 2027, with two berths each before the playoff.
Women's football at the Games has no age limit, so full senior national teams take part.
Unlike the previous three editions, no group-stage matches are scheduled near Los Angeles. The preliminary match schedule was released on November 12, 2025.

facts: This session is a women's quarterfinal, the first knockout round of the 16-team tournament. The teams are not yet known.
The Rose Bowl Stadium in Pasadena hosts the final-stage matches, including the men's gold medal match on July 28, 2028 and the women's gold medal match on July 29, 2028.
The United States beat Brazil 1-0 in the Paris 2024 final on a Mallory Swanson goal, winning a record fifth women's gold. Germany took bronze.
The women's tournament expands to 16 teams for 2028 after the IOC Executive Board approved FIFA's recommendation in April 2025.
The United States qualified automatically as host nation.

The FIFA Council's December 2025 allocation gives women's berths of 2.5 to AFC, 2 to CAF, 3 to Concacaf, 2.5 to CONMEBOL, 1 to OFC and 4 to UEFA, plus the host slot, with an AFC-CONMEBOL playoff in 2028 for the final place.
Brazil and Colombia qualified by reaching the 2025 Copa America Femenina final, which Brazil won 5-4 on penalties after a 4-4 draw on August 2, 2025, with Marta named player of the match.
Concacaf's three women's berths are decided at the 2026 Concacaf W Championship, scheduled for November 27 to December 5, 2026, in the United States.

UEFA's four women's berths go to the four highest-ranked eligible League A teams in the 2027 UEFA Women's Nations League, which runs February 25 to June 15, 2027. Spain are the two-time defending Nations League champions.
AFC women's qualifying runs April 2027 to March 2028 and CAF women's qualifying runs June 2026 to December 2027, with two berths each before the playoff.
Women's football at the Games has no age limit, so full senior national teams take part.
The football tournaments run July 10 to 29, 2028, and no group-stage matches are scheduled near Los Angeles.

Spain are the defending men's champions after beating host France 5-3 after extra time in the Paris 2024 final, and Morocco won bronze, the country's first medal in the sport.
The men's tournament is expected to keep its mostly under-23 squad format; no men's semifinalists are known as qualification has not been completed.

The 2025 world men's team épée event drew 47 teams from 47 nations, which shows how deep the field is behind the eight teams that will reach the 2028 Table of 8.
Koki Kano, the Paris 2024 individual épée champion, also won the 2025 individual world title, beating teammate Masaru Yamada in the semifinals and Hungary's Gergely Siklósi in the final.

facts: Canada's women are the reigning world champions after beating the United States 27-20 in the 2026 IFAF World Championship final in Dusseldorf.
The 2026 loss ended a streak of three consecutive women's world titles for the United States.
Canada and Mexico women earned 2028 Games quotas at the 2026 Worlds, and the U.S. women qualify as hosts.
Mexico played Great Britain in the 2026 women's bronze medal game.
Great Britain's women retained the 2025 IFAF European Flag Football Championship title by beating Austria in the final.
A U.S. women's player scored 10 combined receiving and rushing touchdowns at the 2026 Worlds, the most by any U.S. player at that event per USA Football.
The women's bronze and gold medal games on the final day of the tournament (July 22, 2028) will award the first women's flag football medals at a Summer Games.
The final day's games are at Exposition Park Stadium (BMO Stadium), home of LAFC and NWSL's Angel City FC, located next to the LA Memorial Coliseum.
Full women's field and rosters for the 2028 Games were not confirmed in sources found.

facts: Men's Qualification 1 is the opening artistic gymnastics session of the 2028 Games, scheduled for Saturday, July 15, 2028, at DTLA Arena (Crypto.com Arena) in downtown Los Angeles.
Artistic gymnastics at the 2028 Games is scheduled to run from July 15 to July 25, and DTLA Arena also hosts trampoline and boxing during the Games.
Men's qualification is split across three subdivisions on July 15, and results from this round set the fields for the men's team final, all-around final and apparatus finals.
The 2028 artistic program has 15 medal events: eight for men, six for women and a new mixed team event, with 192 gymnasts in total (96 men and 96 women).
Each nation may enter at most one team of five gymnasts per gender with no reserves, and nations without a team may enter up to three individual gymnasts.

At the 2025 World Championships in Jakarta, Daiki Hashimoto of Japan won his third straight world all-around title with 85.131, ahead of Zhang Boheng of China (84.333) and Noe Seifert of Switzerland (82.831).
Paris 2024 all-around champion Shinnosuke Oka finished fifth in the all-around at the 2025 World Championships with 81.797.
Carlos Yulo of the Philippines, who won floor and vault at Paris 2024, won vault gold at the 2025 World Championships with 14.866, edging Artur Davtyan of Armenia (14.833).
Noe Seifert's 2025 world all-around bronze was Switzerland's first world all-around medal since 1950.
Colombia's Angel Barajas, the Paris 2024 horizontal bar silver medalist, placed sixth in the all-around at the 2025 World Championships.

In the 2025 European mixed team format, each team was one man and one woman, and qualification was by name, so gymnasts could not be substituted unless injured.

Shinnosuke Oka won three golds at Paris 2024 (team, all-around and horizontal bar) and a parallel bars bronze.

facts: Skye Blakely (USA) won the women's all-around title at the 2026 World Championships in Rotterdam on Oct 23, 2026, with 55.733 points.
Liudmila Roshchina, competing for the neutral Russian team listed as WG2, took 2026 world all-around silver (55.199), and Ke Qinqin of China took bronze (55.032).
Kaylia Nemour (ALG) finished fourth in the all-around at both the 2025 Worlds (54.564) and the 2026 Worlds (54.998).
Blakely missed Paris 2024 after an injury at the U.S. Trials, and she is the ninth American woman to win the world all-around title.
Angelina Melnikova, competing as a neutral athlete, won the 2025 world all-around title in Jakarta with 55.066, just ahead of Leanne Wong (USA) at 54.966 and Zhang Qingying (CHN) at 54.633.
At least one U.S. woman has reached every world and Games all-around podium since 2003, a run of 23 straight global championships going into the 2026 Worlds, which Blakely's 2026 title extended.
Simone Biles, the Paris 2024 all-around champion, said in September 2026 that she still had not decided whether to try for a fourth Games in 2028; she will be 31 when the Los Angeles Games open.
Biles said her coach Laurent Landi told her to 'give me two years,' and in August 2026 she posted photos from her childhood training gym in Texas that set off talk of a comeback.

Rebeca Andrade, the Paris 2024 all-around silver medalist, went back to training in early 2025 and said she plans to compete at a fourth Games in 2028, which she has called likely her last competition.
Andrade won the vault title at the 2026 World Championships, her third world vault title.
Suni Lee won the Paris 2024 all-around bronze; the sources reviewed did not show her competing at the 2025 or 2026 Worlds.

facts: All golf at the 2028 Games, including the men's 72-hole individual stroke play event, is set for The Riviera Country Club in Pacific Palisades, Los Angeles, according to the International Golf Federation.
Riviera Country Club is the annual host of the PGA Tour's Genesis Invitational.
The individual fields are 60 men and 60 women, based on the IGF's mixed-team proposal, which draws its teams from those already-qualified players.
Adding the mixed-team event meant moving the men's competition to a Wednesday-to-Saturday schedule so the team event could be held on the Sunday and Monday between the men's and women's events.
Scottie Scheffler (USA) is the defending champion; he won Paris 2024 at 19 under after a closing 62, with Tommy Fleetwood (GBR) taking silver and Hideki Matsuyama (JPN) bronze.
Scheffler won six PGA Tour events in 2025, including the PGA Championship and the Open Championship, bringing his career major total to four.
Scheffler was named 2025 PGA Tour Player of the Year, his fourth straight time winning the award.
Tommy Fleetwood won the 2025 Tour Championship for his first PGA Tour title and the FedEx Cup.
Fleetwood reached a career-high world ranking of No. 3 on 30 November 2025.

facts: The IOC Executive Board approved a golf mixed-team event for the 2028 Games on 9 April 2025.
According to the IGF, the mixed-team event is 36 holes: 18 holes of four-ball (best ball) in the first round, then 18 holes of foursomes (alternate shot) in the final round.
Some earlier media reports of the proposal listed foursomes first, but the IGF's official 2028 competition page lists four-ball as Round 1.
Each country may enter at most one team, made up of one man and one woman already qualified for the individual stroke play events.
The IGF's proposal called for 16 teams drawn from the 60 men and 60 women in the individual fields.
The mixed-team event is played after the men's four-round individual event and before the women's.
The IGF says this will be golf's first team competition at the Games since 1904.
Media previews have floated a possible USA pairing of Scottie Scheffler and Nelly Korda; teams have not been announced.

facts: Denmark won the 2025 IHF Men's World Championship, beating co-host Croatia 32-26 in the final in Baerum, Norway, on 2 February 2025.
The 2025 title made Denmark the first men's national team to win four consecutive world titles (2019, 2021, 2023, 2025).
Mathias Gidsel was MVP and top scorer at the 2025 Men's World Championship with 74 goals from 107 shots, including 10 goals from 11 attempts in the final.
Denmark won the 2026 EHF Men's Euro on home soil, beating Germany 34-27 in the final in Herning on 1 February 2026, its third European title and first since 2012.
Gidsel was MVP of the 2026 EHF Euro with 68 goals, a record for a single European Championship.
After the 2026 EHF Euro, Denmark held the world, European and Paris 2024 titles at the same time, a feat previously achieved only by France.
Germany, the Paris 2024 runner-up, also reached the 2026 EHF Euro final, its second major final against Denmark after the Paris 2024 gold medal match.
France, the 2024 European champion, was eliminated in the main round of the 2026 EHF Euro and finished 7th.
Croatia won silver at the 2025 Men's World Championship, its first world podium since 2013.

As host nation, the United States holds one automatic quota place per gender, with the remaining places decided through continental events and three qualification tournaments per gender in spring 2028.

Brazil (6th) and Angola (10th) were the only non-European teams in the top 10 at the 2025 Women's World Championship.
Netherlands veterans Lois Abbingh and Estavana Polman retired from the national team after the 2025 Women's World Championship.

Mathias Gidsel was MVP and top scorer at the 2025 Men's World Championship with 74 goals from 107 shots, including 10 goals from 11 attempts in the final.
Denmark won the 2026 EHF Men's Euro on home soil, beating Germany 34-27 in the final in Herning on 1 February 2026, its third European title and first since 2012.
Gidsel was MVP of the 2026 EHF Euro with 68 goals, a record for a single European Championship.
After the 2026 EHF Euro, Denmark held the world, European and Paris 2024 titles at the same time, a feat previously achieved only by France.
Germany, the Paris 2024 runner-up, also reached the 2026 EHF Euro final, its second major final against Denmark after the Paris 2024 gold medal match.
France, the 2024 European champion, was eliminated in the main round of the 2026 EHF Euro and finished 7th.
Croatia won silver at the 2025 Men's World Championship, its first world podium since 2013.

As host nation, the United States holds one automatic quota place per gender, with the remaining places decided through continental events and three qualification tournaments per gender in spring 2028.
All handball matches at the 2028 Games are scheduled for Long Beach Arena, located within the Long Beach Convention and Entertainment Center in downtown Long Beach, California.
Each 12-team tournament opens with a preliminary round before quarterfinals, semifinals and the bronze and gold medal matches.

facts: The 2028 men's quarterfinals are scheduled for Sunday, July 23, at Long Beach Arena, with four matches across the day.
Each 2028 tournament has 12 teams in two groups of six, with the top finishers advancing to the quarterfinals.
The U.S. men lost all three preliminary-round matches at the 2025 World Championship, to Portugal 30-21, Norway 33-17 and Brazil 31-24, and went to the President's Cup.
Denmark won Paris 2024 gold by beating Germany 39-26 in the final, with Spain taking bronze.
Denmark won the 2025 IHF Men's World Championship, beating co-host Croatia 32-26 in the final in Baerum, Norway, for an unprecedented fourth consecutive world title.
Denmark won the 2026 EHF Men's European Championship, beating Germany 34-27 in the final in Herning on 1 February 2026, its first European title in 14 years.
Mathias Gidsel, a right back for Fuechse Berlin, was MVP and top scorer of the 2026 European Championship with 68 goals, a record for a single men's European Championship.
Gidsel was MVP and top scorer at the 2025 World Championship with 74 goals from 107 shots and scored 10 goals from 11 attempts in the final.
Germany reached the final at both Paris 2024 and the 2026 European Championship, losing to Denmark each time.
Croatia took silver at the 2025 World Championship, its first podium at a world championship since 2013; captain Domagoj Duvnjak retired from international handball after that final.
Defending European champion France was eliminated in the main round of the 2026 European Championship and finished 7th.

As of July 2026 the United States men were the only qualified team, via the host place; men's qualification runs through the 2027 World Championship in Germany (13-31 January 2027), continental events and three qualification tournaments on 3-9 April 2028.
All 2028 handball matches are at Long Beach Arena in downtown Long Beach; the men's tournament runs from July 12 to July 27, 2028.

Spain, the Paris 2024 bronze medalist, would be projected as a quarterfinal contender if it qualifies; its 2028 qualification path includes the 2028 European Championship it co-hosts with Portugal and Switzerland (13-30 January 2028).
Denmark won Paris 2024 gold by beating Germany 39-26 in the final, with Spain taking bronze.
Denmark won the 2025 IHF Men's World Championship, beating co-host Croatia 32-26 in the final in Baerum, Norway, for an unprecedented fourth consecutive world title.
Denmark won the 2026 EHF Men's European Championship, beating Germany 34-27 in the final in Herning on 1 February 2026, its first European title in 14 years.
Mathias Gidsel, a right back for Fuechse Berlin, was MVP and top scorer of the 2026 European Championship with 68 goals, a record for a single men's European Championship.
Gidsel was MVP and top scorer at the 2025 World Championship with 74 goals from 107 shots and scored 10 goals from 11 attempts in the final.
Germany reached the final at both Paris 2024 and the 2026 European Championship, losing to Denmark each time.
Croatia took silver at the 2025 World Championship, its first podium at a world championship since 2013; captain Domagoj Duvnjak retired from international handball after that final.
Defending European champion France was eliminated in the main round of the 2026 European Championship and finished 7th.

As of July 2026 the United States men were the only qualified team, via the host place; men's qualification runs through the 2027 World Championship in Germany (13-31 January 2027), continental events and three qualification tournaments on 3-9 April 2028.
All 2028 handball matches are at Long Beach Arena in downtown Long Beach; the men's tournament runs from July 12 to July 27, 2028.

facts: The 2028 women's quarterfinals are scheduled for Monday, July 24, at Long Beach Arena, with four matches across the day.
Each 2028 tournament has 12 teams in two groups of six, with the top finishers advancing to the quarterfinals.
Norway won Paris 2024 gold by beating France 29-21, with Denmark taking bronze.
Norway won the 2024 Women's EHF European Championship, beating Denmark 31-23 in the Vienna final for its 10th European title and third in a row.
Norway won the 2025 IHF Women's World Championship, beating Germany 23-20 in the final at Ahoy Arena in Rotterdam on 14 December 2025.
Germany knocked defending world champion France out in the semifinals of the 2025 Women's World Championship before losing the final to Norway.
Henny Reistad of Norway and Team Esbjerg was named IHF World Player of the Year for 2023, 2024 and 2025; she is the second woman after Cristina Neagu to win it three times.
Brazil's Bruna de Paula and Norway goalkeeper Katrine Lunde finished behind Reistad in the 2025 IHF World Player of the Year vote.
Reistad was top scorer of the 2024/25 EHF Champions League Women with Team Esbjerg.
As of July 2026 the United States women were the only qualified women's team, via the host place; no other team had yet earned a 2028 berth.
All 2028 handball matches are at Long Beach Arena; the women's tournament runs from July 13 to July 28, 2028, alternating days with the men through the group stage.

facts: The two men's semifinals are scheduled for Tuesday, July 25, at Long Beach Arena, ahead of the men's medal matches, with the men's tournament ending on July 27.
Semifinal winners advance to the gold medal match; losers play for bronze.
Denmark has beaten Germany in two straight major finals: 39-26 at Paris 2024 and 34-27 at the 2026 European Championship.
Denmark won Paris 2024 gold by beating Germany 39-26 in the final, with Spain taking bronze.
Denmark won the 2025 IHF Men's World Championship, beating co-host Croatia 32-26 in the final in Baerum, Norway, for an unprecedented fourth consecutive world title.
Denmark won the 2026 EHF Men's European Championship, beating Germany 34-27 in the final in Herning on 1 February 2026, its first European title in 14 years.
Mathias Gidsel, a right back for Fuechse Berlin, was MVP and top scorer of the 2026 European Championship with 68 goals, a record for a single men's European Championship.
Gidsel was MVP and top scorer at the 2025 World Championship with 74 goals from 107 shots and scored 10 goals from 11 attempts in the final.
Germany reached the final at both Paris 2024 and the 2026 European Championship, losing to Denmark each time.
Croatia took silver at the 2025 World Championship, its first podium at a world championship since 2013; captain Domagoj Duvnjak retired from international handball after that final.
Defending European champion France was eliminated in the main round of the 2026 European Championship and finished 7th.
All 2028 handball matches are at Long Beach Arena in downtown Long Beach; the men's tournament runs from July 12 to July 27, 2028.

facts: All handball matches at the 2028 Games will be played at Long Beach Arena, on the downtown Long Beach waterfront.
The handball competition starts on July 12, 2028 with the men's preliminary round, two days before the Opening Ceremony, and the women's preliminary round begins a day later.
Norway are the reigning Paris 2024 champions, having beaten France 29-21 in the final, and Denmark took bronze.
Norway won the 2025 IHF Women's World Championship, beating Germany 23-20 in the final at Ahoy Arena in Rotterdam on December 14, 2025.
In the 2025 world championship semifinals, Norway beat the Netherlands 35-25 and Germany knocked out defending world champions France.
Norway's 2025 world title was its fifth, making it the only team with five women's world championship trophies.
Henny Reistad was MVP and top scorer, with 55 goals, at the 2025 Women's World Championship, her second straight world championship MVP award.
The IHF named Reistad women's world handball player of the year in 2023, 2024 and 2025.
Brazil finished sixth at the 2025 world championship, the best result by a non-European team.
As host, the United States has an automatic women's quota place, which will be its first women's handball appearance at the Games since 1996.

facts: Denmark are the Paris 2024 champions after beating Germany 39-26 in the gold medal match, and Spain won bronze.

Mathias Gidsel scored 10 goals in the 2025 world final and was named tournament MVP.
Co-host Denmark won the 2026 EHF European Championship, beating Germany 34-27 in the final at Jyske Bank Boxen in Herning, for its third European title and first in 14 years.
Gidsel was MVP of the 2026 European Championship with 68 goals, a record for any European Championship.
Before the 2026 European Championship, Gidsel publicly said it would be wrong not to call Denmark the biggest favorites.
Gidsel was born on February 8, 1999, plays right back for Füchse Berlin and will be 29 at the 2028 Games.
Germany, the Paris 2024 silver medalists, also lost the 2026 European final to Denmark, so the two teams have met in back-to-back major finals.
The men's gold medal match is at Long Beach Arena, where men's handball begins on July 12, 2028.

facts: The women's play-in round is on Sunday, July 23, 2028 at Carson Field, with two matches from 9:00 to 14:00 and two more from 17:00 to 22:00.
Under the 2028 format, eight teams that do not go straight through from the pool stage play off for four quarterfinal places.
The women's tournament has 12 teams of 16 players, the same 12-team field used for each gender since 2008.

The USA has a host-nation place; the other places come from the FIH Hockey Pro League, five continental championships and two eight-team qualification tournaments in early 2028, with the top two from each tournament qualifying.
The Netherlands won the 2025-26 Women's FIH Pro League, which counts toward 2028 qualification, and the FIH said 2025-26 and 2026-27 winners qualify directly.
At the end of 2025 the FIH women's world rankings had the Netherlands first, followed by Argentina, Belgium and China.
New Zealand moved up to ninth in the women's rankings in 2025 after winning the Women's FIH Nations Cup and the Oceania Cup, passing India, who were relegated from the Pro League that year.
Italy, Uruguay and South Africa finished 2025 just inside the women's top 20, with Canada and Malaysia just outside.
Spain took bronze at the 2025 Women's EuroHockey Championship, behind the Netherlands and Germany.
At Paris 2024, Argentina won women's bronze by beating Belgium in a shoot-out, and China took silver.

Hungary's Roza Gyertyas and Germany's Mascha Ballhaus were the 2025 women's -52kg world bronze medalists.

Portugal's Patricia Sampaio won the women's -78kg title at the 2025 European Championships in Podgorica, beating Anna Monta Olek in the final.
As host nation, the USA gets one quota place in each individual weight category, including men's -100kg and women's -78kg.

facts: Lacrosse at the 2028 Games runs July 24-29, 2028 at Exposition Park Stadium in Los Angeles.

Six men's teams will compete in the Sixes format, with a round-robin stage followed by bronze and gold medal games on Saturday, July 29.
The United States qualifies as host; World Lacrosse expects about 100 men's and women's teams to enter the qualification pathway.
The qualification pathway was formally approved by the IOC Executive Board on February 1, 2026.
Canada is ranked No. 1 in World Lacrosse's men's sixes rankings, followed by the United States, Japan, Great Britain, Haudenosaunee and Australia.
Exposition Park Stadium (BMO Stadium) seats about 22,000, sits next to the LA Memorial Coliseum, and is home to LAFC and Angel City FC.
Men's qualifying teams other than the United States had not been decided as of late 2026; most spots will be settled at the 2027 World Lacrosse Sixes Championships.

facts: The men's lacrosse tournament at the 2028 Games will have six teams playing the Sixes format, with a round-robin stage followed by bronze and gold medal games.
As host, the United States gets one guaranteed place in each gender, provided it takes part in its continental qualifier and the 2027 World Lacrosse Sixes Championships.
Four men's places will be decided at the 2027 World Lacrosse Sixes Championships, set for October 4-10, 2027 in Colorado Springs, USA, with 16 teams per gender.
The last men's place will be decided at a final qualifying tournament expected in March/April 2028, featuring the top six men's teams not already qualified.
At the 2026 Pan-American Sixes Lacrosse Championships in Oshawa, Canada, the United States men won gold and Canada finished second.
The USA, Canada, Haudenosaunee, Puerto Rico and Brazil men qualified from the 2026 Pan-American Sixes Championships for the 2027 World Sixes Championships.
Australia's men took the first Asia-Pacific spot for the 2027 World Sixes Championships at the 2026 Asia-Pacific Sixes Lacrosse Championships on the Sunshine Coast, Australia.
The Philippine men qualified for the 2027 World Sixes Championships at the 2026 Asia-Pacific event after losing 15-14 to China in their opener and then beating South Korea 22-7.
Canada beat the United States in the men's Sixes gold medal game at The World Games 2022 in Birmingham, Alabama, and the Haudenosaunee finished fifth.

Andy Shay is head coach of the U.S. Men's Sixes National Team, and in 2025 he split a 24-player pool into two squads for the Atlas Cup and World Lacrosse Super Sixes as the program builds toward the 2028 Games.
The 2025 U.S. Sixes player pool included PLL MVP finalists Pat Kavanagh, Brennan O'Neill, Connor Shellenberger and Michael Sowers, plus goalies Liam Entenmann, Logan McNaney and Blaze Riorden.
At the September 2025 Atlas Cup, U.S. attacker Coulter Mackesy led the team with 11 goals and 16 points in three games, and Matt Brandau made the all-tournament team with 15 points.
Canada's 2025 Atlas Cup men's roster included PLL Championship Game MVP Jeff Teat.

The Haudenosaunee Nationals, credited with originating lacrosse, have pushed for inclusion at the 2028 Games, and in January 2025 the U.S. and Canada issued a statement backing their participation; their final eligibility for the Games was not confirmed in available sources.

facts: The women's lacrosse tournament at the 2028 Games will be the first time women's lacrosse is played for medals at the Games, with six teams in the Sixes format and a round-robin stage ahead of bronze and gold medal games.

Four women's places will be decided at the 2027 World Lacrosse Sixes Championships in Colorado Springs (October 4-10, 2027), and the last place at a final qualifying tournament expected in March/April 2028.
The United States women beat Canada 16-8 in the Sixes gold medal game at The World Games 2025 in Chengdu, China, on August 11, 2025.
The 2025 World Games win avenged the U.S. women's 14-12 loss to Canada in the Sixes final at The World Games 2022.
Canada's Jordan Dean got a red card 1:52 into the 2025 World Games final, and the U.S. led 7-3 after the first quarter.
Australia won women's Sixes bronze at The World Games 2025, beating Japan 13-12 on a Georgia Latch golden goal 27 seconds into overtime, which defended its 2022 bronze.
Marie McCool of the United States was MVP of The World Games 2025 women's Sixes tournament, and teammates Charlotte North and Shea Dolce also made the World Team.
Canada's Erica Evans and Brooklyn Walker-Welch made The World Games 2025 women's Sixes World Team.
The U.S. women's roster for the September 2025 Atlas Cup included Chloe Humphrey, Sam Apuzzo, Marie McCool, Charlotte North, Izzy Scane, and goalies Taylor Moreno and Shea Dolce.
At the 2026 Pan-American Sixes Championships in Oshawa, the United States women won gold and Canada finished second.

The USA, Canada, Haudenosaunee, Puerto Rico and Argentina women qualified from the 2026 Pan-American event for the 2027 World Sixes Championships, and Argentina took the last spot by beating Jamaica 17-11 in the fifth-place game.
At the 2026 Asia-Pacific Sixes Championships, Australia's women beat the Philippines 24-3, and the Philippine women also qualified for the 2027 World Sixes Championships.

facts: The women's individual semifinal at the 2028 Games is scheduled for Saturday, July 15, 2028, 9:00-13:30 Pacific Time at Valley Complex 2 in the Valley Zone, formerly called the Sepulveda Basin Recreation Area, in the San Fernando Valley.
Modern pentathlon opens the 2028 Games program, holding the first four days of competition (July 15-18) for the first time since 1992, with women's and men's semifinals on the first two days.
Under the new format, each semifinal and final has 18 athletes and runs in this order: direct-elimination fencing, then obstacle, then swimming, then the laser run.
In the obstacle discipline, athletes race head-to-head over a 70m course with eight obstacles, and it replaces the horse riding last used at Paris 2024.
Michelle Gulyas (HUN) won gold at Paris 2024, ahead of Elodie Clouvel (FRA) with silver and Seong Seung-Min (KOR) with bronze.
Egypt's Farida Khalil, aged 14 in 2025, won the 2025 senior world title in Kaunas, Lithuania, and also won world titles at Junior (U22), U19 and U17 level that year.
Before the 2025 World Championships, UIPM described Khalil as world No.1 and world record-holder, and she won the 2025 World Cup Final in Alexandria, Egypt.
Blanka Guzi (HUN), fourth at Paris 2024, won a second straight world silver medal in 2025, and Aurora Tognetti (ITA) took bronze.
Gulyas won the 2025 World Cup in Budapest on home soil in April 2025 but missed the 2025 World Championships because she had not recovered from an injury.

Other women expected to contend, based on 2025 form, include France's Rebecca Castaudi, the 2025 European champion, Hungary's Blanka Bauer and Seong Seung-Min, who was reigning world champion going into 2025.

facts: The men's individual final at the 2028 Games is scheduled for Tuesday, July 18, 2028, 9:00-11:00 Pacific Time at Valley Complex 2, and is the last of the sport's four days.

Moutaz Mohamed (EGY) won the 2025 world title in Kaunas by 17 seconds and dominated the laser run, after already winning the 2025 World Cup Final.
France's Rochat, a former world junior champion, won world silver in 2025.
Czechia's Matej Lukes won bronze at the 2025 World Championships, after taking silver at the 2025 World Cup Final.
Egypt holds both the Paris 2024 men's title through El-Gendy and the 2025 men's world title through Mohamed.

facts: The 2028 Games mountain bike races will be held at the Industry Hills MTB Course in the City of Industry, Los Angeles County, next to the Pacific Palms Resort, after organizers moved the venue from Bonelli Park in San Dimas.

Organizers describe the Industry Hills course as set in the hills of the San Gabriel Valley with technical sections including drops and jumps, plus spectator areas close to the action; exact route length and elevation profile had not been published as of the 2025 announcement.

Tom Pidcock (GBR), gold medalist at Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024, won the 2026 men's elite XCO world title in Val di Sole, starting 35th on the grid and finishing ahead of fellow Briton Charlie Aldridge, his second XCO world title after 2023.
Pidcock won the 2026 world title after finishing ninth overall at the 2026 Tour de France, and he had raced his mountain bike only once that year before the championships.

After the 2026 world championships, Pidcock said he would focus on road racing in 2027 and return to mountain biking before the 2028 Games, where he would be going for a third consecutive gold in the event.

Alan Hatherly (RSA), Paris 2024 bronze medalist, won back-to-back XCO world titles in 2024 and 2025; in 2025 at Crans-Montana, Switzerland, he won in 1:30:30, 48 seconds ahead of Simone Avondetto (ITA) and 51 seconds ahead of Victor Koretzky (FRA).
Hatherly joined the road team Jayco-AlUla in 2025 and said combining road and mountain bike racing that season was difficult, with the world title defense a major goal.
Victor Koretzky (FRA), Paris 2024 silver medalist, won the short track (XCC) world title and took XCO bronze at the 2025 world championships.

Christopher Blevins (USA) won both the 2025 XCO and XCC World Cup overall titles, finishing the XCO series with 1996 points ahead of Martín Vidaurre Kossmann (CHI) on 1695 and Luca Martin (FRA) on 1546.
Pinkbike readers noted Blevins was the first American man to win the XCO World Cup overall since John Tomac, a storyline for a home-soil race at the 2028 Games.
Charlie Aldridge (GBR) won the 2025 World Cup finale at Mont-Sainte-Anne and was runner-up to Pidcock at the 2026 world championships.
Ten-time world champion Nino Schurter (SUI) rode his final world championships in 2025, finishing 42nd, and Mathieu van der Poel (NED) finished 29th in that race.
The men's cross-country is a single mass-start final with no heats, scheduled for July 17, 2028 at Industry Hills.

facts: The women's 10km at the 2028 Games is scheduled for July 17 at Belmont Shore in Long Beach, California, raced in the Pacific Ocean, with the men's race the following day.

The 2028 field is capped at 22 athletes, and the main qualification routes are the 2027 World Aquatics Championships in Budapest (open water July 4-8, 2027), the open water world ranking in February 2028, and a 2028 qualification event.

The top three finishers in the women's 10km at the 2027 World Aquatics Championships in Budapest earn places at the 2028 Games, and the remaining spots are decided at a qualification event planned for spring 2028.
Paris 2024 champion Sharon van Rouwendaal of the Netherlands announced her retirement on September 5, 2025, at age 31, so she will not defend her title in 2028.
Van Rouwendaal retired as the only swimmer to win two gold medals in the 10km (2016 and 2024), and she also took silver at Tokyo 2020.
Paris 2024 silver medalist Moesha Johnson of Australia won the women's 10km at the 2025 World Aquatics Championships in Singapore in 2:07:51.3, the first world 10km title ever won by an Australian.
Johnson also won the 5km and took bronze in the 3km knockout sprint in Singapore, and SwimSwam reported she finished 2025 ranked No. 1.
World Aquatics named Johnson its 2025 female Open Water Swimmer of the Year.
Paris 2024 bronze medalist Ginevra Taddeucci of Italy took silver in both the 10km and the 5km at the 2025 World Championships, finishing about 4.4 seconds behind Johnson in the 10km.
Monaco's Lisa Pou won bronze in the 2025 world 10km, Monaco's first ever medal at a World Aquatics Championships.
Taddeucci won the 2025 World Cup overall women's title after winning the final 10km stop in Golfo Aranci, Italy, in October 2025.
Johnson and Taddeucci went one-two at the 2025 World Cup opener in Soma Bay, Egypt, finishing 16 seconds clear of third place, which continued a rivalry from their Paris podium.
The 2025 world 10km races in Singapore were postponed because of poor water quality off Sentosa, so water conditions remain a storyline for ocean venues.
Johnson and Taddeucci are projected to contend in 2028 based on their 2025 form, but neither has qualified yet.

facts: The men's 10km at the 2028 Games is scheduled for July 18 at Belmont Shore in Long Beach, California, raced in the Pacific Ocean, one day after the women's race.

The 2028 field is capped at 22 athletes, and the main qualification routes are the 2027 World Aquatics Championships in Budapest (open water July 4-8, 2027), the open water world ranking in February 2028, and a 2028 qualification event.

The top three in the men's 10km at the 2027 World Aquatics Championships in Budapest earn places at the 2028 Games, and the remaining spots are decided at a qualification event planned for spring 2028.

Germany's Florian Wellbrock won the men's 10km at the 2025 World Aquatics Championships in Singapore, holding off a late charge from Italy's Gregorio Paltrinieri, with Australia's Kyle Lee taking bronze.
Wellbrock's 2025 win made him the first swimmer to win three world titles in the 10km, and it was his seventh world title in open water.
Wellbrock won the 10km at Tokyo 2020, and World Aquatics named him its 2025 male Open Water Swimmer of the Year.
The 2025 silver gave Paltrinieri his 17th World Championships medal, and the bronze was Kyle Lee's first individual medal at an international event.
Paris 2024 champion Kristof Rasovszky of Hungary and his teammate, bronze medalist David Betlehem, were among the pre-race favorites in Singapore in 2025 but did not reach the podium.
Rasovszky won the first European 3km knockout sprint title at the 2025 European Open Water Championships in Stari Grad, Croatia.
Paris 2024 silver medalist Oliver Klemet of Germany was listed among the top contenders before the 2025 world 10km.
The 2025 world 10km races in Singapore were postponed because of poor water quality, and Wellbrock described the conditions as very warm water.
Wellbrock and Paltrinieri are projected to contend in 2028 based on their 2025 form, but neither has confirmed participation or qualified.

facts: Beach sprint coastal rowing at the 2028 Games is held along Belmont Shore in Long Beach on July 24-25, 2028.
The 2028 Games will be the first time a rowing event at the Games is raced on the ocean.
The 2028 Games allocate 64 of rowing's 502 quota places to beach sprints, and each nation can qualify at most one male and one female athlete.
The main qualification event is the 2027 World Rowing Beach Sprint Finals in Oeiras, Portugal, scheduled for 6-9 October 2027, along with continental qualification events.
A beach sprint race includes a run up the sand, a 250m slalom row with two buoys, a 180-degree turn around a final buoy and a row back to shore before a run to the finish.
At the 2026 World Rowing Beach Sprint Finals in Qingdao, Moritz Wolff (GER) set the fastest men's solo time trial, 3.3 seconds ahead of defending champion Chris Bak (USA).
At the 2026 world finals in Qingdao, Isabella Scammell (AUS) won the women's solo time trial 1 by seven seconds over Raminta Morkunaite (LTU) and Zhu Wenjie (CHN), with Magdalena Lobnig (AUT) fourth.

At the 2025 world finals in Antalya, Wolff was fastest in the men's solo time trials and Emma Twigg (New Zealand) posted the fastest women's time, while defending champions Bak and Lobnig also advanced to the knockouts.
The 2026 time trials in Qingdao were run in difficult surf, with many capsizes, after storms cancelled training and competition over the opening weekend.
The men's solo at the 2026 world finals drew 48 entries, the largest men's solo field in World Rowing beach sprint history.
Samuel Forbes (AUS) was seventh in the 2026 time trials and went on to win men's solo silver, which shows that a seeding position from the time trials does not decide the knockouts.
