facts: Chris Bak (USA) won the men's solo at the World Rowing Beach Sprint Finals in 2024 and 2025 and is a four-time beach sprint world champion.
After the 2025 world finals, Bak had six World Rowing Beach Sprint Finals medals (four gold, one silver, one bronze), and nobody has won more gold medals.
Bak won the first-ever US beach sprint gold in the men's solo in 2022 in Saundersfoot, Wales.
At the 2026 world finals in Qingdao, 21-year-old Liu Jiayu (CHN) won the men's solo ahead of 20-year-old Samuel Forbes (AUS), and Moritz Wolff (GER) took bronze over Allison Russo (POR).
Liu Jiayu overcame an equipment failure in the 2026 final when his boat's sliding seat came loose, and he won China's first men's solo world title.
On the way to the 2026 final, Forbes knocked out Bak in the quarterfinals, and Liu beat European champion Ander Martin (ESP).
At the 2025 world finals, Bak beat Ander Martin (ESP) in the men's solo final, after Wolff tripped and fell on the beach run in his semifinal against Martin.
Isabella Scammell (AUS) won the 2026 women's solo world title ahead of Zhu Wenjie (CHN), which was Australia's first gold at any Beach Sprint Finals.
Magdalena Lobnig (AUT) won women's solo bronze in 2026, after gold in 2024 and silver in 2025, and has reached the podium three years in a row.
In the 2026 women's solo knockouts, Christine Cavallo (USA) missed the buzzer in her quarterfinal against Scammell, and Lobnig went the wrong way around a slalom buoy in her semifinal.
None of these athletes has been confirmed for the 2028 Games, because quota places will be decided mainly at the 2027 world finals in Oeiras, Portugal.

facts: The mixed double sculls at the 2028 Games will be the first mixed-gender rowing event ever held at the Games.
The mixed double sculls is one of three beach sprint medal events at the 2028 Games, alongside the men's and women's solos, held at Belmont Shore in Long Beach.
At the 2026 world finals in Qingdao, Isabella Scammell won the mixed double sculls time trial for Australia with Oscar Scheel Gambo, in addition to winning the women's solo time trial.
Germany split up its European champions Julia Tertuente and Moritz Wolff to race solos at the 2026 world finals, and entered Franz Werner with Sophie Leupold in the mixed double.
Lithuania's Dominykas Jancionis and Martyna Kazlauskaite won mixed double sculls gold in 2024 in Genoa and in 2025 in Antalya.
The 2025 mixed double sculls field drew 33 entries, including multi-gold medallist Adrian Miramon Quiroga of Spain and Tokyo 2020 champion Federica Cesarini of Italy.
The 2028 qualification system allows a nation to enter a boat with different athletes from those who earned the quota place at the qualification events.

Results from the last 16 of the three 2028 event classes at the 2026 world finals qualified China, Australia, Germany, Lithuania, Portugal, Spain and the USA for the new World Rowing Beach Sprint Series in 2027.

facts: The mixed double sculls final at the 2028 Games will award the first medals ever given in a mixed-gender rowing event at the Games.
At the 2026 world finals in Qingdao, Germany won mixed double sculls gold over two-time champions Lithuania, and Poland took bronze for its first-ever beach sprint medal.
Germany's pre-event entry for the 2026 mixed double was Franz Werner and Sophie Leupold, according to World Rowing's preview; the final report did not name the gold-medal crew.
Lithuania's Dominykas Jancionis and Martyna Kazlauskaite won mixed double sculls gold in 2024 and 2025.
In 2024 in Genoa, Italy's Silvia Tripi and Federico Ceccarino took mixed double silver and Spain's Ander Martin and Esther Briz Zamorano took bronze.
At the 2025 world finals in Antalya, the USA won mixed double sculls silver behind Lithuania, with Chris Bak sprinting in the finish run.
Spain's Ander Martin has won two mixed double sculls world golds and a bronze, and was 2025 men's solo silver medallist and European men's solo champion.
Mixed double crews for the 2028 Games have not been confirmed; nations earn places mainly at the October 2027 world finals in Oeiras, Portugal.

Karolien Florijn (NED) won the women's single sculls at Paris 2024 ahead of Emma Twigg (NZL) and Viktorija Senkute (LTU).
Fiona Murtagh (IRL) won the women's single sculls at the 2025 World Rowing Championships in Shanghai in 7:12.27, ahead of Lauren Henry (GBR) and Frida Sanggaard Nielsen (DEN).
The 2025 world championship women's single sculls field had 19 scullers from 19 nations.
Romania won the men's double sculls and Croatia won the men's pair at Paris 2024.
Simon van Dorp (NED), the Paris 2024 men's single sculls bronze medalist, won the men's double sculls title at the 2026 World Rowing Championships in Amsterdam.
Most 2028 Games boats will qualify at the 2027 World Rowing Championships in Lucerne, followed by continental and final qualification regattas.

facts: RU701 is the opening session of the women's rugby sevens tournament at the 2028 Games, with six pool-play matches on Wednesday, July 12, 2028.
The 2028 women's tournament has 12 teams and runs July 12-15, 2028, before the men's tournament (July 16-18), which reverses the Paris 2024 order.
Matches are played at Carson Stadium, the venue known as Dignity Health Sports Park in Carson, California.
The United States qualifies automatically for the women's tournament as host nation.
The other places go to the top four eligible teams in the 2027 SVNS World Championship standings, six regional qualifier winners, and one repechage winner.
New Zealand is the two-time defending women's champion after winning in Tokyo and beating Canada 19-12 in the Paris 2024 final.
Canada won silver at Paris 2024, and the United States won its first-ever medal in the sport with bronze, beating Australia 14-12 on a try in the final seconds.
Australia won the first women's rugby sevens gold at the Rio 2016 Games and finished fourth at Paris 2024.
Pool-play results decide quarterfinal seeding and which teams drop into the 9-12 classification bracket.
Final pool compositions and the full qualified field for 2028 had not been confirmed when this brief was compiled, because live search was unavailable.
RU702 is the second women's pool-play session of the 2028 Games, with six matches on the evening of Wednesday, July 12, 2028.
All rugby sevens matches at the 2028 Games are at Carson Stadium (Dignity Health Sports Park) in Carson, California.
The women's tournament has 12 teams in pool play, followed by quarterfinals, classification matches, semifinals, and medal matches.
As host, the United States qualifies automatically and comes in as the Paris 2024 bronze medalist.
Ilona Maher's high profile helped make the Paris 2024 U.S. women's sevens team one of the big stories of those Games.

Since Paris 2024, Maher has also played fifteens, including for the United States at the 2025 Women's Rugby World Cup; she had not given a public final decision on a 2028 sevens roster spot when this brief was compiled.
New Zealand, the Paris 2024 gold medalist, has won the last two women's titles at the Games.
Canada reached the Paris 2024 final and lost 19-12 to New Zealand after leading.
RU703 is the final women's pool-play session of the 2028 Games, with six matches on the morning of Thursday, July 13, 2028.
The results of this session complete the pool standings and set the quarterfinal matchups played that afternoon in RU704.
Teams that do not advance from pool play move to the 9-12 classification bracket.
The venue is Carson Stadium (Dignity Health Sports Park) in Carson, California.
Qualification for 2028 comes from host status (USA), the top four eligible teams in the 2027 SVNS World Championship, six regional qualifiers, and a repechage.
New Zealand (gold), Canada (silver), and the United States (bronze) were the Paris 2024 women's medalists.
Australia finished fourth at Paris 2024 after losing the bronze medal match 14-12 to the United States.
Rugby sevens drew more than 500,000 fans at the Stade de France during Paris 2024, an attendance record for the sport.
RU704 on Thursday, July 13, 2028, has the women's 9-12 classification matches and the four women's quarterfinals.
Quarterfinal winners go to the semifinals on Saturday, July 15; quarterfinal losers move to the 5-8 classification bracket.
In the Paris 2024 women's knockout stage, New Zealand, Canada, the United States, and Australia reached the semifinals.
The United States beat Australia 14-12 for the Paris 2024 bronze medal with a try in the final seconds, the country's first medal in the sport.
New Zealand is trying to win a third straight women's title after its wins in Tokyo and Paris 2024.
The session is played at Carson Stadium (Dignity Health Sports Park) in Carson, California.
Each match is seven-a-side with two seven-minute halves, so one try can decide a knockout game.
RU705 on Saturday, July 15, 2028, has the women's 5-8 classification matches, the 9-12 placing matches, and both women's semifinals.
The semifinal winners play for gold, and the semifinal losers play for bronze in the evening session, RU706.
At Paris 2024, New Zealand and Canada won their semifinals to reach the women's final.
Canada's semifinal win at Paris 2024 put it into its first women's sevens final at the Games.
The United States lost its Paris 2024 semifinal and then won bronze against Australia.
The session is played at Carson Stadium (Dignity Health Sports Park) in Carson, California.
The United States qualifies automatically as host and would be playing a semifinal at home if it gets this far.
RU706 on Saturday evening, July 15, 2028, has the women's 5-8 placing matches, the bronze medal match, and the gold medal match.
These are the first rugby sevens medals of the 2028 Games, because the women's tournament comes before the men's this time.
New Zealand won the Paris 2024 women's gold by coming from behind to beat Canada 19-12, keeping the title it won in Tokyo.
Australia won the first women's sevens gold at Rio 2016, and New Zealand took silver there.
The United States won its first medal in the sport at Paris 2024, a bronze, by beating Australia 14-12 with a last-second try.
A New Zealand win in 2028 would give it a third straight women's title.
The medal matches are played at Carson Stadium (Dignity Health Sports Park) in Carson, California.
Ilona Maher's public profile grew a great deal after Paris 2024; whether she will be on the 2028 U.S. sevens roster had not been confirmed when this brief was compiled.
RU707 opens the men's rugby sevens tournament at the 2028 Games, with six pool-play matches on Sunday, July 16, 2028.
The 12-team men's tournament runs July 16-18, 2028, after the women's tournament; at Paris 2024 the men played first.
The United States qualifies automatically for the men's tournament as host.
The other men's places come from the top four eligible teams in the 2027 SVNS World Championship, six regional qualifiers, and a repechage.
France is the defending men's champion after beating Fiji 28-7 in the Paris 2024 final.
Fiji won the men's gold at Rio 2016 and Tokyo, and its loss in the Paris 2024 final ended its unbeaten record at the Games.
South Africa won the men's bronze at Paris 2024.
Matches are played at Carson Stadium (Dignity Health Sports Park) in Carson, California.
RU708 is the second men's pool-play session, with six matches on the evening of Sunday, July 16, 2028.
France comes into 2028 as defending champion; Antoine Dupont came off the bench in the Paris 2024 final to score two tries and set up a third.
France's sevens gold was the host nation's first gold medal of Paris 2024.
Dupont went back to fifteens after Paris 2024 and had a serious knee injury in March 2025; he had not publicly committed to a 2028 sevens return when this brief was compiled.
Fiji, the two-time champion before Paris, took silver after losing 28-7 to France in the 2024 final.
The session is played at Carson Stadium (Dignity Health Sports Park) in Carson, California.
The United States qualifies automatically as host for the men's tournament.
RU709 is the final men's pool-play session, with six matches on the morning of Monday, July 17, 2028.
The results of this session complete the men's pool standings and set the quarterfinals played that afternoon in RU710.
Teams that do not advance from the pools move to the 9-12 classification bracket.
The Paris 2024 men's medalists were France (gold), Fiji (silver), and South Africa (bronze).
Fiji won the first two men's sevens golds at the Games, in Rio 2016 and Tokyo.
The venue is Carson Stadium (Dignity Health Sports Park) in Carson, California.
Final men's pool compositions for 2028 depend on qualification that finishes after the 2027 SVNS World Championship standings, the regional qualifiers, and the repechage.
RU710 on Monday, July 17, 2028, has the men's 9-12 classification matches and the four men's quarterfinals.
Quarterfinal winners go to the semifinals, and quarterfinal losers move to the 5-8 classification bracket; the men's medal matches are on July 18.
France won the Paris 2024 men's title by beating Fiji 28-7 in the final.
South Africa won the Paris 2024 men's bronze medal match.
Fiji's loss in the Paris 2024 final was its first defeat at the Games after golds in Rio 2016 and Tokyo.
The session is played at Carson Stadium (Dignity Health Sports Park) in Carson, California.
As host, the United States qualifies automatically and would play any quarterfinal in front of a home crowd.
This session includes the men's rugby sevens semifinals plus classification matches for places 5-8 and placing matches for 9-12 at Carson Stadium on July 18, 2028.
The men's tournament at the 2028 Games has 12 teams, and the United States qualifies automatically as host.
Other men's places come from the top four eligible teams in the 2027 SVNS World Championship standings, six regional qualifiers, and a final repechage.
At the 2028 Games the women's tournament runs first (July 12-15) and the men's follows (July 16-18), the reverse of the Paris 2024 order.
At Paris 2024, France won men's gold by beating Fiji 28-7 in the final, ending Fiji's unbeaten record at the Games, and South Africa took bronze.
Antoine Dupont came off the bench in the Paris 2024 final to score two tries and set up a third for France.
South Africa won the 2025/26 men's HSBC SVNS Series title, clinching it with a 10-7 win over Fiji in the SVNS New York Cup Final on March 15, 2026.
The 2026 New York Cup Final between South Africa and Fiji was a winner-takes-all match between the two in-form men's sevens sides, based on RugbyPass reporting.
As the SVNS 1 series champion, South Africa was exempt from relegation at the following World Championships.
Fiji won men's gold at Rio 2016 and Tokyo 2020 before taking silver at Paris 2024.
Full qualification for the 2028 men's field is not yet settled; apart from the host United States, contenders such as South Africa, Fiji and France are projected to contend based on recent form.

facts: World Sailing says the 2028 sailing competition runs July 16-28, 2028, with the board events (kite and windsurfing) held first at Belmont Shore in Long Beach.
Belmont Shore also hosted sailing at the 1984 Los Angeles Games and is set to be part of an aquatics hub that will also stage open water swimming and coastal beach sprint rowing.
The 10 sailing events will be staged one after another; World Sailing says this is meant to boost spectator engagement and broadcast coverage.
Men's and women's kite will be the first sailing medals decided, on July 19, 2028.
Italy's Riccardo Pianosi and Jessie Kampman won the 2025 Formula Kite World Championships in Quartu Sant'Elena, Sardinia (Sept 28-Oct 5, 2025).
Singapore's Max Maeder, the Paris 2024 bronze medalist, came into the 2025 Worlds as defending world champion, led after the opening day and finished with silver.
Switzerland's Gian Stragiotti and Britain's Sam Dickinson were named as up-and-coming men's riders at the 2025 Formula Kite Worlds, where Stragiotti was in second place overall after day four.
The 2025 Formula Kite World Championships drew 96 riders.

In Paris 2024 men's kite, Valentin Bontus (AUT) won gold, Toni Vodišek (SLO) silver and Max Maeder (SGP) bronze; in women's kite, Ellie Aldridge (GBR) won gold, Lauriane Nolot (FRA) silver and Annelous Lammerts (NED) bronze.

facts: The Port of Los Angeles in San Pedro hosts the six boat events at the 2028 Games: men's and women's dinghy, men's and women's skiff, mixed dinghy and mixed multihull.
The board events go first at Belmont Shore in Long Beach, and then the competition moves to the Port of Los Angeles for the boat events.
The organizing committee confirmed the split venue plan on June 30, 2025, citing good racing conditions and spectator viewing at the Port.
Sailing at the 2028 Games runs from July 16 to July 28, 2028, with the men's and women's skiff as the last medals decided.
At Paris 2024, Australia's Matt Wearn won the men's one-person dinghy (ILCA 7), Cyprus's Pavlos Kontides took silver and Peru's Stefano Peschiera took bronze.
At Paris 2024, Marit Bouwmeester of the Netherlands won the women's one-person dinghy (ILCA 6), Denmark's Anne-Marie Rindom took silver and Norway's Line Høst took bronze.
Willem Wiersema of the Netherlands, then 23, won the 2025 ILCA 7 World Championship in Qingdao on 11 points, one ahead of Pavlos Kontides (12) and two ahead of Australia's Zac Littlewood (13).
Louise Cervera of France won the 2025 ILCA 6 Women's World Championship in Qingdao, where four windless days left only a few races.
Hungary's Jonatán Vadnai won the 2026 ILCA 7 Men's World Championship in Dún Laoghaire, Ireland, Hungary's first title in the event.
Charlotte Rose of the United States won the 2026 ILCA 6 Women's World Championship on Dublin Bay, the first non-European winner of that title in 20 years.

Qualification for the 2028 Games has begun: South Korea's Jeemin Ha (ILCA 7) and Thailand's Sophia Montgomery (ILCA 6) won the first one-person dinghy quota spots at an Asian qualifier in October 2026.

facts: This session opens the men's skiff (49er) and women's skiff (49erFX) and continues the one-person dinghy, mixed dinghy and mixed multihull series.
At Paris 2024, Spain won the men's skiff, New Zealand took silver and the United States took bronze.
Spain's Diego Botín and Florian Trittel, who won the men's skiff at Paris 2024, won their first 49er world title in Cagliari in October 2025 after nearly a year away from the class.
At the 2025 49er worlds, the Netherlands' Bart Lambriex and Floris van de Werken took silver and Denmark's Jonas Warrer and Mathias Lehm Sletten took bronze.
Spain's Paula Barceló and María Cantero won the 2025 49erFX World Championship, completing a Spanish sweep of both skiff titles.

At the 2025 49erFX worlds, Sweden's Vilma Bobeck and Ebba Berntsson took silver and Canada's Georgia and Antonia Lewin-LaFrance took bronze, Canada's first world championship podium in the class in over two decades.
New Zealand's Seb Menzies and George Lee Rush won the 2026 49er World Championship in Quiberon, France.
Norway's Pia Dahl Andersen and Nora Edland won the 2026 49erFX world title by one point over Barceló and Cantero.
John Gimson and Anna Burnet (GBR) won the 2025 Nacra 17 world title, and Jordi Xammar and Marta Cardona (ESP) won the 2025 470 world title.

facts: The men's and women's one-person dinghy medals are decided in this session at the Port of Los Angeles.
Matt Wearn of Australia is the reigning men's one-person dinghy champion from Paris 2024, where Pavlos Kontides (CYP) took silver and Stefano Peschiera (PER) took bronze.
Marit Bouwmeester of the Netherlands is the reigning women's one-person dinghy champion from Paris 2024, where Anne-Marie Rindom (DEN) took silver and Line Høst (NOR) took bronze.
Pavlos Kontides, silver medalist at Paris 2024, also took silver at the 2025 ILCA 7 worlds, finishing one point behind Willem Wiersema (NED).
Peschiera, bronze medalist at Paris 2024, finished eighth at the 2025 ILCA 7 worlds, and Hungary's Jonatán Vadnai finished fourth.
Vadnai went on to win the 2026 ILCA 7 World Championship in Dún Laoghaire, Hungary's first title in the event.
The 2026 ILCA 7 worlds were decided under sailing's new finals format, and the 49er class pointed to its close finish as evidence the format works.
American Charlotte Rose won the 2026 ILCA 6 Women's World Championship after leading going into the Final Series, which would make her a home contender at the 2028 Games.
Belgium's Emma Plasschaert led the 2026 ILCA 6 women's worlds after day three, and Ireland's Eve McMahon finished seventh.
France's Louise Cervera won the 2025 ILCA 6 women's world title in Qingdao.

In this session the mixed dinghy and multihull run their third day and the skiffs run their second day; at Paris 2024, Spain won the men's skiff, New Zealand took silver and the United States took bronze.

facts: The mixed two-person dinghy (470) and mixed multihull (Nacra 17) medals are decided in this session at the Port of Los Angeles, and the skiffs race their third day.
Italy is the reigning Nacra 17 champion from Paris 2024, with Argentina taking silver and New Zealand bronze.
Austria is the reigning mixed 470 champion from Paris 2024, with Japan taking silver and Sweden bronze.
Britain's John Gimson and Anna Burnet won the 2025 Nacra 17 world title in Cagliari, their third in the class, finishing just ahead of Italy's Gianluigi Ugolini and Maria Giubilei.
The 2025 Nacra 17 medal races were sailed on foiling catamarans at more than 20 knots in rough seas.
At the 2026 Nacra 17 World Championship in Quiberon, a new world champion was crowned and Gimson and Burnet took bronze.
Australia's Brin Liddell and Rhiannan Brown finished fourth at the 2025 Nacra 17 worlds, their career best.
Spain's Jordi Xammar and Marta Cardona won the 2025 mixed 470 world title in Gdynia, Poland, overtaking Britain's Martin Wrigley and Bettine Harris on the final leg; the British pair finished third.
France's Matisse Pacaud and Lucie de Gennes led the 2025 470 worlds after two days.

facts: The men's skiff (49er) and women's skiff (49erFX) medals are the last medals of the 2028 Games sailing competition, decided on July 28 at the Port of Los Angeles.
At Paris 2024, Spain won the men's skiff, New Zealand took silver and the United States took bronze.
Spain's Diego Botín and Florian Trittel, the Paris 2024 men's skiff champions and SailGP champions, won their first 49er world title in Cagliari in October 2025 after years of near-misses.
The 2025 skiff world championship medals were decided in a double-race medal series.
New Zealand's Seb Menzies and George Lee Rush won the 2026 49er World Championship in Quiberon after a close final race; Austria's Keanu Prettner and Jakob Flachberger took silver.
The Netherlands' Bart Lambriex and Floris van de Werken, three-time 49er world champions, took silver at the 2025 worlds and bronze at the 2026 worlds.
Menzies also co-helms Emirates Team New Zealand's America's Cup boats, and he and Lee Rush won the open European 49er title in 2025.
Spain's Paula Barceló and María Cantero won the 2025 49erFX world title, ahead of Sweden's Vilma Bobeck and Ebba Berntsson and Canada's Lewin-LaFrance sisters.
Norway's Pia Dahl Andersen and Nora Edland won the 2026 49erFX World Championship by one point over Barceló and Cantero, winning the final race.

facts: Men's and women's 10m air rifle are among the 15 shooting medal events confirmed for the 2028 Games, and the IOC kept shooting at 340 athlete quota places, the same as Paris 2024.
ISSF said its format changes for the 2028 Games cycle apply from 1 January 2026, so athletes can adapt during qualification.
Qualification for the 2028 Games starts at the ISSF World Championship Rifle/Pistol/Shotgun in Doha in 2026, where the first quota places are awarded.
At Paris 2024, China's Sheng Lihao won the men's 10m air rifle and South Korea's Ban Hyo-Jin won the women's 10m air rifle ahead of China's Huang Yuting.
Ban Hyojin of South Korea won the women's 10m air rifle world title at the 2025 ISSF World Championship Rifle/Pistol in Cairo, scoring 255 in the final, with China's Wang Zifei taking silver on 254.
India's Elavenil Valarivan won bronze in the women's 10m air rifle at the 2025 World Championship in Cairo.
Germany's Maximilian Dallinger won the men's 10m air rifle world title in Cairo in November 2025 with 252, just ahead of Sweden's Victor Lindgren on 251.7.
China won the men's 10m air rifle team event at the 2025 World Championship in Cairo with a world record 1898.4, ahead of Germany, and also won the women's team title with 1901.7.
The 2025 World Championship Rifle/Pistol ran 6-18 November 2025 in Cairo, Egypt, and was the first rifle/pistol world championship since Paris 2024.
The 2028 Games session at Long Beach Target Shooting Hall runs qualification and finals for both the women's and men's 10m air rifle on the same day.

facts: Men's and women's 10m air pistol are among the 15 shooting medal events confirmed for the 2028 Games, and shooting keeps 340 athlete quota places.
ISSF format changes for the 2028 Games cycle apply from 1 January 2026.
The first quota places for the 2028 Games will be awarded at the 2026 ISSF World Championship Rifle/Pistol/Shotgun in Doha.
At Paris 2024, China's Xie Yu won the men's 10m air pistol.
At Paris 2024, South Korea's Oh Ye-Jin and Kim Ye-Ji took gold and silver in the women's 10m air pistol, and India's Manu Bhaker won bronze.
Manu Bhaker did not win a medal in the women's 25m pistol at the 2025 World Championship in Cairo, while fellow Indian Esha Singh won bronze there.
China's Yao Qianxun won three gold medals at the 2025 World Championship in Cairo, including a world-record win in the women's 50m pistol, which is not a 2028 Games event.
The 2025 World Championship Rifle/Pistol ran 6-18 November 2025 in Cairo and was the first world championship in these disciplines since Paris 2024.
The 2028 Games session at Long Beach Target Shooting Hall runs qualification and finals for both the men's and women's 10m air pistol on the same day.

facts: The 2028 Games shotgun events will be held at Whittier Narrows Clay Shooting Center in South El Monte, within the Whittier Narrows Recreation Area, while rifle and pistol events go to the Long Beach Target Shooting Hall.
Under the ISSF 2026 Rulebook, skeet finals now take eight athletes instead of six, so the top eight from qualification advance to the final.
The new eight-athlete skeet final format was tested at the 2025 ISSF World Cup Final in Doha, and the rules took effect on January 1, 2026.
Vincent Hancock (USA) won Paris 2024 men's skeet gold, his fourth in the event, and has said he intends to go for a fifth men's skeet gold at the 2028 Games.
Hancock won his fifth world title in men's skeet at the 2025 ISSF World Championship Shotgun in Athens, and the USA (Hancock, Conner Prince, Christian Elliott) also won the men's skeet team title.
Samantha Simonton (USA) won her first world title in women's skeet at Athens 2025 with 57, ahead of Mexico's Gabriela Rodriguez (54) and Sweden's Victoria Larsson.
At the 2025 ISSF World Cup Final in Doha, Christian Elliott won men's skeet ahead of Hancock and Dustan Taylor, so Americans took all three men's skeet medals.
At the 2025 ISSF World Cup Final, China's Jiang Yiting won women's skeet ahead of Simonton and Greece's Emmanouela Katzouraki.
ISSF reported that all three U.S. women's skeet athletes, Kimberly Rhode, Samantha Simonton and Dania Vizzi, won ISSF World Cup gold medals in 2025.
Francisca Crovetto (CHI) is the reigning Paris 2024 women's skeet champion, with Amber Rutter (GBR) silver and Austen Smith (USA) bronze.
The first skeet quota places for the 2028 Games are scheduled to be awarded on November 6, 2026 at the ISSF World Championship in Doha, three each for men and women.

facts: The 10m air rifle mixed team and 10m air pistol mixed team events are part of the 2028 Games shooting programme of 15 medal events.
ISSF has confirmed that in the 10m air rifle, 10m air pistol and trap mixed team events at the 2028 Games, the top four qualifying teams go straight into one medal final.
The new mixed team format replaces the separate gold and bronze medal matches used at Paris 2024, and the four finalist teams now compete together using an elimination format.
ISSF said the new mixed team format followed extensive testing at ISSF competitions and feedback from athletes, coaches, officials and broadcasters.
ISSF said the format changes need no extra technology or space and do not affect technical official resources.
At Paris 2024, China won the 10m air rifle mixed team gold, beating South Korea in the gold medal match, which gave Sheng Lihao his second gold of those Games.
At Paris 2024, Serbia won the 10m air pistol mixed team gold ahead of Türkiye, and India, with Manu Bhaker, won bronze.
China won both the men's and women's 10m air rifle team events at the 2025 World Championship in Cairo, setting a world record of 1898.4 in the men's event.
Qualification for the 2028 Games starts at the 2026 ISSF World Championship in Doha.

facts: Men's and women's skeet medals for the 2028 Games are decided in an eight-athlete final at Whittier Narrows Clay Shooting Center, up from six finalists at Paris 2024.
At Paris 2024, Vincent Hancock (USA) won men's skeet gold ahead of his student and teammate Conner Prince (USA), with Lee Meng-Yuan (TPE) taking bronze.
Hancock hit 58 of 60 shots in the Paris 2024 final and closed with 26 straight hits.
After Paris, Hancock said he had expected to retire but could not pass up competing at a home Games, and a fifth men's skeet gold would be a Games first.

Hancock won the 2026 USA Shooting National Championship in men's skeet, breaking all 36 final targets to win by one over Christian Elliott, and both Hancock and Prince made the U.S. men's skeet national team.
Hancock won his fifth men's skeet world title at the 2025 ISSF World Championship in Athens.
Christian Elliott (USA) won the 2025 ISSF World Cup Final men's skeet title in Doha ahead of Hancock and Dustan Taylor.
Francisca Crovetto (CHI) is the reigning women's skeet champion from Paris 2024, ahead of Amber Rutter (GBR) and Austen Smith (USA).
Samantha Simonton (USA) won the 2025 women's skeet world title with a final score of 57 and took silver at the 2025 World Cup Final behind China's Jiang Yiting.
Three-time Games champion Kimberly Rhode (USA) won ISSF World Cup gold in 2025; her only individual world title came in 2010.

facts: The men's 50m rifle 3 positions is part of the 2028 Games shooting programme.

ISSF has approved a new 50m rifle 3 positions final format for the 2028 Games in which kneeling and prone are merged into one phase with an overall time limit, and athletes control their own change between the two positions.
Under the approved 3 positions final format, the standing position and the elimination phases still decide the medals.
China's Liu Yukun, the Paris 2024 champion, won the men's 50m rifle 3 positions world title at the 2025 World Championship in Cairo with 467.1.
India's Aishwary Pratap Singh Tomar took silver in the Cairo 2025 men's 3 positions final on 466.9 after challenging late, and Liu regained the lead with his final shot.
France's Romain Aufrere won bronze in the men's 50m rifle 3 positions at the 2025 World Championship in Cairo.
France, with Brian Baudouin, Lucas Kryzs and Romain Aufrere, won the men's 50m rifle 3 positions team world title in Cairo, ahead of Norway and Switzerland.
Norway's Jon-Hermann Hegg and India's Niraj Kumar also took part in the Cairo 2025 3 positions competition, both scoring 592 in qualification.
Athletes begin qualifying for the 2028 Games at the 2026 ISSF World Championship in Doha.

facts: The women's 50m rifle 3 positions is part of the 2028 Games shooting programme.
ISSF has approved a 3 positions final format for the 2028 Games in which kneeling and prone become one time-limited phase, and athletes choose when to change position.
In the new 3 positions final, the standing position and the elimination phases still decide the medals.
At Paris 2024, Switzerland's Chiara Leone won the women's 50m rifle 3 positions ahead of Sagen Maddalena of the USA.
At the 2025 World Championship in Cairo, India's Ashi Chouksey placed 15th in women's 50m rifle 3 positions qualification and did not reach the final, and Anjum Moudgil was 17th.
The 2025 World Championship Rifle/Pistol ran 6-18 November 2025 in Cairo.
The first quota places for the 2028 Games will be awarded at the 2026 ISSF World Championship in Doha.

facts: Trap qualification for the 2028 Games takes place at Whittier Narrows Clay Shooting Center, which the organizers describe as one of Southern California's premier shotgun ranges.
Under the 2026 ISSF Rulebook, trap finals now take eight athletes instead of six, so eight shooters advance from qualification.
Croatia's Josip Glasnovic won men's trap at the 2025 ISSF World Championship in Athens, ahead of Spain's Andres Garcia and India's Zoravar Singh Sandhu, in a field of 133 athletes.
Spain's Mar Molne Magrina won women's trap at the 2025 World Championship, ahead of Italy's Silvana Stanco and Poland's Sandra Bernal, in a field of 73 athletes.
Will Hinton (USA) won men's trap at the 2025 ISSF World Cup Final in Doha, and Silvana Stanco (ITA) won women's trap there.
Croatia won the 2025 men's trap team world title with 368, ahead of the USA (Hinton, Derrick Mein, Walton Eller) and Czechia, both on 361.
Paris 2024 men's trap champion Nathan Hales (GBR) finished 78th in qualification at the 2025 World Championship in Athens with 113.
The first trap quota places for the 2028 Games are scheduled for November 12, 2026 at the ISSF World Championship in Doha, three each for men and women.
India's Neeru Dhanda was described as in-form ahead of the 2026 Doha World Championship, where India is entered in all 12 individual events.

At Paris 2024, South Korea's Yang Ji-In won the women's 25m pistol ahead of France's Camille Jedrzejewski.
Yang Jiin won the women's 25m pistol world title in Cairo in November 2025, scoring 40 in the final, ahead of China's Yao Qianxun on 38, with India's Esha Singh taking bronze.
Qualification for the 2028 Games starts at the 2026 ISSF World Championship in Doha.

facts: Men's and women's trap medals for the 2028 Games are decided in an eight-athlete final at Whittier Narrows Clay Shooting Center, up from six finalists at Paris 2024.
Nathan Hales (GBR) won Paris 2024 men's trap gold with a Games-record final in which he missed two of 50 shots, ahead of China's Qi Ying and Guatemala's Jean-Pierre Brol.
Hales's Paris 2024 win was Great Britain's first trap gold since 1968.
Adriana Ruano (GUA) won Paris 2024 women's trap, Guatemala's first gold medal, ahead of Italy's Silvana Stanco and Australia's Penny Smith.
Silvana Stanco (ITA) took silver at the 2025 World Championship and then won women's trap at the 2025 ISSF World Cup Final in Doha.
Spain's Mar Molne Magrina is the 2025 women's trap world champion.
Croatia's Josip Glasnovic is the 2025 men's trap world champion, ahead of Spain's Andres Garcia and India's Zoravar Singh Sandhu.
Will Hinton (USA) won men's trap at the 2025 ISSF World Cup Final and led the U.S. team to men's trap team silver at the 2025 World Championship.
The 2026 ISSF World Championship in Doha, running November 1-14, 2026, opens qualification for the 2028 Games, with trap quota places awarded on November 12.

facts: Mixed team trap replaces the Paris 2024 mixed team skeet event on the 2028 Games program; Italy (Diana Bacosi and Gabriele Rossetti) won the one-time mixed skeet title in Paris, ahead of the USA and China.
At the 2028 Games, the top four mixed trap teams from qualification advance directly to one medal final and all shoot at the same time, instead of separate gold and bronze medal matches.
ISSF says the four-team final is meant to keep every medal contender in the contest throughout and to give spectators a clearer storyline.
Italy's Massimo Fabbrizi and Alessia Iezzi won mixed team trap at the 2025 ISSF World Championship in Athens, topping qualification with a combined 145.
San Marino's Gian Marco Berti and Alessandra Perilli took 2025 world silver in mixed team trap after reaching the top two through a four-way shoot-off.
Walton (Glenn) Eller and Ava Downs (USA) won mixed trap bronze at the 2025 World Championship by beating Egypt's Ahmed Zahar and Maggy Ashmawy, and it was Downs's first world medal, at age 20.
Eller's 2025 mixed team bronze was his first world medal in trap, as distinct from double trap.
India's skeet medalist Maheshwari Chauhan said the switch from mixed skeet to mixed trap was disappointing for skeet shooters but that athletes would adapt.
The 2026 Doha World Championship quota places cover the 12 individual events; the mixed team event awards no quota places there.

facts: Women's street at the 2028 Games will field 22 skaters, with preliminary rounds deciding who advances to the final, and is scheduled at Valley Complex 1 in the Sepulveda Basin Recreation Area.
The Sepulveda Basin's Valley Zone is split into four complexes and will host BMX, skateboarding, modern pentathlon and 3x3 basketball at the 2028 Games.
Qualification Phase 1 runs from 11 June 2026 to 31 March 2028 and uses the World Skateboarding Ranking, which counts athletes' best World Skateboarding Tour results from the previous 18 months.
The WST World Cup Rome in June 2026 was the first event to award ranking points toward 2028 Games qualification; 134 skaters from 59 countries entered the street contest.
Japan's Ibuki Matsumoto won the women's street world title at the WST World Championships in Sao Paulo (held March 2026), and was ranked world No. 1 in women's street going into Rome 2026.
Matsumoto won her first WST title at the World Cup Kitakyushu in November 2025 at age 13, edging Japan's Yumeka Oda 160.51 to 160.29, with Australia's Chloe Covell third.

Paris 2024 champion Coco Yoshizawa (JPN) missed the semifinals at the Kitakyushu 2025 World Cup by 0.04 points, took bronze at the Sao Paulo world championships, and won X Games street silver at Chiba 2026.
Brazil's Rayssa Leal, the Paris 2024 bronze medalist, won her fourth straight SLS Super Crown title in December 2025 and was the first skater ever to win four in a row.
Leal came fourth at the Sao Paulo world championships on home soil and fifth at the Rome 2026 World Cup.
Chloe Covell (AUS) won the WST Rome street World Cup in both 2025 and 2026, scoring 177.01 in the 2026 final.
Paige Heyn was the top American at Rome 2026, finishing fourth; China's Chenxi Cui got her first WST podium there in third.
The next stop after Rome on the World Skateboarding Tour was the World Skate Games in Paraguay in October 2026.

facts: Men's street at the 2028 Games will field 22 skaters, with preliminaries leading to a final, and is scheduled at Valley Complex 1 in the Sepulveda Basin.

Qualification uses the World Skateboarding Ranking, with Phase 1 running from 11 June 2026 to 31 March 2028; under Phase 1 rules a nation can have up to six additional athletes who rank in the top 30.
Japan's Sora Shirai won the WST World Cup Rome street event in both 2025 and 2026, leading a Japanese sweep in 2026 (177.92) ahead of Kairi Netsuke and Toa Sasaki.
Toa Sasaki (JPN) defended his men's street world title at the Sao Paulo world championships (March 2026) with 174.10, ahead of Peru's Angelo Caro and Shirai.
Ginwoo Onodera (JPN) won the 2025 SLS Super Crown at age 15, finishing ahead of Shirai.
Two-time champion Yuto Horigome (JPN) went out in the semifinals at the Kitakyushu 2025 World Cup after landing no tricks, and in the quarterfinals at the Sao Paulo world championships.
Paris 2024 silver medalist Jagger Eaton (USA) was knocked out before the semifinals at the Rome 2026 World Cup.
Paris 2024 bronze medalist Nyjah Huston (USA) fractured his skull and eye socket in a skating crash in early January 2026.
Huston has said he is aiming for the 2028 Games in Los Angeles and that he is near the end of his contest career; he will be 33 when the Games start.
Huston won SLS Miami in May 2025, which was his 27th career SLS win.
After Paris 2024, Huston and Eaton both said they wanted to qualify for the 2028 Games and go for gold.
Korea's Juni Kang (fourth) and Brazil's Wallace Gabriel (fifth) also made the Rome 2026 men's final, and Julian Agliardi was the top American in seventh.

facts: The women's street final at the 2028 Games is at Valley Complex 1 in the Sepulveda Basin and features the top skaters from the preliminary round.
The Paris 2024 women's street podium was all Japanese and Brazilian teenagers: Coco Yoshizawa (gold), Liz Akama (silver) and Rayssa Leal (bronze).
Ibuki Matsumoto (JPN) is the reigning women's street world champion from Sao Paulo (March 2026) and was ranked world No. 1 going into the 2028 qualifying period.
In recent WST finals the winner has often been decided by the last trick: Matsumoto won Kitakyushu 2025 with her third and final trick, beating Yumeka Oda by 0.22 points.
Chloe Covell (AUS) won the Rome 2026 World Cup final with 177.01, more than 20 points ahead of runner-up Yumeka Oda (155.15).
Japan's Yumeka Oda finished second at both Kitakyushu 2025 and Rome 2026.
Rayssa Leal (BRA) won four straight SLS Super Crown titles through December 2025, but finished fourth at the 2025 world championships and fifth at Rome 2026.
Coco Yoshizawa came eighth in the Rome 2026 final (42.34) after taking bronze at the Sao Paulo world championships.
The Rome 2026 final also included Paige Heyn (USA, fourth), Chenxi Cui (CHN, third) and Korea's Jiyul Shin (sixth).
At Paris 2024 Leal scored 92.88 on a trick, one of the highest single-trick scores in the women's final.

facts: Yuto Horigome of Japan won men's Street gold at Paris 2024, defending his Tokyo 2020 title, with Jagger Eaton (USA) taking silver and Nyjah Huston (USA) bronze.
Horigome was in fourth place before his last trick in the Paris 2024 final and won with a nollie 270 bluntslide.
Japan's Sasaki Toa kept his men's Street world title at the WST Skateboarding World Championships in São Paulo, decided on March 8, 2026, after building a strong lead in the run section.
The 2025 WST Skateboarding World Championships were first set for Washington, D.C. in September 2025, then moved to São Paulo and held in March 2026, where weather delays hit the street finals.
Japanese skaters won both the men's and women's Street world titles in São Paulo, with 13-year-old Matsumoto Ibuki taking the women's title.
Japan's Sora Shirai won the men's Street final at the WST Street World Cup in Rome in June 2025.
Sora Shirai also won the men's Street final at the WST World Cup in Kitakyushu, Japan, on November 29, 2025.
Japan's Ginwoo Onodera placed first in the men's Street quarter-finals at the WST Rome World Cup in June 2025.
France's Joseph Garbaccio, who competed at Paris 2024, finished first in men's open qualifying at WST Rome 2025 with a best run of 70.49.
Qualification for 2028 Games skateboarding goes through the World Skateboarding Rankings and a final Q-Series, and 22 men will compete in Street.
The men's Street final at the 2028 Games is an eight-skater medal session scheduled for July 20 at Valley Complex 1, with scoring based on the best run plus the two highest single-trick scores.

facts: Men's park preliminaries at the 2028 Games take place at Valley Complex 2, part of the skateboarding venue cluster in the Sepulveda Basin Recreation Area in the San Fernando Valley, Los Angeles.
Each park event at the 2028 Games has 22 quota places per gender, with at most three skaters per nation per event.
Places will be allocated from the World Skateboarding Ranking of 11 June 2028: the top 20 skaters qualify, plus one universality place.

Qualification runs in two phases: World Skateboarding Tour events from 11 June 2026 to 31 March 2028, then a cut to the top 44 skaters per discipline, who go on to a 2028 Qualification Series that decides the final park places.
The WST World Cup Rome park event at The Spot skatepark in Ostia in June 2026 was the first competition to award direct ranking points toward the 2028 Games.
Spain's Egoitz Bijueska won the men's park world title at the 2025 World Championships in São Paulo, which were held in March 2026, with a 95.83 run in the final.
Bijueska also won the men's park title at the WST Park World Cup Rome 2025.
Paris 2024 silver medalist Tom Schaar (USA) took bronze at the São Paulo world championships with a 90.51 run and is listed as the silver medalist at the 2026 Rome park World Cup.
Keegan Palmer (AUS), who won park gold at both Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024, took X Games silver in Osaka in 2025 and bronze in Chiba in 2026.
Gavin Bottger (USA), the 2023 park world champion, won X Games park gold in Salt Lake City in 2025 and in Sacramento in 2026, after finishing 10th at Paris 2024.
In the Paris 2024 men's park final, only two of the eight finalists landed their first runs, and Palmer's 93.11 first run held up for gold.
Palmer was born in San Diego, California, and represents Australia, which gives him a Southern California connection for the 2028 Games.

facts: Women's park preliminaries at the 2028 Games take place at Valley Complex 2 in the Sepulveda Basin skateboarding venue cluster in Los Angeles.
Each park event has 22 quota places, allocated from the World Skateboarding Ranking of 11 June 2028, with at most three skaters per nation.
Japan could therefore enter no more than three women in park, even though several Japanese skaters are among the leading contenders.
Qualification started at the WST World Cup Rome park event in Ostia in June 2026 and ends with a 2028 Qualification Series for the top 44 ranked skaters.

Japan's Mizuho Hasegawa, aged 15, won the women's park final at the 2026 Rome World Cup with a 96.33 run, which World Skate called the highest score ever in women's park on the World Skateboarding Tour.
Hasegawa also won the women's park title at the WST Park World Cup Rome 2025 and took silver at the São Paulo world championships, held in March 2026, with 84.36.
Sky Brown (GBR) won her second women's park world title in São Paulo in March 2026 with 88.16 in a rain-affected final, after her first world title in 2023.
Brown finished second at the 2026 Rome World Cup after landing three runs over 90 points.
Cocona Hiraki (JPN), silver medalist at Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024, finished third at the 2026 Rome World Cup and eighth in the São Paulo world championship final.
Arisa Trew (AUS) won both women's park and vert at X Games Osaka 2025, her third straight X Games park-vert double.

facts: The men's park final is scheduled for the evening of Wednesday, July 26, at Valley Complex 2 in the Sepulveda Basin, Los Angeles.
Keegan Palmer (AUS) has won both men's park golds awarded so far, at Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024; a third in 2028 would make it three in a row.
At Paris 2024 Palmer won with a 93.11 first run, ahead of Tom Schaar (USA) in silver and Augusto Akio (BRA) in bronze.
Egoitz Bijueska (ESP) won the men's park world title in São Paulo in March 2026 with a 95.83 run, and he also won the 2025 Rome park World Cup.
Tom Schaar, a Californian, won the 2025 Rockstar Energy Open men's park final in Portland with a 90-point run and is listed as the silver medalist at the 2026 Rome park World Cup.
Schaar took bronze at the São Paulo world championships with a 90.51 run.
Gavin Bottger (USA), of Oceanside, California, won X Games park gold in 2025 (Salt Lake City) and 2026 (Sacramento) and is the 2023 park world champion.
Palmer's recent X Games park results are silver in Osaka in 2025 and bronze in Chiba in 2026.
World Skate described the 2026 Rome World Cup men's park final as the highest standard of men's park skating it had seen.
Final places at the 2028 Games depend on the World Skateboarding Ranking of 11 June 2028, so the final line-up is not yet set.

facts: This session decides the first women's squash medals in Games history: the bronze medal match between the semifinal losers, then the gold medal match.
Squash was added to the 2028 program by the IOC Session in Mumbai in October 2023, along with baseball/softball, cricket, flag football and lacrosse.
Nouran Gohar won the 2024 women's world title, Nour El Sherbini the 2025 title and Amina Orfi the 2026 title, all three for Egypt.
El Sherbini has won eight world titles; her 2025 final win was over Hania El Hammamy in Chicago.
Orfi was reported as the youngest female world champion in history after her 2026 title.
Because each country is capped at two athletes per event, Egypt cannot fill all three medal positions with Egyptians unless both of its qualifiers reach the medal matches.
Olivia Weaver of the United States reached world championship semifinals in 2024 and 2025, which makes her a possible home medal contender depending on qualification and form.
The medal matches are on the Comcast Squash Center court at Courthouse Square on the Universal Studios Hollywood backlot.

facts: This closing session of the squash tournament decides the first men's squash medals in Games history, with the bronze medal match followed by the gold medal match.
Mostafa Asal of Egypt is the reigning two-time men's world champion (2025, 2026) and was world No. 1 in the SquashInfo PSA rankings dated 26 October 2026.
Asal beat four-time world champion Ali Farag to win his first world title in Chicago in 2025, then beat Youssef Ibrahim in Giza in 2026 to keep it.
Diego Elias won the 2024 world title for Peru by beating Asal in the final and was ranked third in October 2026.
Paul Coll of New Zealand was ranked second in the 26 October 2026 PSA men's rankings.

Other top-12 men in the 26 October 2026 list included Mohamad Zakaria and Karim Gawad of Egypt, Victor Crouin of France, Joel Makin of Wales, the ElShorbagy brothers of England and Leonel Cardenas of Mexico.
With at most two Egyptian men allowed in the draw, the men's podium will include at least one player from another country.
The squash tournament runs July 15-24, 2028, so this men's final is the last squash session of the Games.

facts: Surfing at the 2028 Games will be held at Lower Trestles, a high-performance cobblestone peak in San Clemente, California, within the state park system.
Lower Trestles was chosen over Huntington Beach as the surfing venue because of wave quality and consistency, according to the International Surfing Association (ISA).
The 2028 surfing field is 48 athletes, 24 men and 24 women, and each nation can qualify up to three surfers per gender, up from two at Paris 2024.
Under the qualification system released in February 2026, qualification starts at the 2026 ISA World Surfing Games and builds toward a decisive 2028 season.
Because most places are allocated in 2028, the full Round 1 field is not expected to be known until shortly before the Games.
The host nation is guaranteed one place per gender unless it already fills that place through another pathway.
Universality places require the nominated athlete to finish in the top 40 at the 2027 or 2028 ISA World Surfing Games, so smaller surfing nations may show up in the opening round.

At Paris 2024, held at Teahupo'o, Kauli Vaast (FRA) won men's gold ahead of Jack Robinson (AUS) and Gabriel Medina (BRA), and Caroline Marks (USA) won women's gold ahead of Tatiana Weston-Webb (BRA) and Johanne Defay (FRA).
Lower Trestles hosted the WSL Finals from 2021 to 2024, and the WSL Championship Tour returned there in 2025 for the regular-season Lexus Trestles Pro.
The 2026 WSL Championship Tour scheduled a Lower Trestles event for September 11-20, 2026.
Brazil's Yago Dora and Australia's Molly Picklum won the 2025 WSL world titles at the WSL Finals in Fiji.

facts: Round 2 of men's and women's surfing at the 2028 Games is set for Lower Trestles in San Clemente, California.
After criticism from the WSL and Championship Tour surfers, the ISA revised the 2028 qualification system and cut the number of places from the 2028 World Surfing Games from 10 per gender to seven.
The revision partly restored the places reserved for the WSL Championship Tour, after an earlier draft that used only 2028 tour rankings as of mid-June 2028.
Places from the World Surfing Games and the Championship Tour are each capped at one surfer per nation, so a country sending three surfers needs results across several pathways.
The top-ranked team per gender at the 2026 and 2027 ISA World Surfing Games earns one place per gender for its nation.
Reigning WSL world champion Yago Dora publicly opposed the original qualification changes.
Yago Dora (BRA) won the 2025 Lexus Trestles Pro at Lower Trestles, and Bettylou Sakura Johnson (HAW) won the women's event.
Caroline Marks (USA), the Paris 2024 gold medalist, won the 2025 MEO Rip Curl Pro Portugal, her seventh Championship Tour win.
Kelly Slater has won at Lower Trestles six times, and San Clemente's Griffin Colapinto is a local favorite there.

Lower Trestles decided the one-day, winner-takes-all WSL Finals from 2021 to 2024; Filipe Toledo (BRA) and Stephanie Gilmore (AUS) won there in 2022.
Kelly Slater has won at Lower Trestles six times, and Carissa Moore, Stephanie Gilmore and Tyler Wright have also won events there.
Griffin Colapinto, from San Clemente, and Kolohe Andino are regarded as local favorites at Lower Trestles.
Marks and Carissa Moore (2021) are the two Americans who have won women's surfing gold at the Games.

facts: The women's duet technical routine opens the 2028 artistic swimming program on Tuesday, July 25, 2028, from 11:00 to 13:00 at the Long Beach Aquatics Center.
Artistic swimming at the 2028 Games is scheduled for July 25-29, 2028, at the Long Beach Aquatics Center, according to the City of Long Beach.
The duet medal is decided by combining the technical routine score with the free routine score held the next day.
Austria's Anna-Maria and Eirini-Marina Alexandri won the women's duet technical world title at the 2025 World Aquatics Championships in Singapore, their second career world title.

China's Lin Yanhan and Lin Yanjun took silver in the 2025 world duet technical final with 301.4057 points, and Mayya Doroshko and Tatiana Gayday, competing as Neutral Athletes B, took bronze with 300.2183.
The top three in the 2025 world duet technical final finished within less than seven points of each other.
The 2025 world duet technical event drew 78 competitors from 39 nations.

Paris 2024 duet silver medalists Kate Shortman and Isabelle Thorpe of Great Britain were reported in March 2026 to be returning as a duet at the Paris World Cup, their first joint competition since Paris 2024.
Shortman took an extended break after Paris 2024, and World Aquatics reported in October 2025 that she is targeting the 2028 Games.
For the United States, Jaime Czarkowski and then 16-year-old junior world champion Ghizal Akbar placed 11th in the 2025 world duet technical prelims with 265.7292 and made the final.

Paris 2024 duet champions Wang Liuyi and Wang Qianyi of China have not been confirmed in the sources reviewed as competing for the 2028 Games; China's 2025 world duet technical entry was Lin Yanhan and Lin Yanjun.

facts: The women's duet free routine on Wednesday, July 26, 2028, from 11:00 to 13:15 at the Long Beach Aquatics Center is the duet medal session.
Duet medals go to the pairs with the highest combined technical and free routine scores.
At Paris 2024, China's Wang Liuyi and Wang Qianyi won duet gold, Great Britain's Kate Shortman and Isabelle Thorpe took silver, and the Netherlands' Bregje and Noortje de Brouwer took bronze.
Spain's Iris Tio Casas and Lilou Lluis Valette won the women's duet free world title at the 2025 World Aquatics Championships in Singapore.

At Singapore 2025, Iris Tio Casas became the first artistic swimmer to win world titles in all four disciplines (solo, duet, mixed duet and team), and she reached the podium in all six events she entered.
Spain topped the 2025 world artistic swimming medal table with nine medals (3 gold, 2 silver, 4 bronze).
Austria's Alexandri twins won the 2025 world duet technical title, so the two 2025 duet world titles went to different pairs.

Shortman and Thorpe won Great Britain's first world championship duet medal with technical silver at Doha 2024, and then won Great Britain's first Games medal in the sport with duet silver at Paris 2024.
Thorpe competed in the mixed duet with Ranjuo Tomblin in 2025 and won world and European medals while Shortman took a sabbatical; the pair announced a return to duet competition in March 2026.
As of the sources reviewed, China has not confirmed whether Wang Liuyi and Wang Qianyi will try to defend their duet title in 2028.

facts: Swimming at the 2028 Games is held in a temporary pool inside SoFi Stadium, called 2028 Stadium during the Games, and the pool program runs July 22-30, 2028.
Swimming moves to the second week of the 2028 Games, swapping places with athletics.

This opening morning session includes heats of the new men's 50m butterfly and women's 50m backstroke, two of six 50m stroke events approved in April 2025 that use a heats, semifinals and final format.
Relays and the 800m/1500m freestyle go straight from heats to finals, so the men's and women's 4x100m freestyle relay heats this morning set the lanes for that evening's finals.

Gretchen Walsh, the 100m butterfly world record holder and Paris 2024 silver medalist, won the 100m butterfly at the 2025 World Aquatics Championships in Singapore in a championship-record 54.73, the second-fastest time in history.
Summer McIntosh beat Katie Ledecky to win the women's 400m freestyle at the 2025 World Championships in Singapore.
Paris 2024 women's 400m freestyle champion Ariarne Titmus of Australia retired from swimming on October 16, 2025, aged 25, so the 2028 event will have a new champion.
Paris 2024 men's 400m freestyle champion Lukas Märtens of Germany took bronze in the 800m freestyle at the 2025 World Championships, behind Tunisia's Ahmed Jaouadi and Germany's Sven Schwarz.
Nicolò Martinenghi won the men's 100m breaststroke at Paris 2024, while Adam Peaty tied for silver, so no bronze was awarded.
The United States won a meet-leading nine swimming golds at the 2025 World Championships.

facts: This is the first finals session of the 2028 Games swimming program, held in the temporary pool inside SoFi Stadium (2028 Stadium); the pool program runs July 22-30, 2028.

Medals in this session: the men's 400m freestyle, the women's 400m freestyle, and the men's and women's 4x100m freestyle relays, with semifinals in four other events including the new men's 50m butterfly and women's 50m backstroke.
Summer McIntosh, the Paris 2024 silver medalist, beat Katie Ledecky to win the women's 400m freestyle at the 2025 World Championships in Singapore, the first of her four golds there.
Ariarne Titmus, who won the women's 400m freestyle at Paris 2024, retired on October 16, 2025, aged 25.
Katie Ledecky won bronze in the women's 400m freestyle at Paris 2024 and went on to win the 800m and 1500m freestyle at the 2025 World Championships.
Lukas Märtens won the men's 400m freestyle at Paris 2024 ahead of Elijah Winnington and Kim Woo-min, and he took bronze in the 800m freestyle at the 2025 World Championships.
The United States won the men's 4x100m freestyle relay at Paris 2024 ahead of Australia and Italy, and Australia won the women's relay ahead of the United States and China.
Gretchen Walsh, who swims in the women's 100m butterfly semifinal, won the 2025 world title in a championship-record 54.73.
At the 2025 World Championships, Australia beat the United States by 0.66 seconds in the women's 4x200m freestyle relay, showing the relay rivalry is still close.

Marchand's 1:52.69 took 1.31 seconds off Ryan Lochte's world record of 1:54.00, which had stood since the 2011 World Championships in Shanghai.

Kós swam a short-course 200m backstroke of 1:45.12 in Toronto on October 23, 2025, which tops the all-time short-course list.

Kliment Kolesnikov won the men's 50m backstroke at the 2025 World Championships in 23.68, the most recent global title in the event.
Pieter Coetze (RSA) and Pavel Samusenko tied for silver in the men's 50m backstroke at the 2025 World Championships. Coetze also won silver in the 200m backstroke at the same meet.
Kristóf Milák (HUN) won the men's 100m butterfly at Paris 2024, ahead of Josh Liendo (CAN) and Ilya Kharun (CAN).

Maxime Grousset (FRA) won the men's 100m butterfly at the 2025 World Championships in 49.62, ahead of Noè Ponti (SUI) and Ilya Kharun (CAN). Grousset had also won the event at the 2023 World Championships.
Caeleb Dressel (USA) holds the men's 100m butterfly world record of 49.45, set in 2021, but did not swim the event at the 2025 World Championships.
Daniel Wiffen (IRL) won the men's 800m freestyle at Paris 2024, ahead of Bobby Finke (USA) and Gregorio Paltrinieri (ITA).
The United States won the mixed 4x100m medley relay at Paris 2024, with China second and Australia third.
In the women's 200m butterfly semifinals, Summer McIntosh (CAN) is the Paris 2024 champion, ahead of Regan Smith (USA) and Zhang Yufei (CHN) on that podium.
In the women's 50m freestyle semifinals, Sarah Sjöström (SWE) is the Paris 2024 champion; Meg Harris (AUS) took silver and Zhang Yufei (CHN) bronze.

facts: This afternoon finals session has the women's 50m freestyle, women's 200m butterfly, women's 800m freestyle, men's 4x100m medley relay and women's 4x100m medley relay finals.
Because swimming moves to the second week of the 2028 Games and swaps places with athletics, these finals fall on the program's final weekend.
Sarah Sjöström (SWE) won the women's 50m freestyle at Paris 2024 as part of a sprint freestyle double, with Meg Harris (AUS) second and Zhang Yufei (CHN) third.
Summer McIntosh (CAN) won the women's 200m butterfly at Paris 2024, one of her three golds there, with Regan Smith (USA) second and Zhang Yufei (CHN) third.
Katie Ledecky (USA) won the women's 800m freestyle at Paris 2024, with Ariarne Titmus (AUS) second and Paige Madden (USA) third.
Ledecky anchored the US women's 4x200m freestyle relay to silver at the 2025 World Championships, which showed she was still racing at the top level after Paris 2024.
China won the men's 4x100m medley relay at Paris 2024, beating the United States into silver, with France third.
The United States won the women's 4x100m medley relay at Paris 2024, with Australia second and China third.
Gretchen Walsh (USA) won the 100m and 50m butterfly at the 2025 World Championships and is a likely butterfly leg for the US women's medley relay (projection).
Kaylee McKeown (AUS) won the 100m and 200m backstroke at the 2025 World Championships and is a likely backstroke leg for Australia's women's medley relay (projection).
Maxime Grousset (FRA), the 2025 world 100m butterfly champion, is a likely butterfly leg for France's men's medley relay (projection); France won bronze in the event at Paris 2024.

facts: The organizers' published competition schedule lists TEN01 as Mixed Doubles Round 1 (3 matches) at Carson Center Court on Wednesday, July 19, 2028, from 11:00 to 16:30, which is Games Day 5.
Mixed doubles opens the 2028 tennis program and runs July 19-20, and the singles draws also begin on July 20.
The mixed doubles draw is planned at 16 pairs, compared with 64 players in each singles draw and 32 pairs in each doubles draw.
Tennis at the 2028 Games will be played outdoors on hard courts at Carson Courts, best of three sets, from July 19 to 28.
Carson Courts is the tennis facility inside the Dignity Health Sports Park complex in Carson, California, and its stadium court seats about 8,000 for tennis.
The 2028 Wimbledon Championships end on July 16, so play in Carson starts three days after the Wimbledon men's singles final.
Organizers have said the published tennis schedule may still change.

Czechia's Katerina Siniakova and Tomas Machac are the reigning mixed doubles champions from Paris 2024, where China's Wang Xinyu and Zhang Zhizhen took silver and Canada's Gabriela Dabrowski and Felix Auger-Aliassime took bronze.
No mixed doubles pairs had been confirmed for the 2028 Games as of October 2026.

facts: The organizers' published competition schedule lists TEN02 as Mixed Doubles Round 1 (3 matches) at Carson Court 1 on Wednesday, July 19, 2028, from 11:00 to 16:30, at the same time as first-round matches on Center Court and Court 2.
Eight first-round mixed doubles matches are spread across three courts on opening day: three on Center Court, three on Court 1 and two on Court 2.
Under the 2028 format, mixed doubles finishes in two days, July 19-20: the first round and quarterfinals on day one, then the semifinals and medal matches on day two.
In the past, Games mixed doubles was played near the end of the tennis program, and coverage noted that the new opening slot follows the U.S. Open's lead.
Matches at the 2028 Games are best of three sets on outdoor hard courts at Carson Courts, inside Dignity Health Sports Park.
Wimbledon 2028 ends July 16, two days after the July 14 opening ceremony, which leaves Wimbledon finalists very little time to recover before mixed doubles starts.

Paris 2024 mixed doubles medalists were Katerina Siniakova and Tomas Machac of Czechia (gold), Wang Xinyu and Zhang Zhizhen of China (silver), and Gabriela Dabrowski and Felix Auger-Aliassime of Canada (bronze).
No mixed doubles entries or pairings for the 2028 Games had been announced as of October 2026.

facts: Tennis at the 2028 Games runs July 19 to 28 at Carson Courts, a purpose-built complex inside Dignity Health Sports Park in Carson.
Friday, July 21 is the second day of singles first-round play; singles begins July 20, the day the mixed doubles medals are decided.
Wimbledon 2028 ends July 16, leaving players only a few days to switch from grass in London to the hard courts in Carson.

Singles qualification uses the ATP and WTA rankings of 12 June 2028: 56 direct-acceptance places, 1 host-country place, 6 ITF continental places and 1 universality place per gender, for 64-player draws.
Carlos Alcaraz won the 2026 Australian Open to complete the career Grand Slam and reach seven major titles.
Alcaraz missed about five months of 2026, including Roland Garros and Wimbledon, with a wrist injury, then won the Japan Open in October 2026 after returning.
Jannik Sinner retook world No. 1 from Alcaraz in April 2026 after beating him in the Monte-Carlo final, and later ended his 2026 season early with a knee injury.

Novak Djokovic, Paris 2024 singles champion, said in October 2026 after reaching the China Open final that he sees no reason not to play in Los Angeles once his physical problems are resolved; he would be 41 in 2028.

Carlos Alcaraz won the 2026 Australian Open to complete the career Grand Slam and reach seven major titles.
Alcaraz missed about five months of 2026, including Roland Garros and Wimbledon, with a wrist injury, then won the Japan Open in October 2026 after returning.
Jannik Sinner retook world No. 1 from Alcaraz in April 2026 after beating him in the Monte-Carlo final, and later ended his 2026 season early with a knee injury.
Alexander Zverev won Roland Garros and the US Open in 2026 and was ranked No. 2 behind Sinner in October 2026.
Elena Rybakina won the 2026 Australian Open, beating Iga Swiatek in the quarterfinals, and top seed Aryna Sabalenka finished runner-up.
Coco Gauff, seeded third at the 2026 Australian Open, lost in the quarterfinals to Elina Svitolina 6-1, 6-2.
Iga Swiatek, Paris 2024 singles bronze medalist, was seeded second at the 2026 Australian Open and lost to Rybakina 7-5, 6-1 in the quarterfinals.
Wimbledon 2028 ends July 16, leaving players only a few days to switch from grass in London to the hard courts in Carson.

facts: Tennis at the 2028 Games runs July 19 to 28 at Carson Courts, a purpose-built complex inside Dignity Health Sports Park in Carson.
This evening Center Court session on Saturday, July 22 closes the singles second round.
Per the published schedule, men's and women's singles begin Thursday, July 20, with the women's singles final on July 27 and the men's singles final on July 28.

Novak Djokovic, Paris 2024 singles champion, said in October 2026 after reaching the China Open final that he sees no reason not to play in Los Angeles once his physical problems are resolved; he would be 41 in 2028.
Djokovic called the 2028 Games a guiding star in December 2025 but has not formally confirmed his entry.
Carlos Alcaraz won the 2026 Australian Open to complete the career Grand Slam and reach seven major titles.
Alcaraz missed about five months of 2026, including Roland Garros and Wimbledon, with a wrist injury, then won the Japan Open in October 2026 after returning.
Jannik Sinner retook world No. 1 from Alcaraz in April 2026 after beating him in the Monte-Carlo final, and later ended his 2026 season early with a knee injury.
Elena Rybakina won the 2026 Australian Open, beating Iga Swiatek in the quarterfinals, and top seed Aryna Sabalenka finished runner-up.
Paris 2024 singles champion Zheng Qinwen had right elbow surgery after Wimbledon 2025, came through qualifying to reach the 2026 US Open quarterfinals, and won the 2026 China Open.
Zheng ended her 2026 season early in October 2026 because of a right shoulder injury, and was ranked No. 22 as of October 19, 2026.
Wimbledon 2028 ends July 16, leaving players only a few days to switch from grass in London to the hard courts in Carson.

Djokovic has described the 2028 Games as a main reason he is still competing, and has talked about possibly finishing his career representing Serbia there.
Coco Gauff is one of the Team USA stars who have said they plan to compete at the 2028 Games; she lost early at Paris 2024 and later posted that she would see fans in 2028.
Aryna Sabalenka finished 2025 as the year-end WTA No. 1 and still held the top ranking in August 2026, with Elena Rybakina closing in.
Zheng Qinwen of China won the women's singles gold at Paris 2024, beating Donna Vekic in the final, and Iga Swiatek took bronze.
As of the latest available reports, no tennis entry lists or player participation for the 2028 Games have been confirmed.

facts: This day session on Carson Center Court features men's singles quarterfinals and the women's singles semifinals, with the women's medal matches two days later on July 27.
Carson Courts sits inside the Dignity Health Sports Park complex in Carson, California, and is home to the USTA's High-Performance Training Center.
Carson Center Court is an outdoor arena with 360-degree seating, and the Carson Courts venue is listed with a seating capacity of 8,000.
Tennis at the 2028 Games runs July 19-28 on outdoor hard courts; 2028 Wimbledon ends July 16, leaving roughly three days between the two events.
Aryna Sabalenka finished 2025 as WTA year-end No. 1 for the second straight season after defending her US Open title.
Iga Swiatek, the 2025 Wimbledon champion and Paris 2024 bronze medalist, finished 2025 at No. 2 in the WTA rankings.
Coco Gauff, the 2025 French Open champion, finished 2025 at No. 3, and Amanda Anisimova of the U.S. finished No. 4.
Elena Rybakina won the 2025 WTA Finals, the last tournament of the 2025 season.
Gauff told Parade in 2025 that she hopes to qualify for the U.S. team for the 2028 Games, calling Paris 2024 her best experience.
Carlos Alcaraz finished 2025 as ATP year-end No. 1, his second year-end No. 1, after trading the top spot with Jannik Sinner through the season.
Alcaraz and Sinner met six times in 2025, with Alcaraz winning four, and between them they won eight of the season's nine biggest ATP ranking-point hauls.

facts: This Carson Court 1 session combines men's doubles semifinals with men's singles and women's doubles quarterfinals; the men's doubles medal matches follow on July 27.
Carson Courts sits inside the Dignity Health Sports Park complex in Carson, California, and is home to the USTA's High-Performance Training Center.
Tennis at the 2028 Games runs July 19-28 on outdoor hard courts; 2028 Wimbledon ends July 16, leaving roughly three days between the two events.
Matthew Ebden and John Peers of Australia won Paris 2024 men's doubles gold, beating Americans Rajeev Ram and Austin Krajicek 10-8 in a match tiebreak; Taylor Fritz and Tommy Paul took bronze.
Julian Cash and Lloyd Glasspool became the first all-British pair to finish as ATP year-end doubles No. 1 in 2025.

Harri Heliovaara and Henry Patten won the 2025 ATP Finals doubles title in Turin, beating Joe Salisbury and Neal Skupski in the final, after also winning the 2025 Australian Open and the Paris Masters.
Marcel Granollers and Horacio Zeballos won two major doubles titles in 2025 after three previous losses in major finals, and made their sixth straight ATP Finals appearance.
Men's doubles has a 32-team draw and runs July 21-27.
Italy's Sara Errani and Jasmine Paolini won Paris 2024 women's doubles gold, beating neutral athletes Mirra Andreeva and Diana Shnaider in a final-set tiebreak; Spain took bronze.
Errani and Paolini won the 2025 French Open women's doubles title, 6-4, 2-6, 6-1 over Anna Danilina and Aleksandra Krunic, their first major title as a team.
Carlos Alcaraz finished 2025 as ATP year-end No. 1, his second year-end No. 1, after trading the top spot with Jannik Sinner through the season.

facts: This night session on Carson Center Court on July 27, 2028 decides the men's doubles bronze and gold medals.
Matthew Ebden and John Peers of Australia won Paris 2024 men's doubles gold, beating Americans Rajeev Ram and Austin Krajicek 10-8 in a match tiebreak; Taylor Fritz and Tommy Paul took bronze.
Julian Cash and Lloyd Glasspool became the first all-British pair to finish as ATP year-end doubles No. 1 in 2025.

Harri Heliovaara and Henry Patten won the 2025 ATP Finals doubles title in Turin, beating Joe Salisbury and Neal Skupski in the final, after also winning the 2025 Australian Open and the Paris Masters.
Marcel Granollers and Horacio Zeballos won two major doubles titles in 2025 after three previous losses in major finals, and made their sixth straight ATP Finals appearance.
Men's doubles has a 32-team draw and runs July 21-27.
Carson Center Court is an outdoor arena with 360-degree seating, and the Carson Courts venue is listed with a seating capacity of 8,000.
Tennis at the 2028 Games runs July 19-28 on outdoor hard courts; 2028 Wimbledon ends July 16, leaving roughly three days between the two events.

facts: This session on Carson Center Court on July 28, 2028 decides the men's singles bronze and gold medals, the final day of the tennis program.

Novak Djokovic, who beat Alcaraz 7-6(3), 7-6(2) for Paris 2024 gold, said in March 2026 at Indian Wells that defending his title in Los Angeles is a long-term goal; he will be 41 when the Games begin.
Lorenzo Musetti of Italy won the Paris 2024 men's singles bronze.
Carlos Alcaraz finished 2025 as ATP year-end No. 1, his second year-end No. 1, after trading the top spot with Jannik Sinner through the season.
Alcaraz and Sinner met six times in 2025, with Alcaraz winning four, and between them they won eight of the season's nine biggest ATP ranking-point hauls.
Sinner won the 2025 ATP Finals title in Turin without losing a match.
Alcaraz has said publicly he would be happy to see Djokovic compete through the 2028 Games.
Men's singles uses a 64-player draw and is the only event that runs the full ten days, finishing July 28.
Carson Center Court is an outdoor arena with 360-degree seating, and the Carson Courts venue is listed with a seating capacity of 8,000.
Tennis at the 2028 Games runs July 19-28 on outdoor hard courts; 2028 Wimbledon ends July 16, leaving roughly three days between the two events.

facts: This night session on Carson Center Court on July 28, 2028 decides the women's doubles bronze and gold medals and closes the tennis program.
Italy's Sara Errani and Jasmine Paolini won Paris 2024 women's doubles gold, beating neutral athletes Mirra Andreeva and Diana Shnaider in a final-set tiebreak; Spain took bronze.
Errani and Paolini won the 2025 French Open women's doubles title, 6-4, 2-6, 6-1 over Anna Danilina and Aleksandra Krunic, their first major title as a team.
Andreeva and Shnaider won the 2025 Miami Open women's doubles title, beating Cristina Bucsa and Miyu Kato.
Veronika Kudermetova and Elise Mertens won the 2025 WTA Finals doubles title, 7-6(4), 6-1 over Timea Babos and Luisa Stefani.
Women's doubles has a 32-team draw and runs July 21-28, ending on the final day of the tennis program alongside the men's singles final.
Carson Center Court is an outdoor arena with 360-degree seating, and the Carson Courts venue is listed with a seating capacity of 8,000.
Tennis at the 2028 Games runs July 19-28 on outdoor hard courts; 2028 Wimbledon ends July 16, leaving roughly three days between the two events.

facts: Taekwondo at the 2028 Games runs July 26-29, 2028 at LA Convention Center Hall 1 in the DTLA Zone, per the organizing committee's hospitality schedule.
Session TKW01 on July 26 covers the Round of 32 and Round of 16 in the women's -49kg and men's -58kg categories.
The LA Convention Center (Halls 1-3) will host fencing, judo, table tennis, taekwondo and wrestling at the 2028 Games.

Paris 2024 women's -49kg champion Panipak Wongpattanakit of Thailand announced her retirement after Paris 2024, citing injuries including a damaged knee ligament, so the 2028 title will have a new winner.
Paris 2024 women's -49kg silver medalist Guo Qing of China was competing at her first Games in Paris.
Croatia's Lena Stojkovic and Iran's Mobina Nematzadeh won the Paris 2024 women's -49kg bronze medals, both as first-time Games competitors.
Chinese Taipei's Liu YouYun won the women's -49kg title at the 2025 World Championships in Wuxi on her Worlds debut, beating Turkey's Elif Sude Akgul in the final.
South Korea's Park Tae-joon, the Paris 2024 men's -58kg champion, was listed at No. 1 in World Taekwondo's ranking for the men's -58kg Games category.
Iran's Abolfazl Zandi won the men's -58kg title at the 2025 World Championships in Wuxi, a field of 68 contestants, without losing a round.
Early rounds in the men's -58kg are expected to be crowded; the 2025 Worlds -58kg drew 68 competitors from 66 nations.

facts: Session TKW03 on the evening of July 26, 2028 at LA Convention Center Hall 1 decides the first two taekwondo titles of the 2028 Games: women's -49kg and men's -58kg.
Each category awards two bronze medals through repechage and bronze medal contests, plus the gold medal contest.

At Paris 2024, South Korea's Park Tae-joon beat Azerbaijan's Gashim Magomedov in the men's -58kg gold medal contest.
Park Tae-joon, born in 2004, was ranked No. 1 in the men's -58kg Games-category ranking per his World Taekwondo profile.
Iran's Abolfazl Zandi is the reigning 2025 world champion at -58kg.
Tunisia's Mohamed Khalil Jendoubi, a silver and bronze medalist at -58kg at the last two Games, won the 2025 world title at -63kg, a non-Games weight.
Chinese Taipei's Liu YouYun is the 2025 women's -49kg world champion and is projected to contend based on 2025 form.
Croatia's Lena Stojkovic beat Turkey's Merve Dincel Kavurat for one of the Paris 2024 -49kg bronze medals; Dincel Kavurat won the 2025 world title at -53kg.
